programs.program: Master mention Audiovisuel, médias interactifs numériques, jeux — parcours Conception sonore (game/interactive sound design)
programs.institution: Conservatoire national des arts et métiers (Cnam) — École nationale du jeu et des médias interactifs numériques (Enjmin)
programs.institutionType: Grand établissement / EPSCP (public higher-education and research establishment) — Enjmin is one of the Cnam's écoles (EPN)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. How I know: the Cnam is a state EPSCP under the Ministry of Higher Education; the Cnam's own governing-board annex on differentiated fees lists ENJMIN among the internal schools (EPN) that deliver initial training and must apply the state 'Bienvenue en France' differentiated-fee policy, which only applies to public establishments. The award is a diplôme national de master delivered by the state.
programs.qualification: Diplôme national de master (DNM), 'Master Sciences, technologies, santé mention Audiovisuel, médias interactifs numériques, jeux, parcours Conception sonore'. Real second-cycle state degree, RNCP code 38202, accreditation stated as running to 31 August 2030. Supports a student residence permit for a non-EU national.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-accredited diplôme national de master; RNCP 38202; accreditation stated to 31/08/2030.
programs.language: French for M1 (semesters 1–2). The official Cnam page states for semester 3: 'les enseignements de ce semestre se déroulent en langue anglaise' — i.e. M2 is taught in English. So the degree is bilingual FR then EN.
programs.languageRequirement: The official application page states international candidates must supply a B2-level French certificate. No English certificate is demanded on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED whether any English proof is required for the English-taught M2; ask scolarite Enjmin (contact via enjmin.cnam.fr).
programs.englishTest: None published on the official pages I opened. UNVERIFIED — ask Enjmin admissions.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, 4 semesters, 120 ECTS.
programs.focus: Sound design and audio implementation for video games and interactive digital media; the only public French school wholly dedicated to video games.
programs.whatYouStudy: Sound design and audio production for games and interactive media inside a multidisciplinary game-production master (the six tracks — conception sonore, conception visuelle, ergonomie UX, game design, management de projet, programmation — build games together). Track chosen at application. M2 delivered in English. Concrete module list not published on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED, request the maquette from the scolarité.
programs.entryRequirements: RNCP level 6 diploma (licence, licence pro, BUT, bachelor) or equivalent bac+3; or VES/VAPP validation (3+ years of professional/personal experience). For a foreign diploma the official page requires an ENIC-NARIC France 'attestation de comparabilité' at CEC level 6 or above, plus B2 French. Then a competitive concours: creative dossier → written exam → oral exam. His BSc Software Engineering satisfies the academic bar; the concours does not.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES on paper — no music degree, conservatoire training or prior audio employment is required; the official page says no specific prior educational path is required and explicitly welcomes candidates with personal project experience. In practice the creative dossier is where a non-portfolio candidate fails.
programs.portfolioSpec: Mandatory 'dossier créatif' answering a published brief — 'Cahier des charges et sujet du concours 2026' (PDF published on enjmin.cnam.fr, released with the call). Followed by a written exam and an oral. Exact sound-track brief contents: see that year's cahier des charges — the 2027 brief will be published when the call opens.
programs.auditionSpec: No musical audition. Selection is: creative dossier, then a remote written exam, then an oral (remote or on site).
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Not detailed on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED. Enjmin is the national public game school with game-production studios in Angoulême.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: the 2026 concours brief was released Friday 12 December 2025, 15:00. Expect the 2027 call around mid-December 2026 — which fits his October 2026–February 2027 window.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: dossier deadline Friday 23 January 2026, 12:00 UTC+1. Dossier results 5 March 2026; written exam 28 March 2026 (remote); orals 26–29 May 2026; final results 3 June 2026; M1 begins 7 September 2026. The equivalent 2027 calendar had not been published at the time of checking.
programs.tuitionEU: Not published on the pages I opened. The Cnam page links to a 'Tarifs' form rather than stating a figure — UNVERIFIED. The national master rate set by ministerial order is the reference; ask Enjmin scolarité.
programs.tuitionNonEU: THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY. The Cnam's own governing-board annex states the differentiated fees are '2 770 € pour une Licence et de 3 770 € pour un Master, avec une majoration prévue à 3 879 € pour le Master à partir de la rentrée 2024-2025', that 'Le CNAM applique les frais d'inscription différenciés', and it names ENJMIN among the schools concerned. Critically, the same document records that only three schools (ESGT, INSEAC, EPN5) agreed to exempt — ENJMIN is NOT among them. So expect roughly 3 879 € per year, no institutional exemption. Confirm the 2027-2028 figure with Enjmin before applying.
programs.otherFees: CVEC (contribution vie étudiante et de campus) is payable in addition — amount not stated on the Cnam pages I opened, UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Roughly 3 900 € tuition per year plus CVEC plus living costs in Angoulême; the school does not publish a living-cost estimate — UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: None specific to this programme on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED. General French-government routes (Eiffel, Campus France Tunisia) are already in the database and would have to be paired with it.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. It is a diplôme national de master at a public establishment. Note the official page's important procedural point: since 2025 international candidates apply DIRECTLY through the Cnam-Enjmin concours, not through Études en France; Études en France is used only afterwards, once admitted, to obtain the visa.
programs.recommendation: The single best thematic fit in this sweep for a software engineer who wants to work in sound — game audio sits exactly on the seam between his BSc and his ambition, and the official page genuinely does not require a music degree. Two hard cautions. (1) The gate is a creative dossier plus written and oral exams for a very small public school; with no portfolio today he must spend 2026 building game-audio work specifically against the published cahier des charges, which appears in December. (2) It is NOT a DJ/producer programme — it trains game sound designers. Also note the cost: unlike most French universities, the Cnam does not exempt non-EU students, so budget ~3 879 €/year rather than the ~255 € headline. Deadline discipline matters: the brief drops mid-December and closes ~23 January, so he must have the ENIC-NARIC attestation de comparabilité and a B2 French certificate in hand by November 2026.

programs.program: Master mention Audiovisuel, médias interactifs numériques, jeux — parcours Ingénierie des Systèmes Images et Sons (ISIS)
programs.institution: Université Polytechnique Hauts-de-France (UPHF), Campus Mont Houy
programs.institutionType: Public university (université, EPSCP), with INSA Hauts-de-France inside the same group
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. How I know: it is a state university (université publique) delivering a diplôme national de master; its own registration-fee page applies the state-set national rate (255 €) and the ministerial differentiated rate for non-EU students, which only public establishments levy.
programs.qualification: Diplôme national de master (the course page carries the 'DNM' label), bac+5, 120 ECTS. Real second-cycle state degree supporting a student residence permit. No RNCP number displayed on the page — UNVERIFIED, ask the scolarité.
programs.accreditationStatus: Diplôme national de master (DNM label shown on the official catalogue page). RNCP number not displayed — UNVERIFIED.
programs.language: French. The official page states B2 French is required.
programs.languageRequirement: French B2 (stated on the official UPHF catalogue page). No English certificate demanded on the page I opened.
programs.englishTest: None required on the official page — his untaken IELTS/TOEFL is not a blocker here.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters, 2 years, 120 ECTS, bac+5.
programs.focus: Audio and audiovisual systems engineering: room acoustics, electroacoustics, sound-reinforcement/diffusion engineering, audiovisual signal processing and transmission.
programs.whatYouStudy: Modules named on the official page include 'Acoustique des salles' (room acoustics), 'Diffusion sonore' (sound reinforcement/distribution), 'Signaux et systèmes audiovisuels' at multiple levels (audiovisual signal processing), and 'Vidéotransmission'. The parent mention's three tracks (ISIS, Productions, Postproduction) all carry 'Son I–IV' teaching. Outcomes named: R&D engineer, technical director, systems engineer, audiovisual architect, for broadcasters, service providers, telecom operators and engineering firms.
programs.entryRequirements: A licence (180 ECTS) in audiovisual, telecommunications, applied physics, IT/computer science, or multimedia; the page also says 'tout titulaire d'une Licence ou équivalent', with VAP available for non-standard backgrounds. His BSc Software Engineering is squarely inside the named list.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — and this is the point: it explicitly targets IT/telecoms/physics graduates. No music degree, no conservatoire training, no audio work history required.
programs.portfolioSpec: None published — selection is on dossier via candidature.uphf.fr. UNVERIFIED whether any additional test exists; ask the scolarité.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Not detailed on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED. Teaching is at Campus Mont Houy, Valenciennes.
programs.applicationOpens: Not published on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED. Procedure is described at https://www.uphf.fr/formation/candidatures-inscriptions ; non-EU applicants resident in an Études en France country (Tunisia is one) go through the Études en France portal, per the official page.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — no date on the official catalogue page. For a Tunisian national the binding date will be the Études en France / Campus France Tunisie campaign deadline, typically closing in the winter/spring before a September intake. Ask candidatures@uphf.fr and Campus France Tunis.
programs.tuitionEU: 255 € for a master, non-scholarship holder, academic year 2026-2027 (0 € for French state grant-holders), per UPHF's own droits d'inscription page.
programs.tuitionNonEU: THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY: '3 950 € par an pour un cycle master ou un cycle d'ingénieur' for students from outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland/Ukraine, academic year 2026-2027, quoted verbatim from UPHF's official droits d'inscription page. No exemption is described on that page. Confirm the 2027-2028 figure and whether UPHF votes an exemption scheme (national rules cap institutional exemptions at 30% of liable students in 2026-2027, falling to 25% then 20%).
programs.otherFees: CVEC 105 € (stated on the same official UPHF page).
programs.totalCostEstimate: ~4 055 €/year (3 950 € + 105 € CVEC) plus living costs; Valenciennes is a low-cost city relative to Paris/Lyon. Living-cost figure not published by UPHF — UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: None specific to this programme found on the official pages — UNVERIFIED. Would have to be paired with Eiffel / French embassy routes already in the database.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — diplôme national de master at a public university; the official page routes non-EU applicants through Études en France.
programs.recommendation: Alongside the Lyon acoustics master, this is one of only two options in this sweep he could actually be admitted to as he stands today: a real state master's degree that names computer science among its expected entry backgrounds, selects on dossier, and asks for no portfolio and no audition. Teaching is in French, which he has. The honest caveat is what it is: broadcast/AV and sound-systems engineering — room acoustics, PA design, signal chains — not music production, and it will not by itself make him a producer or DJ. Treat it as a fundable, visa-safe technical base with a strong regional cost profile, and build the music side privately alongside. Budget the real 3 950 €/year, not the 255 € headline, unless he secures an exemption or an Eiffel-type scholarship.

programs.program: International Master of Science in Acoustics (Master Acoustique)
programs.institution: École Centrale de Lyon, in partnership with INSA Lyon and ENTPE (Université de Lyon), supported by the CeLyA acoustics laboratory cluster
programs.institutionType: Three public grandes écoles d'ingénieurs (state engineering schools) delivering a joint national master
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. How I know: Centrale Lyon, INSA Lyon and ENTPE are all state engineering schools (EPSCP / public establishments under ministerial supervision); the programme's own application page applies the state differentiated fee for non-EU students, a public-sector mechanism.
programs.qualification: Master of Science in Acoustics — a French diplôme national de master delivered jointly by Centrale Lyon, INSA Lyon and ENTPE. Real second-cycle state degree supporting a student residence permit. RNCP number not shown on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED.
programs.accreditationStatus: State master delivered by three accredited public engineering schools. Specific RNCP registration not displayed on the official pages — UNVERIFIED, ask the programme office.
programs.language: English. Centrale Lyon's official page states the programme is delivered in English; the programme site notes English and/or French courses are provided, with French/English language support in M1 so that M2 courses can be followed in either language.
programs.languageRequirement: English B2 for both M1 and M2 entry (official Centrale Lyon page). The application page requires an English certificate — TOEFL iBT, TOEIC, IELTS or Cambridge — unless English is the applicant's native language or he completed at least 3 years of education in English.
programs.englishTest: REQUIRED: TOEFL iBT, TOEIC, IELTS or Cambridge, at a level corresponding to B2. Exact minimum scores are not published on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED, ask the programme office. He has not sat one; this is the one certificate he must book.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years (M1 + M2), 740 hours of in-person instruction across both years, plus a 4–12 week internship in M1 and a 22–26 week thesis placement in M2. Total ECTS not stated on the pages I opened (27 ECTS are attributable to M2 optional specialisation courses) — UNVERIFIED, though a French DNM is 120 ECTS.
programs.focus: Scientific and engineering acoustics, with M2 specialisation options including sound perception — the closest branch to audio/psychoacoustics.
programs.whatYouStudy: M1: fundamentals of mechanics, continuum physics and data/signal processing plus introductory acoustics. M2 specialisation choices published on the official programme site: aeroacoustics, building acoustics, vehicle acoustics, sound perception, ultrasounds, vibro-acoustics, fluid-structure interactions. Theoretical courses, numerical and experimental work, laboratory projects, and more than one semester of research training as an intern in a laboratory or in industry, in France or abroad.
programs.entryRequirements: M1 entry: a bachelor's degree in a scientific subject related to the master's themes, plus English B2. Selection is on dossier. Required documents (official application page): CV, motivation letter, passport/ID copy, ID photo, reference letter(s), transcripts, copy of last degree awarded, English language certificate.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — it is a physics/engineering master and expects no music background whatsoever. His BSc Software Engineering is a plausible 'scientific subject', though acoustics normally assumes stronger physics/mechanics than a pure software curriculum; the admissions committee judges relatedness on dossier. Worth writing to them first with his transcript.
programs.portfolioSpec: None. No creative portfolio is requested — selection is purely academic dossier. This is decisive for a candidate with no portfolio.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition.
programs.equipmentRequired: None published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Backed by the CeLyA (Centre Lyonnais d'Acoustique) laboratory cluster, with laboratory-based projects and research internships; the programme states close connections to industry across several fields.
programs.applicationOpens: Not published on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — the official application page I opened does not publish a dated calendar. Secondary sources referenced an application deadline of 30/04/2026 with a committee reply on 29/05/2026 (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date), but I could not confirm those dates on the institution's own page; ask the programme office directly. The official page does state that international students must follow the Études en France procedure in parallel with the online application — for a Tunisian national the Campus France Tunisie calendar will bind first, so treat autumn 2026 as the real start.
programs.tuitionEU: Not stated on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED (the national master rate applies; ask the school).
programs.tuitionNonEU: THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY: 3 770 € stated for non-EU students on the programme's official application page (master-acoustics.ec-lyon.fr/application). Confirm the 2027-2028 figure — the national differentiated master rate was uplifted to 3 879 € from 2024-2025 and several institutions now publish 3 941–3 950 €, so this figure may be behind.
programs.otherFees: CVEC payable in addition — amount not published on the programme pages, UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: ~3 800–4 000 €/year tuition plus CVEC plus Lyon living costs (Lyon is France's second-most expensive student city). No official living-cost estimate on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: No scholarship information on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED. Ask about Centrale Lyon / Université de Lyon international scholarships and pair with Eiffel (already in the database; note Eiffel is nominated by the institution, so he would need Centrale Lyon to put him forward, which means contacting them by autumn 2026).
programs.visaEligible: Yes — public establishments, national master, and the programme explicitly instructs international applicants to run Études en France in parallel.
programs.recommendation: Realistically his most admissible option in France: no portfolio, no audition, no music degree, no French-language gate, and an entry rule written for science graduates. It is also the one where his software background is an asset rather than an oddity, and 'sound perception' plus signal processing is a legitimate on-ramp to audio DSP and immersive-audio work. Three honest caveats. (1) It is acoustics engineering — it will not train him as a producer or DJ; that ambition has to be pursued in parallel. (2) His curriculum is software, not mechanics/physics; he should email the programme office with his transcript in autumn 2026 before investing in an application. (3) He must book IELTS or TOEFL — this is the only programme in this batch that demands a certificate he does not yet have. Cost is the standard non-EU rate with no exemption published, so plan on paying, or get nominated for Eiffel early.

programs.program: Master mention Musicologie — parcours Création-Production en musiques actuelles (CPMA) (the faculty also lists the track under the name 'Écoute critique et production en musiques actuelles')
programs.institution: Université de Strasbourg, Faculté des arts, Département de musique
programs.institutionType: Public university (EPSCP)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. How I know: Université de Strasbourg is a state university; its own tuition page publishes the ministerially-set national rate (255 €) and the differentiated non-EU rate, and its exemption decisions are taken by an institutional committee — both public-sector mechanisms.
programs.qualification: Diplôme national de master, mention Musicologie. Real second-cycle state degree supporting a student residence permit. RNCP number not shown on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED.
programs.accreditationStatus: State-accredited diplôme national de master at a public university.
programs.language: French (stated explicitly on the official catalogue page). An English course is included in the curriculum but instruction is French.
programs.languageRequirement: French at C1 — listed as a mandatory prerequisite on the official catalogue page ('bonne maîtrise de l'expression et de la rédaction en français', C1). He is fluent in French, so this is one of the few programmes where his language profile is an advantage; but he should expect to have to evidence C1 with a DELF/DALF or TCF certificate for the visa file.
programs.englishTest: None required.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 ECTS, 724 total teaching hours, in-person only (no distance option). Ends with a dissertation articulated with a public recital/production of roughly 60 minutes.
programs.focus: Music production and studio technology in the service of creation, in popular/contemporary music (musiques actuelles) — the closest thing in this sweep to his stated goal of music production and electronic music.
programs.whatYouStudy: Named on the official faculty page: critical listening and technical ear training; composition and orchestration with digital audio workstations; sound recording, mixing and mastering; analogue synthesis; composition for audiovisual and video games; sound design and artistic direction; professional practice in music production, publishing and copyright. Project-based pedagogy with substantial autonomous work; a 120-hour internship. Named outcomes: sound engineer, music producer, composer for audiovisual/games, sound designer, artistic director.
programs.entryRequirements: The official page states eligibility as 'Tout étudiant titulaire d'une licence de musique (ou d'un diplôme étranger équivalent)'. Mandatory prerequisites listed: advanced DAW skills; strong practical musicianship; composition and/or production competence; knowledge of sound reinforcement, acoustics or popular-music instrumentation; knowledge of the contemporary music industry; C1 French; academic research and writing competence; and music-theory fundamentals (score reading, analysis, composition), history and aesthetics of popular music.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO, in practice. The official entry rule is a music licence or an equivalent foreign degree, and the published prerequisites include score reading, analysis and orchestration. A BSc Software Engineering with no conservatoire training and no portfolio does not meet the stated conditions. He could only argue equivalence, and would still have to demonstrate the musicianship prerequisites.
programs.portfolioSpec: Not explicitly published on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED. Given the prerequisites, expect production work to be assessed; ask the programme director, Sébastien Lebray (lebray@unistra.fr).
programs.auditionSpec: Not published — UNVERIFIED. The degree concludes with a public recital of ~60 minutes, which indicates a performing/producing standard is expected at entry. Confirm with the department.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Studio-based teaching (recording, mixing, mastering, analogue synthesis) at the Faculté des arts, 14 rue René Descartes, Campus Esplanade. Specific studio inventory not published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — no dated calendar on the pages I opened. Route: applications go through Mon Master (monmaster.gouv.fr), EXCEPT non-European candidates resident in a country covered by the Études en France procedure. Tunisia is an Études en France country, so he would apply through Campus France Tunisie / Études en France, not Mon Master — and that calendar opens in autumn.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — confirm with the Faculté des arts and with Campus France Tunisie for the Études en France campaign closing date for a September 2027 intake.
programs.tuitionEU: 255 € for master level, published on the University of Strasbourg's own tuition page (2025-2026).
programs.tuitionNonEU: THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY: 3 950 € at master level for non-EU (extracommunautaire) students, published on the University of Strasbourg's own tuition page (2025-2026). Strasbourg operates a Tuition Fee Exemption Committee through which international students may individually request exemption from the differentiated fees — the exemption rate and criteria are not stated on the page I opened (UNVERIFIED; ask the Service de la vie universitaire). A transitional exemption exists only for students already enrolled at Unistra in 2023/24 and 2024/25, which would not cover him.
programs.otherFees: CVEC payable in addition — amount not stated on the page I opened, UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: ~3 950 €/year plus CVEC plus Strasbourg living costs, unless the exemption committee reduces the fee to the national 255 €. No official living-cost figure — UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: None specific to this programme on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED. The relevant lever is the Unistra Tuition Fee Exemption Committee plus the national Eiffel route already in the database.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — public university, national master; but note the applicant route for Tunisians is Études en France rather than Mon Master.
programs.recommendation: On content this is the best match in France for what he actually wants — mixing, mastering, analogue synthesis, DAW composition, music for games, and the business of production, in a real state master's degree at low national fees if he wins an exemption. On eligibility it is the worst match in this batch: the official entry rule is a music licence, and the published prerequisites (score reading, analysis, orchestration, existing production competence) describe someone with years of formal musical training. He has none. Do not build the plan around it. If he wants to keep it alive, the only route is (a) write to Sébastien Lebray in autumn 2026 asking whether a non-music bachelor with a strong production portfolio can be considered under 'diplôme étranger équivalent', and (b) spend 2026-27 producing enough finished, mixed and mastered work to make that argument. Realistically this is a 2028 target, not 2027.

programs.program: Master mention Musicologie — parcours Musiques Appliquées aux Arts Visuels (MAAAV), M1 and M2
programs.institution: Université Lumière Lyon 2, UFR Lettres, sciences du langage et arts (LESLA), Campus Rachais
programs.institutionType: Public university (EPSCP)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. How I know: Université Lumière Lyon 2 is a state university; its official pages state that enrolment consists of 'les droits d'inscription nationaux, plus la contribution Vie Etudiante et de Campus (CVEC)' and it publishes the ministerially-set differentiated fee for non-EU students — public-sector mechanisms.
programs.qualification: Diplôme national de master, mention Musicologie, parcours MAAAV. Registered RNCP N°39199 (stated on the official M2 page). Real second-cycle state degree supporting a student residence permit.
programs.accreditationStatus: Diplôme national de master, RNCP 39199.
programs.language: French. An English-language course is part of the curriculum, but instruction is in French.
programs.languageRequirement: No certificate level published on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED. Assume French B2/C1 will be demanded in the Études en France file; ask the LESLA scolarité (lesla.m1maaav@univ-lyon2.fr).
programs.englishTest: None required.
programs.durationEcts: M1 60 ECTS + M2, 2 years total. M1 includes a compulsory internship of at least 12 weeks full-time in semester 2; M2 semester 4 is a compulsory internship plus dissertation defence. In-person only, Campus Rachais, Lyon.
programs.focus: Composing and producing music for the moving image — cinema (animation, live action, documentary), video games, advertising, television and multimedia.
programs.whatYouStudy: From the official M2 page, semester 3 covers: cinematic culture and research methodology, intellectual property law, history of film sound, improvisation for visual media, electronic music, virtual instrument programming, advanced mixing and mastering, English, and musical composition and orchestration applied to image. Semester 4 is a compulsory internship plus dissertation. Core competences named: image analysis, orchestration technique, and command of digital audio workstations (MAO).
programs.entryRequirements: Entry is at M1 by competitive selection (concours), 16 places per cohort; open to holders of a licence in any field, or via continuing education/VAPP with at least 5 years of professional activity in music. Critically, the official M1 page states the target profile as 'Etre déjà compositeur au moment du recrutement' — i.e. already a composer at the time of recruitment — with command of music notation, orchestration and DAW tools. M2 entry is normally reserved for those who completed M1 MAAAV.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Formally yes — a licence in ANY discipline is accepted, which is unusual and would admit his BSc Software Engineering. Substantively no — the official page requires the applicant to already be a composer with command of music notation and orchestration. The open-discipline rule exists for self-taught composers, not for career changers with no music.
programs.portfolioSpec: A composition portfolio is the selection instrument. The programme requires three recent personal compositions in varied styles, written to three short films: three audio files (wav or mp3) synchronised to three short films of 3–5 minutes maximum, plus three corresponding scores in PDF. NOTE: this specification comes from the programme's own dedicated site (maaav.fr) rather than the univ-lyon2.fr catalogue pages I opened — confirm the exact 2027 brief with the scolarité before relying on it.
programs.auditionSpec: Selection is by concours on the composition portfolio; whether an interview follows is not stated on the official pages I opened — UNVERIFIED.
programs.equipmentRequired: Stated on the official M1 page: a powerful computer; advanced DAW software (Logic Pro X, Reaper or Cubase); quality headphones; an audio interface with a keyboard controller. This is a published, mandatory technical prerequisite — a real cost line for him.
programs.facilities: Campus Rachais, Lyon; students work on their own DAW rigs (see equipment requirement). Studio inventory not published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED. Route: the official M1 page states applications are made exclusively online through Mon Master (monmaster.gouv.fr); the M2 page refers to eCandidat and notes separate procedures for EU and non-EU applicants. As a Tunisian national resident in Tunisia he would normally go through Études en France/Campus France Tunisie instead of Mon Master — confirm which portal applies to him before the campaign opens.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — no dated calendar on the pages I opened; the M2 page refers to a 'calendrier de candidature'. Confirm with lesla.m1maaav@univ-lyon2.fr and Campus France Tunisie.
programs.tuitionEU: 255 € for 'Master, Préparation CAPES et Agrégation', academic year 2026-2027, from Lyon 2's official droits d'inscription page.
programs.tuitionNonEU: THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY: 3 950 € at master level for non-EU students, academic year 2026-2027, from Lyon 2's official droits d'inscription page. programs.otherFees: CVEC payable in addition (Lyon 2 states enrolment = national fees + CVEC); amount not shown on the page I opened — UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: ~3 950 €/year plus CVEC plus Lyon living costs, plus the mandatory home studio rig (computer, DAW licence, interface, controller, headphones). No official estimate — UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: None specific to this programme on the official pages — UNVERIFIED. Note the programme states international recruitment with 36 countries represented, so non-EU applicants are clearly admitted in practice; ask the scolarité what fee exemption exists.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — public university, diplôme national de master, RNCP 39199.
programs.recommendation: Report it so he knows it exists, but do not queue it for 2027. The unusual open-discipline rule (a licence in any field) makes it look reachable for a software engineer, and the M2 content — electronic music, virtual instrument programming, advanced mixing and mastering — reads well against his goals. The gate closes it: 16 places a year, decided on three original scored compositions written to three short films, with the official page stating the candidate must already be a composer commanding music notation and orchestration. He cannot write orchestral scores and has a year, not five. If film/game scoring genuinely attracts him, this is a 2029-2030 target reachable only after sustained composition study; the ENJMIN sound-design route and the two engineering routes are the ones that fit the profile he actually has.

programs.program: Medieningenieurwissenschaften (M.Sc.) — Media Engineering Science (successor title of the former M.Sc. Medientechnologie)
programs.institution: Technische Universität Ilmenau
programs.institutionType: Technische Universität (state technical university), Free State of Thuringia
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. TU Ilmenau is a Körperschaft des öffentlichen Rechts and a state institution of the Free State of Thuringia, funded and governed under the Thüringer Hochschulgesetz. Its fee page publishes only a Semesterbeitrag plus statutory administrative fees (no tuition), which is only possible for a state institution.
programs.qualification: Master of Science (M.Sc.) — a genuine second-cycle German degree, 120 ECTS, awarded by a state university with the right to award doctorates. Fully supports a §16b AufenthG student residence permit.
programs.accreditationStatus: State university programme under Thuringian higher-education law. The specific programme accreditation seal/expiry is not published on the programme page — UNVERIFIED; ask info.apply@tu-ilmenau.de or check the Akkreditierungsrat database (antrag.akkreditierungsrat.de) for 'Medieningenieurwissenschaften TU Ilmenau'.
programs.language: German AND English — the official programme page states the degree can be completed bilingually (Deutsch/Englisch). Many audio/media modules are taught in English, but a German-free path is NOT guaranteed.
programs.languageRequirement: The programme page says only that 'language certificates may be required for international applicants depending on their educational background'. The exact required level (German DSH/TestDaF vs English B2/C1) is NOT published — UNVERIFIED. Ask info.apply@tu-ilmenau.de before investing in a test. Note: the sibling English-taught Ilmenau masters normally require English B2/C1 only.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS. Start 1 October or 1 April.
programs.focus: Media/audio engineering: audio signal processing, audio coding (psychoacoustics, quantisation, filterbanks, MPEG audio, parametric coding), video technology, media production technology, software development for digital media. Ilmenau's Electronic Media Technology and Audiovisual Technology groups (psychoacoustics, virtual acoustics, audio signal processing, quality evaluation) teach into it, and Fraunhofer IDMT — the mp3/AAC institute — sits on the same campus.
programs.whatYouStudy: Roughly 34-42% engineering disciplines, 17% media technology, 13-21% research/media project work, 4% soft skills, 25% thesis. A large group media project is a core element. Work in the I3TC laboratories.
programs.entryRequirements: A related bachelor's degree (engineering/computer science/media technology). NC-free (no numerus clausus). A master aptitude assessment (Master-Eignungsprüfung) run by the department is a standard part of the master application at TU Ilmenau. A BSc Software Engineering is a plausible related degree, but the department decides; the number of ECTS in electrical engineering/signal processing on his transcript will be the deciding factor.
programs.auditionSpec: None. No audition.
programs.portfolioSpec: None required. This is an engineering master — his lack of a music portfolio is NOT a barrier here. This is the single most important reason to put Ilmenau at the top of his German list.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly an engineering degree; no music degree, conservatory training or audio work experience is required.
programs.equipmentRequired: None stated. University laboratories/studios are provided.
programs.facilities: I3TC (Ilmenau Interdisciplinary Innovation Test Centre) laboratories; Electronic Media Technology Group and Audiovisual Technology Group labs (listening rooms, virtual acoustics); campus adjacency to Fraunhofer IDMT.
programs.intakes: Winter semester (start 1 October) and summer semester (start 1 April).
programs.applicationOpens: Non-EU/EEA applicants: the application window for the winter semester runs 16 January – 15 May; for the summer semester 1 August – 15 November. Applications go through uni-assist, not the direct portal. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date (these are the recurring windows published on the application page, not year-stamped).
programs.deadline: 15 May for a winter (October) start, for applicants with foreign qualifications. For a SEPTEMBER/OCTOBER 2027 intake he must apply between 16 January and 15 May 2027. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.tuitionEU: No tuition fee. Semester contribution only.
programs.tuitionNonEU: IDENTICAL to the EU rate — Thuringia charges no tuition to non-EU nationals. He would pay the same semester contribution as a German student. Note one real risk: TU Ilmenau charges a Langzeitstudiengebühr of EUR 500.00 per semester once the standard study period is exceeded, and EUR 20.00 for late payment of the contribution.
programs.otherFees: Semester contribution: the official 'Beiträge und Gebühren' page does NOT publish a flat figure — it says the amount is calculated per student and shown in the Campus Portal under Studienservice > Zahlungen. The exact amount is UNVERIFIED; ask studierendensekretariat/info.apply@tu-ilmenau.de. Published add-ons: EUR 20.00 student ID card, EUR 20.00 late-payment fee, EUR 500.00 per excess semester. A EUR 25.00 administrative fee is charged for checking foreign educational certificates (waived if a uni-assist VPD is already supplied).
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition EUR 0. Semester contribution UNVERIFIED (Thuringian contributions are typically well under EUR 200/semester, but do not budget on that — confirm). Living costs plus the blocked account (Sperrkonto) required for the visa are the real cost: the blocked-account amount is set nationally by the Foreign Office and must be checked at the German embassy in Tunis for 2027 — UNVERIFIED here.
programs.scholarships: No programme-specific scholarship is published. A Tunisian national would realistically compete for DAAD Study Scholarships or the Deutschlandstipendium (nomination by the university, 300 EUR/month). Neither is guaranteed. UNVERIFIED whether TU Ilmenau nominates Deutschlandstipendium holders in this programme — ask the Studierendenservice.
programs.fundingLevel: None (no tuition to fund; no programme stipend). Living costs self-funded unless he wins DAAD.
programs.englishTest: Possibly none, possibly B2/C1 English — UNVERIFIED, see languageRequirement. Do not book IELTS until the Studierendensekretariat confirms which certificate this programme demands.
programs.visaEligible: YES. Full-time, on-campus, state second-cycle degree at a state university — a textbook basis for a German student residence permit (§16b AufenthG).
programs.recommendation: STRONGEST realistic German target found in this sweep for him. It is the only one of these records that needs no portfolio, no audition and no music degree, and it sits in the German audio-engineering heartland (Fraunhofer IDMT = mp3/AAC). It will not make him a DJ, but it makes him employable in audio tech and buys him three years in Germany to build the DJ/producer career on the side. Two things to settle before he commits: (1) the language certificate actually demanded, (2) whether his SMU MedTech transcript carries enough signal-processing/EE credits for the departmental aptitude assessment. Both are single emails.

programs.program: Medientechnologie (M.Sc.) — Media Technology
programs.institution: Technische Hochschule Köln (TH Köln / Cologne University of Applied Sciences), Faculty of Information, Media and Electrical Engineering (F07), Campus Deutz
programs.institutionType: Fachhochschule / University of Applied Sciences (state)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. TH Köln is a state university of applied sciences of North Rhine-Westphalia, governed by the Hochschulgesetz NRW and financed by the Land. NRW abolished tuition fees in 2011 and TH Köln charges none.
programs.qualification: Master of Science (M.Sc.), 90 ECTS — a real, state-recognised second-cycle degree. Research-oriented profile, so it also opens a doctorate route (through a cooperating university or the NRW Promotionskolleg).
programs.accreditationStatus: State programme under HG NRW; TH Köln is system-accredited. Programme-level seal/expiry not shown on the programme page — UNVERIFIED; check antrag.akkreditierungsrat.de.
programs.language: GERMAN ONLY. The official programme page states the language of instruction is German, with no English track.
programs.languageRequirement: TH Köln's international admissions page states that for German-taught programmes proof of at least C1 German is generally required at the time of application (DSH-2 / TestDaF 4x4 / telc C1 Hochschule or equivalent). For a candidate who currently has no German at all, C1 by early 2027 is roughly 900-1000 contact hours — realistically 12-18 months of full-time study.
programs.durationEcts: 3 semesters, 90 ECTS. Start possible in both winter and summer semesters.
programs.focus: Audio and acoustics is one of the named specialisation strands: methods of virtual acoustics that convey a realistic spatial sound impression interactively, object-based audio concepts and simulation methods — i.e. 3D/immersive audio and room acoustics simulation, alongside video/audiovisual media technology.
programs.whatYouStudy: Semesters 1-2: three compulsory modules plus six elective modules (audio/acoustics electives among them) and a large group master project in which a complete technical system is specified, built and tested. Semester 3: master thesis and colloquium.
programs.entryRequirements: HARD GATE. Requires (a) a degree in a relevant natural-science or technical field, (b) at least 110 ECTS in mathematics, physics, electrical engineering and computer science, (c) an overall grade of 2.7 (German scale) or better, and (d) a first degree worth AT LEAST 210 ECTS. A standard 3-year 180-ECTS BSc does NOT meet (d) — he would have to make up 30 ECTS, or the examination committee may impose conditions to be completed before thesis submission. He must have his SMU MedTech transcript credit-converted before assuming eligibility.
programs.auditionSpec: None.
programs.portfolioSpec: None required.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — it is an engineering master and expects a technical, not musical, background. But the 210-ECTS rule and C1 German are the real filters.
programs.equipmentRequired: None stated; laboratory and studio facilities provided.
programs.facilities: F07 media technology laboratories at Campus Deutz, including facilities for virtual acoustics and object-based audio work (the faculty's acoustics group is well known for spatial audio research).
programs.applicationOpens: TH Köln's online application opens around end of April for the winter semester and around end of November for the summer semester. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.deadline: 15 July for the winter semester and 15 January for the summer semester are the key dates published for most TH Köln programmes; applicants with foreign qualifications route through uni-assist, which needs several weeks of lead time. For a September/October 2027 start: submit to uni-assist by roughly April 2027 and to TH Köln by 15 July 2027. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date on the programme's own 'Bewerbung' tab.
programs.tuitionEU: No tuition fee (NRW).
programs.tuitionNonEU: IDENTICAL — NRW charges no tuition to non-EU nationals. He pays only the semester contribution.
programs.otherFees: Semester contribution (Sozialbeitrag + NRW/Deutschlandsemesterticket): exact amount NOT published on the programme page — UNVERIFIED. Ask the TH Köln Studierendensekretariat (studierendensekretariat@th-koeln.de). uni-assist charges its own handling fee (first application EUR 75, further applications EUR 30 in recent cycles — confirm on uni-assist.de).
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition EUR 0 + semester contribution (UNVERIFIED) + uni-assist fee + Cologne living costs, which are among the higher German ones. Blocked-account requirement per German embassy Tunis — UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: None specific to the programme. DAAD and Deutschlandstipendium are the realistic routes. UNVERIFIED whether F07 nominates for Deutschlandstipendium.
programs.englishTest: None — this is a German-taught programme. IELTS/TOEFL is irrelevant here; his money should go to German instead.
programs.visaEligible: YES. Full-time state M.Sc. at a state UAS.
programs.recommendation: Technically the best spatial-audio content of any German UAS master I verified, and free. But for THIS candidate it is a stretch on three axes at once: C1 German from zero, 210 ECTS in a first degree he probably does not have, and a 2.7-or-better grade conversion. Treat as a stretch/second-cycle target (2028+) rather than a September 2027 plan, unless he starts intensive German now AND gets a written ECTS assessment from the F07 examination committee (Prof. Dr. Gregor Fischer, gregor.fischer@th-koeln.de) this year.

programs.program: Populäre Musik und Medien (M.A.)
programs.institution: Universität Paderborn, Fakultät für Kulturwissenschaften, Fach Musik (in the Musikwissenschaftliches Seminar Detmold/Paderborn, run jointly with the Hochschule für Musik Detmold)
programs.institutionType: Universität (state research university), North Rhine-Westphalia
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Universität Paderborn is a Land NRW state university; its fee page publishes only a Semesterbeitrag and states no tuition fees are charged.
programs.qualification: Master of Arts (M.A.) — a real, state-recognised second-cycle university degree with doctoral progression rights.
programs.accreditationStatus: State university programme under HG NRW. Programme seal/expiry not on the page — UNVERIFIED; check antrag.akkreditierungsrat.de.
programs.language: GERMAN. The teaching and the entire programme documentation are in German; the subject matter (German popular-music culture, media discourse) is language-bound.
programs.languageRequirement: Not stated on the programme's own admission page — UNVERIFIED. Paderborn's general international-applicant route requires DSH/TestDaF for German-taught programmes and offers a preparatory German course (indicated in question 11 of the admission application), during which applicants apply for the degree via PAUL. Ask international-office@zv.uni-paderborn.de for the exact level demanded for this M.A.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters is the standard for this M.A.; the exact ECTS figure is not stated on the admission page — UNVERIFIED (the Prüfungsordnung on the Fach Musik site will state it). About 20 places.
programs.focus: Popular music and media: history and current developments of popular music, music and media industries, production and mediation cultures, analysis of popular music. It is a cultural-studies/musicology master, NOT a studio or production degree — he would write about music production, not do it.
programs.whatYouStudy: Module descriptions are published on the Fach Musik site; the emphasis is historical and current developments in popular music and media, with research methods and a master thesis.
programs.entryRequirements: The same-named B.A. or a 'fachverwandter' (subject-related) bachelor. For a related degree the examination committee decides on equivalence on the basis of the file, a letter of motivation and possibly an interview. A BSc Software Engineering is NOT obviously fachverwandt — he would need the motivation letter plus documented engagement with popular music (coursework, internships, artistic activity) to carry the case. The programme is zulassungsfrei (admission-free, no competitive NC), which materially improves his odds if the committee accepts equivalence.
programs.auditionSpec: NO audition. The page states evaluation is on academic background, professional experience in music/media, and demonstrated engagement with popular music and culture.
programs.portfolioSpec: No formal portfolio required; a letter of motivation is required and evidence of engagement with the field (internships, artistic activity) is weighed.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY — no music degree or conservatory training is required and there is no audition, but the committee must accept his BSc as subject-related. This is the one German record here where his missing portfolio is least fatal.
programs.equipmentRequired: None.
programs.facilities: Shared with the Hochschule für Musik Detmold / Musikwissenschaftliches Seminar Detmold-Paderborn.
programs.intakes: Winter semester primarily; summer semester only if winter places remain unfilled.
programs.applicationOpens: Winter semester: from early June. Summer semester: from early December. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date (the page carried a November 2021 place-count note, so the whole date block must be re-checked).
programs.deadline: Winter semester: 23 October. Summer semester: 21 March. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. WARNING: a 23 October deadline is AFTER the semester starts and leaves no time to obtain a visa — an international applicant must apply far earlier via uni-assist and should ask the Studierendensekretariat for the international deadline, which is normally 15 July.
programs.tuitionEU: No tuition fee.
programs.tuitionNonEU: IDENTICAL — no tuition for non-EU nationals in NRW.
programs.otherFees: Semester contribution winter semester 2026/27: EUR 351.15 total, published as Sozialbeitrag EUR 110.00 + AStA EUR 12.50 + Deutschlandsemesterticket EUR 226.80 + Kulturticket EUR 1.85. (Guest auditors pay EUR 100.00.) uni-assist handling fee extra.
programs.totalCostEstimate: About EUR 702/year in semester contributions at the 2026/27 rate, plus living costs in Paderborn (one of the cheaper German university towns) and the blocked account for the visa.
programs.scholarships: None programme-specific. DAAD / Deutschlandstipendium only.
programs.englishTest: None — German-taught. IELTS/TOEFL not the relevant test.
programs.visaEligible: YES. Full-time state M.A.
programs.recommendation: Include on the list only if he is willing to learn German to DSH level AND accepts that this is an academic degree ABOUT popular music, not a production degree. Its virtues are real for his profile: admission-free, no audition, no portfolio requirement, EUR 351.15/semester and nothing else. Its vice is that it does not advance the DJ/producer craft. Best treated as a visa-and-network route into Germany, not as training.

programs.program: Digitale Medien / Digital Media (M.A. at HfK Bremen — media design track; M.Sc. at Universität Bremen — media informatics track). One joint programme, two award routes.
programs.institution: Hochschule für Künste Bremen (University of the Arts Bremen) jointly with Universität Bremen
programs.institutionType: State university of the arts (HfK) jointly with a state research university (Uni Bremen)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC (both partners). The HfK Bremen is a state art college of the Free Hanseatic City of Bremen and the Universität Bremen is a Land university; the HfK programme page lists only a semester contribution of EUR 431.40 and no tuition line.
programs.qualification: Master of Arts (HfK Bremen) or Master of Science (Universität Bremen), 120 ECTS — real, state-recognised second-cycle degrees. The M.Sc. route from Universität Bremen carries full doctoral progression.
programs.accreditationStatus: State programme with a published joint Aufnahmeordnung (admission regulation) for the 'hochschulübergreifender Masterstudiengang Digitale Medien'. Programme accreditation seal/expiry not shown on the pages read — UNVERIFIED; check antrag.akkreditierungsrat.de.
programs.language: ENGLISH. The official HfK page states the language of instruction is English and describes it as an English-language master's degree programme. This is the only fully English-taught record in this sweep.
programs.languageRequirement: English proficiency certificate required: CEFR C1, or TOEFL iBT >= 95, or IELTS Band 7, or Cambridge CAE/CPE, or UNIcert III. Waived only if the qualifying degree or secondary education was taught in English (with proof). NO German certificate is required for admission. For this candidate that means one specific, expensive gate: IELTS 7.0 overall — a high band that he must plan a real preparation year for.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, full-time. Semesters 1-2 introductory and project-preparation courses; semester 3 a full major project; semester 4 the thesis.
programs.focus: Digital media at the intersection of media design (HfK) and media informatics (Uni Bremen) — experimental-artistic and applied engagement with new technologies. Sound/audio is a legitimate project area within the HfK's digital-media practice, but this is NOT a dedicated sound degree: he would have to make sound his own project focus.
programs.whatYouStudy: Openly structured, project-driven: the third semester is given over entirely to one major project of the student's own definition, which is where sound design or electronic-music work would live.
programs.entryRequirements: A bachelor's degree with AT LEAST 150 ECTS in a relevant field — computer science, design, media arts, fine arts, architecture, systems engineering and related. A BSc Software Engineering fits this list cleanly (this is a notably low ECTS bar compared with TH Köln's 210). Documents: 1-page letter of motivation, 1-page CV, English certificate, degree certificate, portfolio. HfK applicants are then invited to an interview (video call or in person) in late June/early July.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition. An interview round applies to HfK (M.A.) applicants after shortlisting.
programs.portfolioSpec: REQUIRED, and the spec differs by route: M.A. (HfK) applicants submit 10-20 works spanning artistic, design, academic or professional projects (PDF, link, or postal); M.Sc. (Uni Bremen) applicants submit a SINGLE video of strictly no more than 5 minutes demonstrating the breadth of their digital-media work. The 5-minute video route is materially easier for someone building a portfolio from zero over one year — this is the single most actionable detail in this record.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES. No music degree, conservatory training or audio experience is required. Software engineering is an explicitly named acceptable background.
programs.equipmentRequired: None stated.
programs.facilities: HfK Bremen digital-media studios and workshops plus Universität Bremen media-informatics labs; the joint 'bremen digitalmedia' infrastructure.
programs.intakes: Winter semester (start 1 October) for all applicants; summer semester (start 1 April) for advanced entrants only.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 April — both the HfK and the Universität Bremen portals open. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.deadline: 31 May (both portals). Then: HfK interview invitations mid-June, interviews late June/early July, results early July, enrolment in October. For a SEPTEMBER/OCTOBER 2027 start he applies 1 April – 31 May 2027. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Note this is a tight visa timeline: an early-July decision leaves roughly three months to obtain a Tunis student visa — he should book the embassy appointment the moment he is offered.
programs.tuitionEU: No tuition fee; semester contribution EUR 431.40.
programs.tuitionNonEU: IDENTICAL — EUR 431.40 per semester, no separate non-EU rate is published. Bremen does not charge non-EU tuition.
programs.otherFees: The EUR 431.40 is the whole published semester cost (it includes the semester ticket). Postal portfolio submission and certified translations of non-German/non-English documents are at his own cost.
programs.totalCostEstimate: About EUR 862.80 per year in semester contributions, plus Bremen living costs (moderate by German standards) and the blocked account required for the visa. Plus the IELTS fee.
programs.scholarships: None programme-specific published. DAAD / Deutschlandstipendium only. UNVERIFIED — ask the HfK International Office.
programs.englishTest: IELTS 7.0 / TOEFL iBT 95 / CEFR C1. This is a demanding band — he should sit a diagnostic test early and budget a preparation year. Waiver only if his SMU MedTech degree was taught in English and he can prove it — worth checking, because SMU MedTech teaches substantially in English and a medium-of-instruction letter could remove this gate entirely.
programs.visaEligible: YES. Full-time state degree at two state institutions.
programs.recommendation: BEST OVERALL FIT of this sweep for him after Ilmenau, and arguably ahead of it on accessibility: English-taught (no German needed), 150 ECTS entry bar his BSc meets, EUR 431.40 a semester and nothing more, software engineering explicitly welcome, and the M.Sc. route only asks for a 5-minute video portfolio — exactly what a year of building work can produce. Two action items now: (1) request a medium-of-instruction letter from SMU MedTech to try to waive IELTS 7; (2) start assembling the 5-minute video around sound/music-technology projects so the portfolio and the career goal point the same way. Second official source for the application detail: https://digitalmedia-bremen.de/profile/master/application-and-requirements/

programs.program: Sound Art (Master of Music)
programs.institution: Hochschule für Musik und Theater München (HMTM — University of Music and Performing Arts Munich)
programs.institutionType: Staatliche Hochschule für Musik (state university of music), Free State of Bavaria
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. HMTM is a Bavarian state university of music, governed under the Bayerisches Hochschulinnovationsgesetz; its own programme page states that only semester fees apply, with no tuition.
programs.qualification: Master of Music (M.Mus.), 120 ECTS — a real, state-recognised second-cycle degree from a state art university. The programme page states it is accredited through 30 September 2031, which is the cleanest accreditation evidence of any record in this sweep.
programs.accreditationStatus: ACCREDITED until 30.09.2031 (stated on the official programme page). State institution.
programs.language: GERMAN. The official page gives the teaching language as German — and, unusually, states that NO language certificate is required.
programs.languageRequirement: Per the official programme page: German is the language of instruction and no certificate is demanded. That is an extraordinary combination and he must confirm it in writing with the admissions office (Alessandra Wührer, HMTM Zulassung) before relying on it — an aptitude interview conducted in German is a de facto language test even when no certificate is on paper. Report it as published, verify before acting.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS.
programs.focus: Sound art as an intermedial art form: installations, performances and media-based works. Three named strands — (1) acoustic ecology and interspecies performance, (2) sonification and materiality (digital/hybrid structures, reinterpreting everyday phenomena), (3) sound and listening as a political act. Career paths named by the school: independent artistic practice, the media industry, and soundscape design in museum and industrial contexts.
programs.whatYouStudy: Individual artistic concept development at an advanced level under Prof. Dr.-Ing. Till Bovermann (academic director), with the three strands above as the intellectual frame. Note Bovermann is an engineer-artist (SuperCollider/live-coding lineage) — code-literate applicants are not out of place here.
programs.entryRequirements: A first professional higher-education degree, German or foreign, in music, media art, interactive media, ACOUSTICS or a RELATED FIELD, plus a passed Eignungsprüfung (aptitude examination), plus an artistic project proposal submitted with the application. 'Related field' is the door a software engineer walks through — but only carried by the project proposal and the aptitude exam.
programs.auditionSpec: Eignungsprüfung required. Its exact format for Sound Art is not published in English — UNVERIFIED; contact Ruth Vollert (ruth.vollert-horch@hmtm.de, +49 89 289-27474) or the admissions office. Regular online information sessions for the Sound Art master are held (e.g. 16 April and 11 May 2026) and are the cheapest way for him to learn the real bar.
programs.portfolioSpec: An artistic project proposal must be submitted with the application; work samples are assessed at the aptitude stage. Exact specification UNVERIFIED — ask the admissions office. He does not have this today; it is exactly what his portfolio year should be aimed at if he wants this school.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES in principle — 'media art, interactive media, acoustics or a related field' is broader than a music degree, and the DAAD/HMTM entry wording does not require a conservatory background. But the aptitude exam is artistic, and admission without demonstrable sound-art work is not realistic.
programs.equipmentRequired: None stated — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: HMTM studios in Munich; the programme is media/installation-oriented rather than commercial-studio-oriented.
programs.applicationOpens: Via the HMTM application portal (zulassung.hmtm.de). Opening date UNVERIFIED — watch the portal from roughly March.
programs.deadline: 31 May (12:00 noon) — for a winter start. For a SEPTEMBER/OCTOBER 2027 intake: 31 May 2027. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date on hmtm.de.
programs.tuitionEU: No tuition; semester fees only.
programs.tuitionNonEU: IDENTICAL — Bavaria charges no tuition to non-EU nationals at state universities of music. He pays the same semester fee as a German student.
programs.otherFees: Exact semester fee (Studentenwerk contribution + Semesterticket) NOT published on the programme page — UNVERIFIED; ask HMTM Studierendensekretariat. Munich is the most expensive German city for accommodation, which dominates the real cost.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition EUR 0; semester fee UNVERIFIED; Munich living costs are the highest in Germany and will exceed the blocked-account minimum in practice.
programs.scholarships: None programme-specific published — UNVERIFIED. DAAD artistic-scholarship routes (already in the database) are the realistic path for a Tunisian national.
programs.englishTest: None demanded (German-taught, no certificate stated).
programs.visaEligible: YES. Full-time accredited state M.Mus.
programs.recommendation: A genuinely distinctive programme that the earlier sweeps missed, and the accreditation position is the most clearly documented of anything here (valid to 2031). For him it is a PORTFOLIO-GATED aspiration, not a 2027 plan: the entry route runs through an artistic project proposal and an aptitude examination, and he has neither yet. Also be honest about direction — this is installation and research sound art, not club music production; it does not serve the 'international DJ and producer' goal directly. Concrete step at zero cost: attend one of the online information sessions and ask Prof. Bovermann directly whether a software-engineering applicant with one year of self-built sound work has a route. His engineering background is a real asset with this particular professor.

programs.program: Klangkunst-Komposition (Musik – Klangkunst – Komposition), Master of Music
programs.institution: Hochschule für Musik Mainz — a school of the Johannes Gutenberg-Universität Mainz (JGU)
programs.institutionType: School of music integrated into a state research university (unusual in Germany — the HfM Mainz is not a free-standing Musikhochschule but part of JGU)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Johannes Gutenberg-Universität Mainz is a Land Rhineland-Palatinate state university; the HfM Mainz is one of its schools and the degree is issued under JGU's authority.
programs.qualification: Master of Music (M.Mus.), 4 semesters — a real, state-recognised second-cycle degree issued by a state university (with doctoral progression available through JGU). Germany's first sound-art composition master at a music college, running since winter semester 2009/10.
programs.accreditationStatus: State university programme under the Landeshochschulgesetz RLP, with published Eignungsprüfungsordnung and study regulations on download.uni-mainz.de. Programme seal/expiry not stated — UNVERIFIED; check antrag.akkreditierungsrat.de.
programs.language: GERMAN.
programs.languageRequirement: REMARKABLY LOW: the official JGU study-programme record demands only 'Nachweis hinreichender deutscher Sprachkenntnisse (vergleichbar Niveau A1-GERR)' — proof of German comparable to CEFR A1, provable by certificate OR by the interview conducted during the aptitude examination. A1 German is achievable in a few months. This is the lowest published German-language bar of any record in this sweep and makes the programme unusually reachable for a non-German-speaking applicant. Confirm in writing with the HfM Mainz admissions office, since it is atypical.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters (2 years). ECTS figure not stated on the pages read — UNVERIFIED (the Studien-/Prüfungsordnung on download.uni-mainz.de will state it; a German M.Mus. of this length is normally 120 ECTS). Additional published rule: applicants whose bachelor is not yet conferred at the application deadline need at least 135 ECTS.
programs.focus: Sound art composition with an emphasis on spatialising and intermedial compositional strategies, drawing together new music, ELECTRONIC COMPOSITION, sound art, audiovisual art, radiophonic art and Ars Acustica into one thematic unit.
programs.whatYouStudy: Advanced individual artistic-compositional research; collaboration with media and art institutions; spatial/multichannel work. Career destinations named by the school: independent artistic practice, media, radio, and museum sound design.
programs.entryRequirements: THE MOST OPEN DOOR IN THIS SWEEP. Three routes: (1) a bachelor in Music, (2) a bachelor in Art, or (3) — stated explicitly — an applicant who completed a DIFFERENT degree programme may be admitted if a high level of artistic ability is demonstrated in the aptitude examination. Route (3) is precisely his situation: a BSc Software Engineering with no music degree is not automatically excluded.
programs.auditionSpec: Two-stage Eignungsprüfung, and note it is NOT an instrumental audition: (1) pre-selection on submitted materials, after which shortlisted candidates are given a project theme and 6-12 weeks to prepare; (2) an aptitude CONVERSATION of 20-45 minutes in which the candidate presents the prepared project sketch and discusses artistic background, interests and expectations. No instrument, no performance, no conservatory technique is tested. For a candidate with no conservatory training this is a far more winnable format than a classical audition.
programs.portfolioSpec: Application must contain: CV; a written justification of the choice of programme; work samples (Arbeitsproben) relevant to the field; a description of planned artistic projects plus a project sketch in sound-art composition. This is a concrete, writable specification — his portfolio year should be built to produce exactly these four items.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, explicitly — the regulation admits candidates from unrelated degrees on demonstrated artistic aptitude. Combined with the A1 German bar, this is the most permissive formal profile of anything found.
programs.equipmentRequired: None stated — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: HfM Mainz studios; collaboration with media and art institutions in the Rhine-Main area.
programs.intakes: Start semester not stated on the pages read — UNVERIFIED (German M.Mus. programmes with an Eignungsprüfung are usually winter-semester entry).
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED. The school's own guidance says applicants must inform themselves in good time at the admissions office, as procedures and deadlines vary. Ask the HfM Mainz Studienbüro directly — and ask early, because the pre-selection stage plus 6-12 weeks of project preparation means the real timeline starts months before the aptitude conversation.
programs.deadline: NOT PUBLISHED on the programme pages — UNVERIFIED. Ask the Hochschule für Musik Mainz admissions office (musik.uni-mainz.de contact) for the Eignungsprüfung registration deadline for the 2027 intake. Do not assume a July date; music-college aptitude deadlines are typically much earlier (often March-April).
programs.tuitionEU: No tuition fee (Rhineland-Palatinate).
programs.tuitionNonEU: IDENTICAL — no non-EU tuition rate at JGU Mainz.
programs.otherFees: Semester contribution (Studierendenwerk + AStA + semester ticket): amount NOT confirmed on the pages read — UNVERIFIED; ask the JGU Studierendensekretariat. JGU semester contributions include a broad regional semester ticket.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition EUR 0 + semester contribution (UNVERIFIED) + Mainz living costs (moderate; Rhine-Main is cheaper than Frankfurt itself) + blocked account for the visa.
programs.scholarships: None programme-specific published. DAAD artistic-field scholarships (already in the database) are the route for a Tunisian national. A Meisterschülerstudium/Konzertexamen exists as a post-master artistic track at JGU, not a funding source.
programs.englishTest: None — German-taught, and only A1 German demanded.
programs.visaEligible: YES. Full-time state M.Mus. from a state university.
programs.recommendation: The most surprising find of this slice and the one I would tell him to look at hardest among the artistic options. It is the only programme found where (a) an applicant from an unrelated degree is explicitly admissible on artistic aptitude, (b) only A1 German is demanded on paper, (c) the aptitude test is a project conversation rather than an instrumental audition, and (d) the entire cost is a semester contribution. The catch is that it is sound-art COMPOSITION — spatial, intermedial, radiophonic — and not dance-music production; he must want that. Two things to do this year: get the exact Eignungsprüfung deadline and the ECTS/Studienordnung from the Studienbüro, and build a real project sketch, because everything turns on that one document. Second official source: https://www.studium.uni-mainz.de/studienwahl/studienangebot/klangkunst-komposition-mmus/

programs.program: Media Production (M.A.) — berufsbegleitend / part-time
programs.institution: Hochschule Mittweida — University of Applied Sciences, Fakultät Medien (taught at the MediaTechSpace in Leipzig)
programs.city: Leipzig (teaching site); institution seated in Mittweida, Saxony
programs.institutionType: Fachhochschule / University of Applied Sciences (state), Free State of Saxony
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Hochschule Mittweida is a state UAS of the Free State of Saxony under the Sächsisches Hochschulgesetz; the official programme page states there are no tuition fees, which is the state-institution signature.
programs.qualification: Master of Arts (M.A.), 120 ECTS — a real, state-recognised second-cycle degree. BUT see visaEligible: the delivery mode, not the degree, is the problem.
programs.accreditationStatus: State programme; study documents (Studien- und Prüfungsordnungen) are published on me.hs-mittweida.de. Programme seal/expiry UNVERIFIED — check antrag.akkreditierungsrat.de.
programs.language: GERMAN. The official page states lectures and other teaching formats are offered in German.
programs.languageRequirement: Not published on the programme page — UNVERIFIED. A German-taught M.A. at a Saxon UAS normally requires DSH-2 / TestDaF 4x4. Ask the Fakultät Medien.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, PART-TIME alongside employment ('berufsbegleitend'), delivered as online coursework plus regular in-person sessions in Leipzig scheduled at off-peak times. Credit rule: 300 ECTS total are required for the degree — 180 from the bachelor + 90 from the master + 30 from professional practice or a pre-master project.
programs.focus: Media production craft: camera, SOUND (Ton), lighting, directing and editing. The faculty's facilities include sound studios, radio rooms and an acoustics lab. Audio is one component of an audiovisual-production degree, not the whole of it.
programs.whatYouStudy: Practice-heavy production training built on the Faculty of Media's long-standing media-training tradition, combining online modules with block attendance in Leipzig.
programs.entryRequirements: A completed first university degree with at least 180 ECTS, PLUS at least one year of professional experience (which in exceptional cases may be acquired during the programme). Enrolment is guaranteed on submission of the required documents — there is no competitive selection. His BSc meets the 180 ECTS bar; the one year of professional experience is the gate, and he has none in audio or media.
programs.auditionSpec: None.
programs.portfolioSpec: None stated — UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — no music degree required. But professional experience is required, which he lacks.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not stated — UNVERIFIED. A part-time online/block format normally assumes the student has their own working setup.
programs.facilities: MediaTechSpace Leipzig (next to the main railway station); Faculty of Media sound studios, radio rooms, acoustics laboratory, print workshop.
programs.applicationOpens: Via hs.mw/apply. Opening date UNVERIFIED.
programs.deadline: NOT published on the English programme page — UNVERIFIED. Ask the Fakultät Medien student office.
programs.tuitionEU: No tuition fees (stated on the official page) — unusual for a berufsbegleitend master, and worth confirming that no separate Weiterbildungsentgelt applies.
programs.tuitionNonEU: No separate non-EU rate is published; the page states no tuition fees. UNVERIFIED whether any part-time/continuing-education charge applies to external students — ask before assuming EUR 0.
programs.otherFees: Semester contribution amount UNVERIFIED. Travel/accommodation for the Leipzig attendance blocks is on the student.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Nominally very low on tuition, but unusable as a primary migration route — see the visa point.
programs.scholarships: None published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.englishTest: None — German-taught.
programs.visaEligible: DOUBTFUL — TREAT AS NO. This is a part-time, employment-accompanying (berufsbegleitend) programme delivered largely online with block sessions. German student residence permits under §16b AufenthG are built around full-time, in-person degree study; part-time/distance formats are routinely refused or granted only where the applicant already holds another residence title. The official page says nothing about visa sponsorship. He should NOT plan a Tunisian student-visa application around this programme without written confirmation from the Ausländerbehörde Leipzig and the university's international office.
programs.recommendation: Reported mainly as a WARNING record. On paper it looks attractive — public, no tuition, 180-ECTS entry, guaranteed enrolment, real sound training. In practice it fails for him on two independent grounds: it requires a year of professional experience he does not have, and its part-time/berufsbegleitend format is a poor and probably invalid basis for a first German student visa. Do not spend application effort here for September 2027.

programs.accreditationStatus: State art college programme. Programme seal/expiry not published on the pages read — UNVERIFIED; check antrag.akkreditierungsrat.de. Two other HBKsaar masters (Kuratieren/Ausstellungswesen and Museumspädagogik) are listed as SUSPENDED from WS 2026/27, which shows the portfolio is actively changing — re-check that Media Art & Design is still admitting before applying.
programs.language: Not stated on the official programme or master-overview pages — UNVERIFIED. HBKsaar teaches predominantly in GERMAN; the International Office page for this subject is written in English but describes the undergraduate course. Ask the International Office (Sabine Rauber, s.rauber@hbksaar.de, +49 681 92652-115) or mad@hbksaar.de which language the master is actually delivered in, and what certificate is demanded.
programs.languageRequirement: UNVERIFIED — not published. Ask s.rauber@hbksaar.de. Assume German at DSH/TestDaF level until told otherwise.
