UNVERIFIED; ask mad@hbksaar.de.
programs.auditionSpec: None (art college; selection is by portfolio/artistic aptitude rather than audition). Exact procedure UNVERIFIED.
programs.portfolioSpec: NOT PUBLISHED on the official pages — UNVERIFIED. An artistic portfolio will certainly be required at a Kunsthochschule; ask mad@hbksaar.de for the specification before building work to the wrong brief.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES for the music point (no music degree needed), but the 240-ECTS rule is a harder obstacle than the artistic one.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not stated — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Media project spaces with current hardware/software; wood, printing, CNC and 3D-printing and metal workshops.
programs.applicationOpens: Not published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.deadline: NOT PUBLISHED on the official master pages — UNVERIFIED. Ask the International Office. German art colleges typically close portfolio applications in spring for a winter start.
programs.tuitionEU: No tuition fee published (Saarland state institution) — UNVERIFIED as an explicit statement.
programs.tuitionNonEU: No separate non-EU rate published — UNVERIFIED. Saarland does not levy non-EU tuition at state institutions, but get this in writing from the International Office rather than assuming.
programs.otherFees: Semester contribution amount UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED — too many unpublished figures to estimate honestly.
programs.scholarships: None published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.englishTest: UNVERIFIED — depends on the (unpublished) teaching language.
programs.visaEligible: Probably yes for the M.A. itself (full-time state degree), but a 60-ECTS one-year master gives a short residence window, and any preliminary bridging year would need its own residence basis. Confirm with the International Office.
programs.recommendation: Reported for completeness of the Saarland — it is the only sound-touching master I could verify in that state — but it is a THIN record by design: HBKsaar publishes almost nothing about language, deadlines, portfolio or fees for its masters, and that opacity is itself the finding. The 240-ECTS entry rule likely excludes him outright unless the unpublished transition programme is generous. Low priority. If he wants to test it, one email to s.rauber@hbksaar.de asking four questions (language, portfolio spec, deadline, and the terms of the transition programme for a 180-ECTS holder) settles it. programs.program: Medien und Musik (M.A.)

programs.program: Master's degree (kandidat/KA) in Electronic Music and Sound Art — Elektronisk Musik og Lydkunst
programs.institution: SDMK – Syddansk Musikkonservatorium / Danish National Academy of Music
programs.institutionType: Music conservatoire (state art academy under the Ministry of Culture)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. SDMK's own international page states it operates on a 'performance contract and annual report with/to the Danish Ministry of Culture' — i.e. it is a state conservatoire under Kulturministeriet, not a private provider. Danish conservatoires sit outside the university sector but inside the state higher-education system.
programs.accreditationStatus: State conservatoire; degrees issued under Danish Ministry of Culture regulation (Bekendtgørelse om uddannelserne ved de videregående kunstneriske uddannelsesinstitutioner). SDMK's own site describes the Danish conservatoire ladder as '3-year bachelor's degree, a 2-year master's degree and an additional 2-year soloist program'.
programs.qualification: Real second-cycle degree. 2-year kandidat (Master of Music) awarded by a state conservatoire. Not a private 'master' certificate.
programs.language: DANISH. SDMK's official language-requirements page states verbatim: 'Group teaching is in Danish.' and 'Solo lessons can be conducted in English upon agreement between student and teacher.' There is NO English-taught version of this master (only the Nordic Master in Folk Music is taught primarily in English).
programs.languageRequirement: No IELTS/TOEFL or Danish test threshold is published on the language-requirements page. It only says: 'Foreign students are warmly encouraged to follow language classes in order to learn Danish as quickly as possible after arriving in Denmark.' UNVERIFIED — ask admissions (Lene Kielsen, lki@sdmk.dk, +45 63119915) whether a Danish certificate is demanded of a non-EU applicant, because the residence-permit rules and the Danish-language group teaching pull in different directions.
programs.focus: Electronic music, sound art, electroacoustic composition, sound-as-material practice
programs.whatYouStudy: SDMK describes the master as giving 'specialised knowledge, skills and competences to work as an electronic musician, composer or sound artist at the highest artistic level' and developing 'your unique artistic profile'. The underlying discipline covers synthesis, electroacoustics, field recording, sound systems, studio and software work.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years (the Danish conservatoire kandidat = 120 ECTS)
programs.intakes: One intake per year, studies start in August
programs.applicationOpens: 15 October (per SDMK's official 'Apply!' page)
programs.deadline: 1 December at 12:00 noon, for both bachelor and master programmes. Entrance exams for Esbjerg specialisations fall in weeks 1–2 (4–15 January). Dates quoted are the 2026–2027 exam calendar published by SDMK — for a September 2027 start, PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.entryRequirements: Official EMOL-KA page: 'A bachelor degree in electronic music from SDMK or an equivalent Danish or foreign music academy' OR 'A bachelor degree (in music) or equivalent from a institution of higher education.' Note the parenthesis — the second limb is ambiguous and is the only crack a non-music BSc could get through. SDMK's FAQ states more bluntly: 'You will only be accepted to the master study if you have a bachelor degree in music', with a recommendation test arranged. Treat a Software Engineering BSc as almost certainly insufficient without a written derogation.
programs.portfolioSpec: 'one or more artistic works of a duration of no more than around 25 minutes', submitted as audio files or a multimedia presentation, all self-created with any collaborators clearly declared; plus a written statement of no more than 2 A4 pages covering concept, potential, planned artistic projects, artistic experience and motivation.
programs.auditionSpec: Two-part entrance exam: (1) a technical presentation of maximum 10 minutes demonstrating your sound-working techniques on your own computer/instrument; (2) a conversation of no more than 10 minutes about artistic ideas, inspiration, target audience and potential.
programs.equipmentRequired: You bring your own computer/instrument to the entrance exam presentation.
programs.facilities: Conservatoire studio facilities at the Esbjerg campus (Kirkegade 61, DK-6700 Esbjerg). Detailed studio inventory not published — UNVERIFIED, ask the programme coordinator.
programs.tuitionEU: Free — EU/EEA/Swiss citizens pay no tuition at Danish conservatoires.
programs.tuitionNonEU: EUR 10,000 per academic year for master programmes (SDMK's own Guide for International Students). Two years = EUR 20,000. SDMK adds: 'all prices listed above are due to yearly change according to indexation', so budget above this for 2027–2029.
programs.otherFees: Application fee DKK 500 for master applicants. (Bachelor students already at SDMK applying to a master with no entrance exam are exempt.)
programs.scholarships: NONE that he could win. SDMK states flatly: 'SDMK - Danish National Academy of Music does not offer any scholarships for foreign students.'
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition EUR 20,000 over two years + DKK 500 application fee. Danish living costs and the immigration self-support requirement are UNVERIFIED here — check SIRI (nyidanmark.dk) for the current documented-means figure per month.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle — a full degree at a state conservatoire under the Ministry of Culture supports a Danish student residence permit, and SDMK's own guide tells non-EU/EEA students they 'need to apply for and obtain the residence permit before coming to Denmark' and to register with the municipality within 5–8 days of arrival.
programs.englishTest: None published for this programme (it is not English-taught).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Effectively no. The FAQ wording ('only be accepted to the master study if you have a bachelor degree in music') is the operative barrier; the 'or equivalent' limb on the EMOL-KA page is untested and would need written confirmation.
programs.recommendation: GENUINE FIND, WRONG FIT FOR HIM. This is the most on-target programme any Nordic sweep has missed — a dedicated electronic music and sound art master at a state conservatoire. But it fails him on three counts simultaneously: (1) group teaching is in Danish; (2) it demands a music bachelor; (3) EUR 10,000/yr with an explicit no-scholarships policy. File it as a target for 2029+ only if he first completes a music bachelor and learns Danish — which is not his plan. Worth one email to lki@sdmk.dk asking whether a non-music BSc plus a strong 25-minute portfolio has ever been admitted, because that answer is genuinely unknown.

programs.program: Sound Design, Master — Master's Degree Programme in Sound Design (Äänisuunnittelu)

programs.focus: Sound design for theatre, performance and live art; sound art
programs.whatYouStudy: Two-year master's studies (120 credits) built around performance production. You work in artistic teams alongside students of lighting design, dramaturgy, directing, choreography, costume design and set design. Three things line up: (1) it does NOT require a music bachelor — any 180 ECTS degree plus English 6 plus the entrance exam; (2) sound art, computer games and interaction design are named parts of its remit, so an electronic-music/game-audio project description belongs there; (3) it runs biennially and skipped autumn 2026, which points at autumn 2027 — his exact target — though KMH has not published that. Two hard cautions. First, KMH tuition is SEK 264,000/yr and the only full funding is roughly THREE institution-wide scholarships awarded AFTER admission in June, which is late for visa sequencing. Second, the entrance exam is artistic and he currently has no portfolio. Concrete action, this month: email international@kmh.se and ask (a) is there admission for autumn 2027, (b) what is the language of instruction, (c) what exactly do the three admission tests consist of. Everything else in his Sweden plan should wait on those three answers.

Second, the programme itself is a conventional composition master requiring ~45 minutes of documented compositional works — unreachable for someone with no portfolio and one year to build one. The University will also consider applications on the basis of experiential learning for those without the normal entry qualifications, with the onus on the applicant to evidence experience equating to honours-level degree study. FOR HIM: option (a)'s 'another relevant discipline' plus option (c)'s open 'other evidence of ability' make this one of the more accessible records here on paper — but see the proposal and interview requirements, which are the real gates.
programs.portfolioSpec: A WRITTEN PROPOSAL is required with the application: 'A written proposal outlining the intended area of individual study (i.e. the Specialism and, ideally, an idea of what the third-semester project might involve) should support the application.' This is a distinctive requirement — it asks for research/practice intent rather than finished work, which suits someone still building a portfolio, but it demands that he can articulate a specific creative-audio project in writing. No formal portfolio of recordings is specified, though supporting evidence of ability is clearly welcome under entry route (c).
programs.auditionSpec: 'ALL APPLICANTS WILL BE INTERVIEWED AND/OR AUDITIONED.' This is unconditional — there is no route into this programme that avoids a live assessment. Plan for it.
programs.tuitionEU: UNVERIFIED for 2027/28. Ulster charges EU students (except Republic of Ireland nationals living in NI, GB or ROI) at the INTERNATIONAL rate post-Brexit. The 2026/27 international rate is published on Ulster's International and EU (excluding ROI) tuition-fees page, which did not render a figure on inspection.
programs.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED. The course page states plainly: '2027/28 Fees: Postgraduate fees are subject to annual review, 2027/28 fees will be announced in due course.' The 2026/27 international rate is published at ulster.ac.uk/student/fees/tuition-fees/international, which did not render a usable figure when fetched. ASK: the Ulster fees team via ulster.ac.uk/student/fees/tuition-fees/contact-us, or the International Portal, for the current postgraduate-taught international rate and for the 2027/28 figure when announced. A missing figure here is a real gap — do not let him plan around an assumed number.
programs.otherFees: Not itemised — UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Cannot be estimated honestly: the 2027/28 international tuition figure is not published and the 2026/27 figure did not render. Derry~Londonderry is among the least expensive places to live in the UK, which is a genuine advantage, but the tuition unknown dominates. Get the fee in writing before this goes on any shortlist.
programs.scholarships: VERIFIED NEGATIVE, and stated bluntly on the course page under 'Scholarships, awards and prizes': 'None.' That is the programme's own words. The Student Finance NI £10,000 tuition-fee loan is restricted to NI/ROI-domiciled students and is NOT available to him; the GB funding bodies likewise. Ulster maintains a general scholarships page (ulster.ac.uk/scholarships) — contents UNVERIFIED, but the course-level statement is unambiguous. Chevening (already in the database) is the only realistic full-funding route to this one.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle — Ulster operates a dedicated International Portal for applicants from outside the UK and Ireland, and the course page cites Tier 4/Student-route English-language equivalences. Confirm on the UKVI Register of Licensed Sponsors.
programs.facilities: Magee campus, Derry~Londonderry, with a published 360° virtual campus tour. A specific studio/equipment inventory is NOT published on the course page — UNVERIFIED. Ulster has invested heavily in screen and creative-industries infrastructure regionally (Studio Ulster), but its relationship to this programme is not stated. Request a facilities list before applying.
programs.equipmentRequired: None stated. Note the programme expects 'relevant instrumental/vocal tuition' alongside the one contact day per week, which implies an instrument or voice as a practice base — worth clarifying whether production/DJ practice satisfies this for the Composition and Creative Audio pathway.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes on the published wording — 'music OR ANOTHER RELEVANT DISCIPLINE', plus an explicit 'other evidence of ability and experience' route and a formal experiential-learning route. But every applicant is interviewed and/or auditioned, so the openness on paper is converted into a live test in practice.
programs.recommendation: Attractive in three specific ways: the lowest English bar (IELTS 6.0, 5.5 floor), an entry route that explicitly accepts 'another relevant discipline' or evidence of ability, and a September 2027 start already published on a dedicated 2027/28 page. The light one-day-a-week contact pattern would leave him real time to produce. Against it: the programme states it has NO scholarships at all, the 2027/28 international fee is unpublished, the facilities are undocumented, and every applicant faces an interview/audition. Action: email Ulster now for (a) the postgraduate international fee, (b) a studio facilities list, and (c) what form the interview/audition takes for the Composition and Creative Audio pathway. If the fee comes back competitive with Bucks New or USW, this becomes a serious contender; if it comes back near Queen's £23,000, drop it.

programs.program: Elektronika, studia II stopnia — specjalność Akustyka (EAK)
programs.institution: Politechnika Wrocławska / Wrocław University of Science and Technology, Wydział Elektroniki, Fotoniki i Mikrosystemów (W12), Katedra Akustyki, Multimediów i Przetwarzania Sygnałów
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. State-funded public technical university (uczelnia publiczna) supervised by the Polish Ministry of Science and Higher Education; fee ordinances are issued by the Rector and published in the university's BIP (Biuletyn Informacji Publicznej), which is a legal obligation only for public bodies. Polish-taught studies are free for Polish/EU students, which is the defining marker of a public HEI in Poland.
programs.language: Polish. Only one specialization of the second-cycle Elektronika degree ('Advanced Applied Electronics') is taught in English; the Akustyka specialization is Polish-only.
programs.languageRequirement: Polish at B2, evidenced by a certificate from the State Certification Commission (PKPZJPO), a Polish-medium school leaving certificate, or completion of a 9+ month preparatory course. EU citizens without a certificate may sit PWr's online Polish test; non-EU applicants are directed to the certificate route. (If he ever switched to the English specialization, PWr accepts IELTS 5.5 / TOEFL iBT 72 / FCE — a notably low English bar.)
programs.qualification: magister inżynier (Master of Engineering) — a genuine state-recognised second-cycle degree under the Polish Law on Higher Education and Science (Prawo o szkolnictwie wyższym i nauce).
programs.accreditationStatus: Fully accredited public university degree; PWr is in the national register of HEIs (POL-on). The magister inżynier award supports a student residence permit (karta pobytu na studia) for a non-EU national.
programs.durationEcts: 3 semesters (1.5 years), full-time (stacjonarne), ogólnoakademicki profile. ECTS total not stated on the faculty page — a 3-semester Polish second-cycle engineering degree is normally 90 ECTS. UNVERIFIED: confirm with Dziekanat W12.
programs.focus: Technical/engineering acoustics with a substantial sound-engineering component — NOT a music production or DJ programme.
programs.whatYouStudy: Physical acoustics, digital sound, loudspeaker devices and electroacoustic transducers, noise and vibration, environmental acoustics prediction and acoustic mapping, analysis and processing of acoustic signals, computer modelling in acoustics, ultrasound in industry and medicine, bio- and hydroacoustics, acoustic diagnostics, and sound engineering (inżynieria dźwięku). Diploma seminar plus master's thesis.
programs.entryRequirements: A completed first-cycle degree. PWr's second-level admission criteria are grade-based (average from the prior degree plus subject-compatibility assessment); an engineering (inżynier) background in electronics/electrical/IT is the expected feed. A BSc in Software Engineering is a plausible but non-standard feed — PWr may impose 'różnice programowe' (bridging modules) or refuse. UNVERIFIED whether a foreign BSc Software Engineering is accepted onto the Akustyka specialization: ask rekrutacja@pwr.edu.pl and the W12 Dziekanat directly, quoting the specialization code EAK.
programs.portfolioSpec: None. This is a technical degree — no portfolio, no artistic dossier. This is the single biggest advantage of the technical-faculty route for this candidate.
programs.auditionSpec: None. No audition, no musical performance test.
programs.equipmentRequired: None specified for admission. Department runs anechoic and reverberation chambers and acoustic measurement labs (Katedra Akustyki, Multimediów i Przetwarzania Sygnałów).
programs.facilities: Department of Acoustics, Multimedia and Signal Processing laboratories; measurement acoustics rather than music studios. There is no commercial-standard music recording studio advertised on the department teaching pages. UNVERIFIED: ask the department whether students get studio/DAW access.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly a non-music, engineering-faculty programme. No musical training is required or assessed. This is the correct family of programme for a software-engineering graduate.
programs.englishTest: None required for the Polish-taught Akustyka specialization. (IELTS 5.5 / TOEFL iBT 72 only apply if he applied to PWr's English-taught specialization instead.)
programs.tuitionEU: 0 PLN per semester for Polish and EU/EEA citizens on Polish-taught full-time studies.
programs.tuitionNonEU: 7,050 PLN per semester (~1,500 EUR/semester, ~3,000 EUR/year) for a non-EU foreigner studying full-time IN POLISH at PWr. This is the rate a Tunisian national pays — Polish-taught study at a Polish public university is NOT free for non-EU nationals unless they hold a Karta Polaka, a NAWA scholarship, a permanent residence/long-term-EU-resident permit, or refugee status. Figure published on PWr's own recruitment site for foreigners; PWr states the amount is fixed for the whole period of study. PRIOR CYCLE (published for 2024/2025 entrants) - confirm new rate; the governing act is Zarządzenie Wewnętrzne Rektora nr 72/2026 of 29 May 2026 on fees for foreigners, available via bip.pwr.edu.pl.
programs.otherFees: Application fee 85 PLN (20 EUR). Living costs Wrocław ~2,500-3,500 PLN/month.
programs.totalCostEstimate: ~21,150 PLN tuition for the full 3-semester degree (~4,500 EUR) plus ~18 months living costs at ~30,000-42,000 PLN/year. Total realistic ~14,000-17,000 EUR for the whole degree.
programs.scholarships: No PWr-specific full scholarship for non-EU degree students found on the recruitment pages. The realistic full-funding vehicle for a Tunisian applying to a Polish public university is the NAWA scholarship system (already in the database as a funding vehicle) — a NAWA award also waives the tuition. UNVERIFIED whether PWr grants its own fee waivers: ask rekrutacja@pwr.edu.pl.
programs.intakes: Two intakes: October (winter) and February (summer). Second-cycle Elektronika second-cycle admission runs in both.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 June for the October intake; registration for the February intake opens in autumn.
programs.deadline: October 2026 intake: applications closed 21 July 2026. February 2027 intake: Admission round 1 closes 13 November 2026, round 2 closes 5 February 2027. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For his SEPTEMBER 2027 target he needs the October 2027 intake, deadline expected around 20 July 2027 — note this is LATER than most of his other targets and does not fit the 'Oct 2026-Feb 2027' window he assumed. The February 2027 intake (deadline 5 Feb 2027) is the one that matches his stated call window, but it would start him in Feb 2027, not Sept 2027.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — full-time degree study at an accredited Polish public HEI supports a Polish national student visa (D-type) and subsequent temporary residence permit for studies.
programs.recommendation: STRONG TECHNICAL FIT, HARD LANGUAGE BLOCKER. This is the best structural match in Poland for his actual background: an engineering master's in acoustics and sound engineering that asks for zero musical training and zero portfolio, at 3,000 EUR/year. The killer is Polish at B2 with a state certificate — that is roughly two years of full-time language study, not one. Realistic play: apply to the English-taught 'Advanced Applied Electronics' specialization instead (IELTS 5.5 is achievable for him within months) and take acoustics electives, OR spend 2026/27 on a Polish preparatory year (NAWA funds these) and enter Akustyka in Oct 2028. Do NOT count on Sept 2027 for this one.

programs.program: Muzyka w mediach i produkcja muzyczna, studia stacjonarne drugiego stopnia — specjalność Realizacja dźwięku (Sound Realization)
programs.institution: Akademia Muzyczna im. Grażyny i Kiejstuta Bacewiczów w Łodzi, Wydział Twórczości, Interpretacji, Edukacji i Produkcji Muzycznej
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. A state art academy (publiczna uczelnia artystyczna) supervised by the Polish Ministry of Culture and National Heritage — the same ministry line that runs the Chopin University and the Łódź Film School. Evidenced by Rector's decisions on foreigner fees published as official acts on the academy's own domain, and by the ministry-set free-tuition rule for Polish citizens.
programs.language: Polish. All teaching, the entrance examination and the oral specialist examination are in Polish. No English-taught track exists for this specialization.
programs.languageRequirement: Polish sufficient to sit an oral examination on electroacoustics, studio technique, microphone technique and timbral solfège, plus a qualification interview. Formally the academy applies the standard Polish rule (B2 certificate or equivalent for non-EU applicants). UNVERIFIED which certificates are accepted — ask kancelaria@amuz.lodz.pl.
programs.qualification: magister sztuki (Master of Arts) — a real, state-recognised second-cycle degree in the Polish system.
programs.accreditationStatus: Fully accredited public art academy in the POL-on register; degree supports a non-EU student residence permit.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, 4 semesters, full-time (stacjonarne). ECTS not published on the admissions page; Polish 4-semester second-cycle art degrees are 120 ECTS. UNVERIFIED - confirm with the Dział Nauczania.
programs.focus: Sound recording and sound realization across classical, popular/entertainment and electroacoustic music, plus sound for audiovisual forms and live broadcast realization. This is the closest thing in the list to actual music production.
programs.whatYouStudy: Deepened sound realization in classical, entertainment (rozrywkowa) and electroacoustic music; operating sound in audiovisual forms; realization of live programmes; studio technique, microphone methods, electroacoustics, timbral solfège (solfeż barwy), specialist English.
programs.entryRequirements: A completed first-cycle degree, PLUS a positive audiometric (hearing) test result, PLUS the three-part entrance examination below. In practice the oral examination presupposes a first-cycle sound-engineering education — the syllabus is explicitly 'selected topics from specialist subjects'.
programs.portfolioSpec: MANDATORY AND HEAVY. The candidate must submit THREE of his own recordings with different instrumentation (scores optional). One of the three may be substituted by a film soundtrack excerpt, a radio-drama fragment, or a sound scene on a self-chosen topic. These must be his own engineering work, not DJ mixes.
programs.auditionSpec: Three-stage: (1) presentation and defence of the three original recordings; (2) oral examination covering electroacoustics, studio technique, microphone methods, timbral solfège and specialist English, including identifying recording errors and assessing audio quality by ear; (3) qualification interview on motivation, career objectives and intended specialization. Trained-ear tasks (error detection, quality assessment) are the hardest element for a self-taught applicant.
programs.equipmentRequired: He must be able to produce three properly engineered multi-instrument recordings — so realistically access to a recording space, microphones and a DAW during the portfolio-building year. A laptop and headphones are not enough for the acoustic-instrument recordings this exam expects.
programs.facilities: Academy recording studios and concert halls; teaching cooperation with the academy's own production infrastructure. UNVERIFIED specifics — ask the Wydział office.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: FORMALLY YES (any first-cycle degree is eligible), PRACTICALLY NO. The oral examination is pitched at graduates of a first-cycle realizacja dźwięku programme. A BSc Software Engineering with no conservatory training and no recording experience would almost certainly fail the timbral solfège and error-detection components. This programme is designed as the continuation of the academy's own bachelor's.
programs.englishTest: None required — English is examined only as 'specialist English' inside the Polish-language oral exam.
programs.tuitionEU: 0 PLN for Polish and EU/EEA citizens on full-time studies (state art academy).
programs.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED as an exact figure. The academy publishes annual Rector's decisions 'w sprawie ponoszenia odpłatności za studia przez cudzoziemców' for 2021/22 through 2026/27 as PDFs on its official fees page, but the amounts are inside the PDFs and are not rendered on the page. Secondary summaries indicate a floor of about 4,000 EUR per year with an additional 200 EUR one-off entry fee and a 30% reduction for persons of Polish descent — TREAT AS UNCONFIRMED. Download the current decision from https://www.amuz.lodz.pl/index.php/pl/dla-studenta/oplaty-za-studia or e-mail kancelaria@amuz.lodz.pl / +48 42 662 16 00 and ask for the decyzja Rektora for 2027/2028 specifically for studia II stopnia, kierunek Muzyka w mediach i produkcja muzyczna.
programs.otherFees: Application/entry fee for foreigners UNVERIFIED (reported ~200 EUR in the first year). Łódź living costs are among the lowest of Poland's big cities, ~2,000-3,000 PLN/month.
programs.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED pending the fee decision. If the ~4,000 EUR/year figure holds, ~8,000 EUR tuition plus ~10,000-14,000 EUR living for the two years.
programs.scholarships: No academy-specific full scholarship for non-EU degree students identified. NAWA (already in the database) is the realistic full-funding route and covers art academies.
programs.intakes: September/October (single annual intake). Entrance examinations are held in the summer.
programs.applicationOpens: Spring; the academy publishes a 'REKRUTACJA — EGZAMINY WSTĘPNE' schedule each year.
programs.deadline: The 2026/2027 examination schedule is published on the academy's recruitment page. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for 2027/2028; expect application spring 2027 with exams in June/July 2027, which is LATER than the Oct 2026-Feb 2027 window he assumed.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — accredited public art academy, second-cycle degree, supports a Polish student visa and residence permit.
programs.recommendation: GENUINE GAP FIND — this is a real sound-production master's at a public Polish music academy that earlier sweeps missed — BUT it is the wrong door for him. The entrance examination assumes a completed first-cycle sound-engineering education (timbral solfège, aural error detection, microphone methods) and is conducted in Polish. Even a strong portfolio year will not close a trained-ear gap. Flag it for the record and as a possible target for 2029+ if he ever completes a first-cycle audio qualification; do not build the 2027 plan around it. The one concrete action worth taking now is to e-mail for the foreigner fee decision, because that number is missing from the database and applies to any Polish public art academy he considers.

programs.program: Teorie a praxe audiovizuální tvorby (N0211P310005), navazující magisterský program — specializace Zvuková skladba (Sound Design)
programs.institution: Univerzita Tomáše Bati ve Zlíně / Tomas Bata University in Zlín, Fakulta multimediálních komunikací (FMK), Ateliér Audiovizuální tvorba
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. UTB states on its own FAQ: 'Jsme veřejná vysoká škola, a proto se u nás školné neplatí' (We are a public higher education institution, and therefore no tuition is charged here). A veřejná vysoká škola is established by act of the Czech Parliament under Act No. 111/1998 Sb.
programs.language: Czech. UTB's admissions office confirms international applicants sit the entrance examination in Czech and therefore do not need a separate B2 certificate — the exam itself is the language screen. No English-taught version of this specialization is offered.
programs.languageRequirement: No formal certificate demanded. Instead the applicant must be able to sit a Czech-language talent examination and defend creative work in Czech. In practice this is a higher bar than a certificate, not a lower one.
programs.qualification: MgA. (Magistr umění) — a real, state-recognised second-cycle degree, accredited by the Czech National Accreditation Bureau (NAÚ) under programme code N0211P310005.
programs.accreditationStatus: Nationally accredited (programme code N0211P310005 in the Czech register of accredited study programmes). Fully supports a long-term residence permit for the purpose of studies for a non-EU national.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters (2 years), full-time (prezenční), 120 ECTS.
programs.focus: Sound design for audiovisual work — film, television and advertising production and post-production — inside a film-school studio structure, not a music-technology department.
programs.whatYouStudy: Sound within the Audiovisual Arts studio: recording, sound dramaturgy, post-production and mixing for film/TV/advertising, taught alongside camera, directing and screenwriting, editing and production specializations so students work on shared crewed productions. Master level offers five specializations (Camera, Production, Direction and Screenwriting, Film Editing, Sound Design) — note Visual Effects exists at bachelor level but is NOT continued at master level.
programs.entryRequirements: A completed bachelor's degree, plus a talent-based entrance examination. Only ONE application per applicant is permitted across the six/five specializations — he cannot hedge by applying to Sound Design and Editing simultaneously. Recognition of the foreign bachelor's degree is required. About 25 students are admitted across ALL specializations of the programme, so Sound Design places are in single figures.
programs.portfolioSpec: Required (talentová zkouška). The specific portfolio list is set annually in the faculty's admissions directive (směrnice k přijímacímu řízení, e.g. SD/07/2026) rather than on the public programme page. UNVERIFIED in detail — download the current směrnice from https://fmk.utb.cz/studium/prijimaci-rizeni/smernice-k-prijimacimu-rizeni/ or e-mail studium@fmk.utb.cz for the Zvuková skladba requirements specifically.
programs.auditionSpec: Talent examination on a single announced date (10 June for the 2026/2027 cycle). Bachelor admission runs in two rounds (talent test then a second stage); master admission is a single examination. Format for Sound Design UNVERIFIED — ask studium@fmk.utb.cz.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED for admission. The studio teaches on professional film-sound workflows; students are expected to arrive with demonstrable sound work.
programs.facilities: Ateliér Audiovizuální tvorba, building U4 on the UTB campus — a full film-school studio complex shared with camera, editing and VFX specializations, giving access to crewed film productions. This is the practical draw: sound students work on real films rather than isolated exercises.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES in principle — the feeder is a film/audiovisual bachelor, not a music conservatory, and no musical performance ability is assessed. But it is a TALENT-BASED art school: a software-engineering bachelor with a strong sound-for-picture portfolio is a coherent applicant; one without a portfolio is not.
programs.englishTest: None. English is irrelevant to this programme; Czech is the operative language.
programs.tuitionEU: 0 CZK. Czech-language study at a Czech public university is free of charge.
programs.tuitionNonEU: 0 CZK — THE SAME AS FOR CZECHS. Under the Czech Higher Education Act, tuition-free status at a public university attaches to the LANGUAGE OF INSTRUCTION, not to nationality: any student, including a Tunisian national, studies free in a Czech-taught programme. UTB confirms fees arise only 'pokud student studuje program, který je veden v jiném jazyce než v češtině' (if the programme is delivered in a language other than Czech). This is the single most important funding fact in this slice.
programs.otherFees: Application fee 990 CZK per application, non-refundable at any stage. Living costs in Zlín are low by Czech standards, roughly 12,000-18,000 CZK/month.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition 0. Realistic total ~300,000-430,000 CZK (~12,000-17,500 EUR) for two years, essentially all living costs. Plus a Czech-language preparatory year if needed (paid, typically 100,000-160,000 CZK).
programs.scholarships: No programme-specific scholarship for non-EU degree students identified. Czech public universities offer merit and accommodation scholarships to enrolled students. UNVERIFIED whether UTB has an entry scholarship for internationals — ask studium@fmk.utb.cz.
programs.fundingLevel: Full (tuition), None (living costs) — the degree itself costs nothing, but he must self-fund living.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 January (e-application at www.eprihlaska.utb.cz).
programs.deadline: Master's applications 1 January - 30 April 2026, entrance examination 10 June 2026. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For a SEPTEMBER 2027 start expect applications 1 Jan - 30 Apr 2027 with the exam in June 2027. NOTE: this is well AFTER his assumed Oct 2026-Feb 2027 window, so he has more runway than he thinks — but also note the bachelor deadline for 2027/2028 is 30 November 2026, so the faculty's calendars differ sharply by level.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — accredited public university, full-time MgA. programme, supports a Czech long-term residence permit for study purposes.
programs.recommendation: THE BEST-VALUE ARTISTIC OPTION FOUND IN THIS SLICE, AND THE HARDEST TO ENTER. Zero tuition for a Tunisian national, a real film-school studio environment, and no music-conservatory gatekeeping. The two obstacles are Czech language (needed to sit the talent exam) and a portfolio strong enough to win one of only a handful of Sound Design places out of ~25 across all specializations. Concrete next step: e-mail studium@fmk.utb.cz now asking (a) for the Zvuková skladba section of the current admissions směrnice, and (b) whether the master's talent exam can be sat in English for an international applicant — some Czech art faculties permit this and it would change the whole calculus. If Czech is immovable, this is a 2028/2029 target, not 2027.

programs.program: Elektronika a komunikace, navazující magisterský program — specializace Audiovizuální technika a zpracování signálů (Audiovisual Technology and Signal Processing)
programs.institution: České vysoké učení technické v Praze (ČVUT) / Czech Technical University in Prague, Fakulta elektrotechnická (FEL / FEE)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. ČVUT is a veřejná vysoká škola established under Act No. 111/1998 Sb.; its admission conditions are issued as a dean's decree (příkaz děkana FEL_PD_2025_05_V01) explicitly governed by that Act and the CTU Statute.
programs.language: TWO PARALLEL TRACKS — this is the key finding. The specialization exists in a CZECH-TAUGHT version (free of charge) and the Electronics and Communications master's is ALSO delivered in ENGLISH (fee-paying), with the faculty's English programme page confirming the audiovisual technology and signal processing content among its seven specializations. Confirm before applying which track carries the Audiovisual Technology specialization in the target year.
programs.languageRequirement: For the English track: proof of English knowledge, assessed by the admissions committee, with a certificate required if the applicant is not a native speaker — NO named IELTS/TOEFL band is set in the dean's decree, the committee judges it. That is unusually flexible and matters for an applicant who has not yet sat a test. For the Czech track: Czech, entrance examination in Czech.
programs.qualification: Ing. (inženýr) — a real, state-recognised second-cycle engineering degree.
programs.accreditationStatus: Nationally accredited public university programme (NAÚ). Supports a Czech long-term residence permit for study.
programs.durationEcts: 120 credits (ECTS) minimum to complete; standard 2 years / 4 semesters, full-time. The study plan is 'Elektronika a komunikace — Audiovizuální technika a zpracování signálů'.
programs.focus: Engineering of audiovisual signals — acoustics, sound and image technology, signal processing — with the human perceiver as the organising principle. NOT a creative sound-design or music-production degree.
programs.whatYouStudy: Sensing, processing and reproduction of audiovisual signals; practical acoustic design and measurement; image and sound technology; modern methods of processing, compression and reconstruction of image, sound and other signals; explicit orientation toward 'the human as recipient of audiovisual information'. Graduates go into television and radio operations, audiovisual and acoustics design, automotive, and biomedical applications. Specialization guarantor: prof. Petr Páta (pata@fel.cvut.cz).
programs.entryRequirements: A completed bachelor's degree, evidenced before enrolment. Entrance examination consists of an ONLINE INTERVIEW plus an optional test if the admissions committee decides to set one — for the English track. Documents required: transcript of results, English certificate (if not a native speaker), and a MOTIVATION LETTER. Documents not in Czech, Slovak or English need a certified translation. Nostrification (recognition) of the foreign higher-education qualification must be completed by the end of October of the first semester — the application itself does not require it up front, which materially lowers the barrier at application time.
programs.portfolioSpec: NONE. No portfolio, no creative dossier, no artistic assessment. Applicants are merely 'recommended' to submit evidence of significant personal achievements or professional/academic excellence in electrical engineering, informatics, mathematics or physics — which a software-engineering graduate can supply directly from his degree and projects.
programs.auditionSpec: None. There is no audition and no musical assessment of any kind.
programs.equipmentRequired: None.
programs.facilities: FEL acoustics and audiovisual-technology laboratories at ČVUT Prague; measurement and signal-processing infrastructure rather than creative studios.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — EMPHATICALLY. This is an electrical-engineering faculty programme that actively prefers applicants from electronics, informatics, mathematics or physics. A BSc in Software Engineering is a normal, expected feeder profile. Of every programme in this slice, this is the one where his existing degree is an asset rather than a liability.
programs.englishTest: No fixed band. The dean's decree requires 'a certificate of English proficiency if the applicant is not a native speaker', with the admissions committee assessing the level — no IELTS/TOEFL minimum is published. He should still sit IELTS Academic (target 6.5) to be safe, but the absence of a hard threshold means a modest score is unlikely to be an automatic bar. UNVERIFIED which certificates the committee accepts — ask the FEL admissions office.
programs.tuitionEU: 0 CZK for the Czech-taught track (all nationalities). For the English-taught track, EU citizens pay the same fee as everyone else.
programs.tuitionNonEU: CZECH-TAUGHT TRACK: 0 CZK for a Tunisian national — CTU FEE states plainly that students in Czech-language programmes 'do not incur these costs, regardless of citizenship'. ENGLISH-TAUGHT TRACK: fee-paying — 'All students enrolled in programs taught in English are supposed to pay tuition fees', with the amount depending on the level of study and the faculty reserving the right to adjust it each semester. THE EXACT AMOUNT IS NOT PUBLISHED on the faculty's tuition-fees page and I will not guess it: e-mail the FEL admissions office or the programme guarantor prof. Páta (pata@fel.cvut.cz) and ask for the per-semester fee for the English-taught Electronics and Communications master's for 2027/2028. A secondary source quoted 66,000 CZK/semester for CTU English-taught programmes generally — TREAT AS UNCONFIRMED until the faculty states it.
programs.otherFees: Application fee 950 CZK per programme AND per specialization — applying to two specializations costs 1,900 CZK. Payment must be made the same day the application is filed; the application is only entered into the procedure once the fee is paid. Prague living costs ~20,000-28,000 CZK/month, the highest in this slice.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Czech track: ~500,000-670,000 CZK (~20,000-27,000 EUR) for two years, all of it living costs. English track: add the unpublished tuition — if the unconfirmed 66,000 CZK/semester figure is right, that would add ~264,000 CZK (~10,700 EUR) over the degree.
programs.scholarships: The faculty states that high-performing international students may be eligible for scholarships to offset expenses, with details on its scholarship pages — no amounts or eligibility rules published there. UNVERIFIED - ask the FEL international office whether any entry scholarship is open to a first-year non-EU master's student.
programs.intakes: Main intake for the following academic year, plus an EXTRAORDINARY SECOND ROUND (mimořádný termín, 2. kolo) that FEL has run in consecutive years — a genuine second chance, but it requires a brand-new application even if one was already filed that year.
programs.applicationOpens: Autumn preceding the academic year; the dean's decree for 2026/2027 was issued 19 November 2025.
programs.deadline: English-taught programmes: application completed AND fee paid by 31 March 2026. Czech-taught: application by 31 March 2026 with the entrance examination on 5 June 2026; a late window running to 13 August 2026 is referenced for the extraordinary round. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For a SEPTEMBER 2027 start expect a 31 March 2027 deadline — this sits just outside his assumed Oct 2026-Feb 2027 window and is the single most important date to diarise.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — accredited public university, full-time Ing. programme, supports a Czech long-term residence permit for study purposes. Note the nostrification requirement lands AFTER arrival (by end of October of semester one), so he must gather diploma, transcripts and legalisations before leaving Tunisia — the faculty explicitly warns applicants to obtain all documents before travelling to the Czech Republic.
programs.recommendation: TOP PICK OF THIS ENTIRE SLICE FOR THIS CANDIDATE. It is the only programme found where every one of his weaknesses is irrelevant: no portfolio, no audition, no music degree, no conservatory training, no fixed IELTS band, and an admissions process that is an online interview plus a motivation letter. His BSc Software Engineering is the preferred feeder. The Czech-taught version costs a Tunisian national nothing; the English-taught version removes the language barrier at an unpublished but probably manageable cost. It is emphatically NOT a DJ or music-production degree — it is audiovisual signal engineering — but it is a credible, fundable, visa-supporting European master's that puts him inside a Prague audio-engineering ecosystem where he can build the production career on the side. Three actions now: (1) e-mail pata@fel.cvut.cz asking whether Audiovizuální technika a zpracování signálů is available in the English track for 2027/2028; (2) ask FEL admissions for the exact English-track fee; (3) start Czech from zero anyway, because the Czech track is free.

programs.program: Multimediálne inžinierstvo (Multimedia Engineering), inžiniersky (2nd-cycle) study programme
programs.institution: Žilinská univerzita v Žiline / University of Žilina, Fakulta elektrotechniky a informačných technológií (FEIT)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. A verejná vysoká škola under Slovak Act No. 131/2002 Z.z.; the faculty's own admission rules state that students studying in Slovak pay no tuition, which is the statutory public-university regime. Programme is listed in the national register portalvs.sk (Portál vysokých škôl, run by CVTI SR under the Slovak Ministry of Education).
programs.language: Slovak. Teaching, the entrance interview and the state examinations are in Slovak. No English-taught version of Multimediálne inžinierstvo is advertised.
programs.languageRequirement: SLOVAK AT B1 — a certificate is explicitly required of applicants educated abroad (Czech-educated applicants exempted). This is a materially LOWER bar than the B2 Polish demanded by Polish public universities and lower than the de-facto fluency needed for a Czech talent exam. UNIZA also runs its own Slovak preparatory courses, which it points applicants toward.
programs.qualification: Ing. (inžinier) — a real, state-recognised second-cycle degree in the Slovak system.
programs.accreditationStatus: Accredited programme in the Slovak national register of accredited study programmes (portalvs.sk); supports a Slovak temporary residence permit for the purpose of study for a non-EU national.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, full-time (denná forma), 120 ECTS. UNVERIFIED - confirm on the faculty's programme sheet.
programs.focus: Multimedia engineering with a declared audio specialization track — a genuine hybrid of technical and creative training, unusually so for an electrical-engineering faculty.
programs.whatYouStudy: Theoretical foundations of informatics; digital and analogue processing of IMAGE AND SOUND SIGNALS; processing and transmission of multimedia streams over communication technologies, networks and services; interface and application development. Crucially, through the choice of compulsory-elective subjects a student can SPECIALISE NARROWLY IN AUDIO INFORMATION PROCESSING (as opposed to image or graphics). Creatively oriented subjects are built in so graduates can 'create and process multimedia works at an appropriate technical, aesthetic and artistic level'; the faculty names 'audio technician and designer' as a target job.
programs.entryRequirements: A completed first-cycle (bachelor) degree. Foreign graduates need recognition of the equivalence of their qualification from a Slovak institution, or may request UNIZA itself to evaluate it — UNIZA doing the evaluation in-house is a significant convenience versus a separate ministry nostrification. Standard route: Slovak/Czech graduates in the same field with a weighted average up to 2.0-2.5 are admitted WITHOUT an entrance exam; others sit a test on bachelor state-exam topics requiring at least 61%. HOWEVER Multimedia Engineering is different — see audition/portfolio.
programs.portfolioSpec: YES, AND IT IS THE UNUSUAL FEATURE THAT MAKES THIS PROGRAMME INTERESTING FOR HIM. Multimediálne inžinierstvo uses a SELECTIVE INTERVIEW that scores general IT knowledge TOGETHER WITH A CREATIVE PORTFOLIO AND MOTIVATION, up to 70 points combined. So a portfolio helps but is weighed alongside IT knowledge — exactly the blend he will have after a portfolio-building year on top of a software-engineering degree. It is not a conservatory-style talent examination and there is no aural/solfège test. Exact portfolio format UNVERIFIED — request the current 'Zásady a pravidlá prijímacieho konania' for Ing. study from the FEIT study office.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition. An interview only.
programs.equipmentRequired: None specified. He should assemble a portfolio of audio/multimedia work he can demonstrate and discuss.
programs.facilities: FEIT multimedia and audio/video processing laboratories. UNVERIFIED specifics — ask the faculty whether there is studio access.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES. No music degree, conservatory training or performance ability is required or assessed. The interview tests IT knowledge plus creative motivation. His BSc Software Engineering is directly relevant to the informatics half of the assessment.
programs.englishTest: None required. Slovak is the operative language; no IELTS/TOEFL is demanded for a Slovak-taught programme.
programs.tuitionEU: 0 EUR for full-time study in Slovak within the standard length of study.
programs.tuitionNonEU: 0 EUR — THE SAME AS FOR SLOVAKS. FEIT's own admission rules state that international students studying IN SLOVAK pay no tuition, while those studying in another language pay fees set by UNIZA regulations. As in the Czech Republic, the fee attaches to the language of instruction, not to nationality. A Tunisian national on this Slovak-taught Ing. programme pays zero tuition. Foreign scholarship recipients are governed by their sponsorship agreements.
programs.otherFees: Application fee UNVERIFIED (Slovak public universities typically charge 20-40 EUR) — check the e-application portal at https://vzdelavanie.uniza.sk/prijimacky/index.php. Žilina living costs are the lowest in this slice, roughly 450-700 EUR/month.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition 0. Realistic total ~11,000-17,000 EUR for the two years, entirely living costs. Add a Slovak preparatory course if he takes UNIZA's.
programs.scholarships: The Governmental Scholarships of the Slovak Republic (already in the database) is the full-degree funding vehicle for non-EU nationals and would apply here. UNVERIFIED whether UNIZA offers its own entry scholarship — ask the FEIT study office.
programs.fundingLevel: Full (tuition free) — and potentially fully funded if combined with the Slovak Government Scholarship.
programs.applicationOpens: Typically opens in the winter/spring preceding the academic year via the UNIZA e-application portal.
programs.deadline: 30 April 2026 for entry in 2026/2027. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For SEPTEMBER 2027 entry expect a deadline around 30 April 2027 — again later than his assumed Oct 2026-Feb 2027 window. But the Slovak Government Scholarship application, if he pursues it, will close much earlier and drives the real timeline.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — accredited public university, full-time Ing. programme, supports a Slovak temporary residence permit for study. Note the qualification-recognition step must be arranged before enrolment; UNIZA can perform the evaluation itself.
programs.recommendation: THE BEST BALANCED OPTION AND A CLEAR GAP FIND — Slovakia was thinly covered and this programme is the country's most under-recognised audio route. Free tuition for a Tunisian, an admission process that scores a creative portfolio ALONGSIDE IT knowledge rather than instead of it, an explicit audio-processing elective track, no audition, no aural test, no music degree needed, and the lowest living costs of any option here. The only real gate is Slovak at B1 with a certificate — the mildest language requirement in this slice, and genuinely reachable in the twelve months he has before an April 2027 deadline. Actions: (1) enrol in a Slovak course now and target a B1 certificate by early 2027; (2) e-mail the FEIT study office for the current 'Zásady a pravidlá prijímacieho konania' for Ing. study and ask what the creative portfolio must contain for Multimediálne inžinierstvo; (3) run the Slovak Government Scholarship application in parallel. Rank this second only to ČVUT, and first if he is willing to learn a language.

programs.program: Multimediální tvorba (N0211P310001), navazující magisterské studium — including the Ateliér zvuku (Sound Studio) line
programs.institution: Filmová akademie Miroslava Ondříčka v Písku, o.p.s. (FAMO Písek)
programs.publicPrivate: PRIVATE. FAMO states on its own site: 'Jsme soukromá vysoká škola' (We are a private higher education institution). Its legal form is o.p.s. (obecně prospěšná společnost — a public-benefit non-profit company), i.e. a private non-state entity, not a veřejná vysoká škola established by act of Parliament. The 79,000 CZK/year tuition charged to Czech nationals is itself conclusive: a Czech public university cannot charge tuition for Czech-taught study.
programs.language: Czech. The site has an English version but instruction language for non-Czech speakers is not addressed. UNVERIFIED whether any English-medium delivery exists — ask the school directly before assuming.
programs.languageRequirement: UNVERIFIED. No published Czech-language certificate requirement was found. Given a private school's commercial incentive to enrol, this may be softer than at public institutions — but confirm in writing, because being admitted without the language and then failing is the classic trap at fee-charging private art schools.
programs.qualification: MgA. (navazující magisterské studium), programme code N0211P310001 — the 'N' prefix and the code format indicate a programme entered in the Czech national register of accredited study programmes. VERIFY INDEPENDENTLY before paying anything: check the code N0211P310001 in the Czech National Accreditation Bureau (NAÚ) / MŠMT register of accredited programmes rather than relying on the school's own page.
programs.accreditationStatus: REQUIRES INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION — this is exactly the category of institution the brief warns about (a private provider selling a 'Master'). The programme code N0211P310001 is consistent with genuine national accreditation, and the school describes itself as operating within the state education system, but I did not open the MŠMT/NAÚ register entry itself and will not assert it. Look up N0211P310001 at https://regvssp.msmt.cz before any commitment. If accredited, an MgA. from an accredited private Czech HEI does support a long-term residence permit for study.
programs.durationEcts: UNVERIFIED. Czech navazující magisterské programmes are normally 2 years / 120 ECTS. Confirm with the school.
programs.focus: Film-school multimedia production with a dedicated sound studio; small, practice-heavy, industry-taught.
programs.whatYouStudy: At bachelor level the Ateliér zvuku gives comprehensive audio technique and theory on professional equipment including Pro Tools and multi-channel recording. The school emphasises 'propojení s praxí' — working professionals teach alongside academic staff. CRITICAL CAVEAT: the sound studio is described in detail at BACHELOR level; whether a distinct sound specialization continues into the follow-up master's Multimediální tvorba is UNVERIFIED. Ask the school in writing which master-level ateliér a sound applicant would join and who leads it.
programs.entryRequirements: A completed bachelor's degree for the navazující master's. UNVERIFIED in detail — request the current admission conditions (podmínky přijímacího řízení) from the school.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED. A film school will normally require a showreel or sound portfolio, but a fee-charging private school's threshold is typically far lower than FAMU's or UTB's. Ask directly.
programs.auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED — ask the school.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED for admission. Teaching uses Pro Tools and multi-channel recording setups.
programs.facilities: Sound studio with professional audio equipment including Pro Tools and multi-channel recording; a small film school with hands-on production access. The small scale cuts both ways — more individual studio time, far less institutional weight than FAMU.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: LIKELY YES. No music-degree requirement was found, and the feeder is film/multimedia rather than a conservatory. A private school with a 79,000 CZK/year fee has a strong incentive to admit a motivated non-traditional applicant. UNVERIFIED - confirm.
programs.englishTest: UNVERIFIED — probably none for Czech-taught study.
programs.tuitionEU: 79,000 CZK per academic year (~3,200 EUR), full payment required BEFORE the programme starts. Same rate for Czech and EU students.
programs.tuitionNonEU: 79,000 CZK per academic year (~3,200 EUR) — the school publishes a SINGLE rate for bachelor's and master's with no separate non-EU tariff, so on the published information a Tunisian national pays the same 79,000 CZK/year as a Czech. UNVERIFIED whether a foreigner surcharge exists — confirm in writing, and confirm whether the full year must be paid up front before a visa is granted (that sequencing is a real financial risk: paying before a visa decision).
programs.otherFees: Application fee UNVERIFIED. Písek is a small town with low living costs, roughly 12,000-16,000 CZK/month.
programs.totalCostEstimate: ~158,000 CZK tuition for two years (~6,400 EUR) plus ~290,000-380,000 CZK living (~12,000-15,500 EUR). Total roughly 18,000-22,000 EUR — cheap by Western European standards but NOT cheap compared with the free Czech public options above.
programs.scholarships: None identified. Private Czech HEIs rarely fund non-EU degree students, and the Czech government scholarship schemes are generally tied to public institutions. Assume self-pay.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — ask the school.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED - ask the school for the 2027/2028 admission calendar.
programs.visaEligible: PROBABLY, CONDITIONAL ON ACCREDITATION. If N0211P310001 is confirmed in the MŠMT/NAÚ register, study at an accredited private Czech HEI supports a long-term residence permit for study purposes. If it is not registered, it would not, and the fee would be money spent on a non-degree. Verify the register entry FIRST.
programs.recommendation: INCLUDED AS A DELIBERATE COUNTER-EXAMPLE AND A LOW-BAR FALLBACK, NOT A RECOMMENDATION. It is the one genuinely private, fee-charging, low-selectivity sound school found in this slice, and it is precisely the kind of institution the brief asks to be labelled clearly. Its merits are real: Pro Tools-equipped sound studio, industry teachers, small cohorts, and a price (~3,200 EUR/year) that is genuinely low. Its risks are equally real: he would pay ~6,400 EUR in tuition for a degree from a small private school when UTB Zlín and ČVUT offer nationally stronger degrees for FREE, and the master-level sound specialization is unconfirmed. Do not apply until three things are answered in writing: (1) the N0211P310001 entry in the MŠMT register, (2) whether sound is an actual master-level specialization, (3) whether the 79,000 CZK must be paid before or after the visa decision. Treat as a Plan C behind ČVUT and UNIZA.

programs.program: Audiovizuální tvorba a divadlo (Audiovisual Arts and Theatre), navazující magisterské studium
programs.institution: Janáčkova akademie múzických umění v Brně (JAMU) / Janáček Academy of Performing Arts, Divadelní fakulta (Theatre Faculty)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. JAMU is a veřejná vysoká škola (state arts academy) established under Act No. 111/1998 Sb., one of the two Czech performing-arts academies alongside AMU Prague.
programs.language: Czech, confirmed on the faculty's own programme page. No English-taught version of this programme.
programs.languageRequirement: Czech, at a level sufficient to sit the faculty's talent-based admission procedure. No certificate level is stated on the programme page. UNVERIFIED - ask the Divadelní fakulta study office.
programs.qualification: MgA. (Magistr umění) — a real, state-recognised second-cycle degree.
programs.accreditationStatus: Accredited public arts-academy programme; supports a Czech long-term residence permit for study purposes.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, full-time (prezenční), specialisation (non-teaching) track. 120 ECTS assumed; UNVERIFIED - confirm.
programs.focus: Multimedia/new-media theatre practice combining visual art, technology and dramatic thinking — sound is a component of contemporary multimedia theatre work rather than a named specialization.
programs.whatYouStudy: The programme 'connects the environment of theatre, film and new media' and guides students 'towards independent creation combining visual art, technology and dramatic thinking in contemporary multimedia forms'. IMPORTANT NEGATIVE FINDING: sound design is NOT named as a specialization on the official programme page. This is not a sound-design master's, and JAMU's Theatre Faculty does not appear to run a standalone Zvuková tvorba master's despite the widespread assumption that it does — the JAMU-linked audio degree is the Audio Engineering Ing. taught jointly with VUT Brno (already in the database).

programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED but effectively certain — this is an arts-academy talent admission. Request the specific requirements from the faculty.
programs.auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED — an arts talent examination is expected. Request details from the faculty.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: JAMU Theatre Faculty multimedia and stage-technology facilities in Brno. UNVERIFIED whether dedicated audio post facilities are available to this programme.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Formally a theatre/new-media programme rather than a music one, so no conservatory music training is implied — but it is a talent-selected arts degree in Czech, and a software-engineering graduate with no theatre or new-media practice would be a very weak applicant.
programs.englishTest: None — Czech-taught programme.
programs.tuitionEU: 0 CZK for Czech-language study at a public university.
programs.tuitionNonEU: 0 CZK for a Tunisian national in the Czech-taught programme — the Czech tuition-free rule attaches to language of instruction, not nationality, and this programme is Czech-only. Confirm with the faculty that no foreign-language surcharge applies.
programs.otherFees: Application fee UNVERIFIED (Czech arts academies typically charge 600-1,000 CZK). Brno living costs ~16,000-22,000 CZK/month.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition 0; roughly 380,000-530,000 CZK (~15,500-21,500 EUR) living costs over two years.
programs.scholarships: UNVERIFIED — ask the faculty. Czech public academies offer merit and accommodation scholarships to enrolled students but rarely fund non-EU entrants.
programs.intakes: Annual. UNVERIFIED - confirm dates with the faculty.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — the faculty publishes a step-by-step admission guide.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED - request the 2027/2028 admission calendar from the Divadelní fakulta.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — accredited public arts academy, full-time MgA., supports a Czech long-term residence permit for study.
programs.recommendation: RECORDED PRIMARILY FOR ITS NEGATIVE FINDING. JAMU Brno's Theatre Faculty is routinely assumed to host a sound-design master's; the official programme list shows it does not — its multimedia master's is a theatre/new-media creation degree with no named sound specialization, and JAMU's actual audio degree is the joint VUT Brno Audio Engineering Ing. already captured. For this candidate the programme is a poor fit: Czech-taught, talent-selected, theatre-rooted, and with no audio-engineering or music-production content he could point to. Do not pursue. Its practical value is that it closes a plausible-looking gap in the database and stops a future sweep from chasing it.

programs.program: Composition and Performance of Electronic Music (LT: Elektroninės muzikos kompozicija ir atlikimas) — MA

KTU links a 'STUDIJŲ KRYPTIES VERTINIMAS IR AKREDITAVIMAS' record and the programme appears in AIKOS (aikos.smm.lt), the official Ministry register. Exact current accreditation expiry date not shown on the programme page — UNVERIFIED; ask studijos@ktu.lt or check the SKVC register.
programs.durationEcts: 1.5 years (3 semesters), full-time, day-time, blended learning. 90 ECTS in total: Sem 1 = 30 cr (Composition of Electronic Music 1, Computer Based Music Analysis, Electronic Music Performance 1, Music Media and New Media, Theories of Music Composition and Interpretation); Sem 2 = 30 cr (Composition for Cinema, TV and Computer Games; Electronic Music Composition 2; Electronic Music Performance 2; Virtual Music Instruments; + 6 cr elective from Composition and Performance of Electroacoustic Music / Programming of Electronic Music / Sound Design Studio); Sem 3 = 30 cr Master's Degree Final Project.
programs.focus: Electronic music composition and performance; sound art; music technology; sound design; music for film, TV and computer games.
programs.whatYouStudy: Electronic music production and performance fundamentals; music/media relationship analysis; music programming; composing for different media; virtual instruments; electroacoustic composition and performance; a dedicated 'Sound Design Studio' elective; a 'Composition for Cinema, TV and Computer Games' core module (i.e. it does cover game audio). Taught by working electronic-music composers/producers (Antanas Jasenka, Jonas Jurkūnas, Titas Petrikis, Andrius Laucevičius). Officially described as 'the first Master's degree of its kind in Lithuania'.
programs.entryRequirements: University-track applicants: a bachelor's degree in ANY field of study is accepted (this is the single most notable feature for a non-music applicant). College (kolegija) graduates: a professional bachelor's in music studies PLUS either 30 credits of supplementary studies (papildomos studijos) or at least 1 year of relevant work experience. A mandatory entrance exam must be passed — failing or not taking it removes the applicant from the competition. Competition score = pass the entrance exam + motivation assessment (oral, 10-point scale, weight 0.1) + up to 4 bonus points (up to 2 for scientific/artistic activity; 0.5 each for ≥1 year field work experience, partial studies abroad ≥24 ECTS, completion of a talent-development programme, diploma with distinction).
programs.auditionSpec: A mandatory entrance exam (stojamasis egzaminas) assessed by the SHMMF faculty admission committee. The content, format and marking of the exam are NOT published on the official programme page or on the faculty event page — UNVERIFIED. Ask shmmf@ktu.lt (Faculty of Social Sciences, Arts and Humanities, A. Mickevičiaus g. 37, Kaunas) or studijos@ktu.lt.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — no portfolio specification is published on the official programme page. Given the entrance exam is run by the arts faculty, a submission of own works is likely but is not documented. Ask shmmf@ktu.lt.
programs.englishTest: None required for this programme (it is not taught in English). KTU's general international requirement of B2 English applies only to its English-taught programmes.
programs.tuitionEU: €10,624 per year for full-time studies; €177.07 per credit (published on the official programme page). Admission is 'only to state-unfunded (VNF) study places' — there are NO state-funded (valstybės finansuojamos) places on this programme, so even Lithuanian/EU students pay.
programs.tuitionNonEU: THE RATE HE WOULD PAY: KTU publishes a single rate for this programme — €10,624/year, €177.07/credit — and does not publish a separate non-EU rate, because the programme is Lithuanian-only and is not marketed to international applicants. Whether a differential international rate would be applied to a Tunisian national is UNVERIFIED. Living costs in Kaunas not published on this page — UNVERIFIED; the Lithuanian migration authority sets a minimum subsistence amount that must be evidenced for the residence permit. Total realistic self-pay burden: clearly above €20,000 for 1.5 years.

It is nevertheless unusable for him on three independent grounds: (1) teaching and assessment are 100% in Lithuanian, a language he does not have and cannot realistically reach by September 2027; (2) there are zero state-funded places, so he would self-pay roughly €15,900 in tuition alone for 90 ECTS — not 'genuinely cheap'; (3) Tunisia is excluded from the Lithuanian state master's scholarship nationality list, so no full funding route exists. programs.program: Film Art (LT: Kino menas) — MA, Sound Design (Garso dizainas) specialisation
programs.institution: Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre (LMTA), National Film School (Nacionalinė kino mokykla)
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. LMTA is a Lithuanian state academy of music and theatre; the programme carries the Lithuanian state study-programme code 6211PX003 and admission for EU/EEA applicants runs through the national LAMA BPO centralised system with state-funded and self-funded places. Non-EU applicants are handled directly by LMTA Admissions.
programs.language: LITHUANIAN ONLY. The LMTA English-language master's page states for Film Art: 'Language of instruction: Lithuanian' and adds 'Full-time studies are conducted in Lithuanian only. A C1-level Lithuanian language certificate is required.' All four specialisation curricula — Cinematography, Film Directing, Production and Sound Design — are marked (LT). Note the contrast within the same institution: LMTA's Composition, Music Performance and Dance Art masters are marked (LT/EN); Film Art is not.
programs.languageRequirement: A C1-level Lithuanian language certificate, stated explicitly on LMTA's own English admissions page. This is a hard, published requirement — not an inference. No English certificate substitutes.
programs.qualification: Menų magistras / Master of Arts, 120 ECTS, second cycle. State code 6211PX003, study field group 'Menai' (Arts), delivered by LMTA's National Film School. A real state-recognised second-cycle degree; graduates may proceed to third-cycle (doctoral) arts studies.
programs.accreditationStatus: Accredited Lithuanian second-cycle arts programme; LMTA's own programme page links the study-field evaluation and accreditation record ('STUDIJŲ KRYPTIES VERTINIMAS IR AKREDITAVIMAS'). Exact accreditation expiry not reproduced on the page — UNVERIFIED; check the SKVC register or ask priemimas@lmta.lt.
programs.durationEcts: 120 ECTS, 2 academic years full-time (30 ECTS per semester).
programs.focus: Film sound design and film sound post-production, inside a four-specialisation film-art master's (Sound Design / Production / Cinematography / Film Directing).
programs.whatYouStudy: The official Lithuanian programme page sets a sound-specific learning outcome for the Garso dizainas specialisation: the graduate 'will know sound research methods and will be able to analyse, evaluate and realise feature-film sound and other creative sound projects, taking account of the relevance and artistic value of the idea or theme.' The programme as a whole trains students to initiate and independently or collegially deliver innovative film projects and conduct artistic research, applying practical and theoretical knowledge of directing, producing, cinematography and sound design. LMTA describes it as the only programme of its kind in Lithuania.
programs.entryRequirements: A bachelor's degree plus a specialisation entrance examination. Documents required for the LMTA route include: online application (LAMA BPO for EU/EEA applicants; direct contact with LMTA Admissions for other international applicants), passport copy, bachelor's diploma and supplement with official translation into Lithuanian or English, an academic-recognition decision issued by LMTA or the Lithuanian Centre for Quality Assessment in Higher Education, proof of Lithuanian language proficiency at the level required for the chosen programme (C1 here), admission-fee receipt. CRITICAL: Film Art does NOT appear on LMTA's published 'Master Entry Requirements' list of second-cycle programmes open to international applicants (updated December 2025) — that list contains only Composition (Academic Composition; Digital Technologies) and the Music Performance specialisations in Vilnius and Klaipėda. Confirm with priemimas@lmta.lt whether a non-EU applicant can be admitted to Film Art at all.
programs.auditionSpec: A specialisation entrance examination set by LMTA; for the 2026 additional round examinations ran 17–19 August 2026 (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date), with remote participation only where explicitly indicated in the timetable or individually approved. The specific Sound Design examination programme is published in LMTA's annual 'Entrance examination requirements' document rather than on the programme page — UNVERIFIED here; request the Garso dizainas exam specification from priemimas@lmta.lt.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — not published on the programme page. An artistic-research/creative-project proposal is implied by the programme's structure (the degree is built around a creative film project plus an artistic research paper). Ask priemimas@lmta.lt.
programs.englishTest: Not applicable — English proficiency of at least B1 is required only for LMTA programmes taught in English. Film Art is Lithuanian-taught, so the Lithuanian C1 certificate is what is demanded instead.
programs.tuitionEU: €3,558 per semester (≈ €7,116 per academic year, ≈ €14,232 for the 120-ECTS degree), as published on LMTA's official English master's page. EU/EEA applicants may additionally compete for state-funded (valstybės finansuojamos) places through LAMA BPO.
programs.tuitionNonEU: THE RATE HE WOULD PAY: LMTA publishes one figure, €3,558 per semester, without a separate non-EU column, so on the published evidence a Tunisian national would pay ≈ €7,116/year self-funded (state-funded places are reserved for those eligible under Lithuanian legislation, i.e. EU/EEA citizens and their family members — a Tunisian national is not eligible). Whether LMTA applies an international surcharge is UNVERIFIED — confirm with priemimas@lmta.lt.

programs.scholarships: None available to him. State-funded places are restricted to applicants eligible under Lithuanian legislation (EU/EEA citizens and family members). The Lithuanian state master's scholarship call (2026: 70 grants) is nationality-restricted to Armenia, Azerbaijan, China (PRC and Taiwan), Georgia, Indonesia, Israel, Japan, Kazakhstan, Moldova, New Zealand, Philippines, South Korea, Ukraine, USA, Uzbekistan, Vietnam and foreign citizens of Lithuanian origin — TUNISIA IS NOT INCLUDED.

The 2026 intake has already run (main round plus an additional round with entrance exams on 17–19 August 2026). On a two-year cycle the following intake falls in 2028, NOT September 2027. ALL PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates. No 2027 dates published because the programme does not recruit in 2027.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle — LMTA is a state academy and the award is an accredited Lithuanian second-cycle degree, so an admitted non-EU student would qualify for a national D visa and temporary residence permit. In practice the C1 Lithuanian requirement, and the programme's absence from LMTA's list of masters open to international applicants, close this route for him.

But the specialisation exam and the programme's premise — that entrants are already working film-sound professionals deepening first-cycle competences — mean an applicant with no film-sound background and no portfolio would not be competitive. LMTA describes the cohort as 'professionals in the film field (video directing, cinematography, sound design and film producing) deepening and expanding knowledge acquired in the first study cycle.'

Teaching by recognised Lithuanian film artists and researchers with regular visiting international lecturers, and close cooperation with the Lithuanian film industry. LMTA is a member of the FilmEU European university alliance. Specific studio/equipment inventory not published on the programme page — UNVERIFIED.
