programs.program: Master akademske studije MUZIČKA PRODUKCIJA (MAS Music Production) — Interdisciplinary Studies
programs.institution: Akademija umetnosti (Academy of Arts), Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
programs.institutionType: State art academy; a constituent faculty (članica) of the public University of Novi Sad. Departments: Music, Fine & Applied Arts, Drama. This programme sits under 'Interdisciplinarne studije', administered by the Drama Department (application e-mail aunsprijemni.dramski@uns.ac.rs).
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Evidence: it is a članica of Univerzitet u Novom Sadu, a state university; the 2026/27 enrolment competition is issued on the basis of a decision of the Government of the Republic of Serbia on the number of students to be enrolled, and the official quota table lists state-BUDGET-funded places (2 budget + 8 self-financing for this programme). Budget places only exist at state-founded institutions.
programs.language: Serbian (Serbian only). All programme documentation, the informator and the entrance exam are in Serbian. No English-taught track exists. Note the parallel programme 'Gluma' is explicitly labelled 'na srpskom jeziku', confirming language-specific delivery at this Academy.
programs.languageRequirement: For foreign nationals the official 2026/27 konkurs requires 'доказ о познавању српског језика' (proof of knowledge of the Serbian language) at application. The required level, accepted certificate and issuing body are NOT published — UNVERIFIED. Ask: Služba za studije i studentska pitanja, +381 21 422-177 ext. 2 / aofarts@uns.ac.rs.
programs.englishTest: None. No IELTS/TOEFL is demanded anywhere in the konkurs or informator. The barrier here is Serbian, not English.
programs.qualification: Master akademske studije (MAS) — a real, state-recognised second-cycle degree (EQF/NQF level 7), 60 ECTS, 1 year. Professional title conferred: 'Мастер музички продуцент' (Master Music Producer). This is a degree, not a certificate.
programs.accreditationStatus: Accredited. The Academy's official accreditation page lists 'Uverenje o akreditaciji studijskog programa Muzička produkcija' under 'Master akademske studije akreditovane 2023. godine' (certificate PDF: https://akademija.uns.ac.rs/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/Muzicka-produkcija-Uverenje-novo.pdf — a scanned image, so the decision number could not be machine-read). Accrediting body: the Serbian Commission for Accreditation and Quality Assurance / National Accreditation Body (NAT). Being a state HEI programme it is automatically listed in the Serbian register of accredited programmes.
programs.durationEcts: 1 year / 2 semesters, 60 ECTS.
programs.focus: Music production. This is the single closest match in the entire Western-Balkan academy sector to a 'producer/DJ' career goal — it is music production proper, not film sound.
programs.whatYouStudy: Compulsory (from the official 2023-accreditation curriculum table, nastavni plan PDF): Muzička produkcija (2+2, both semesters); Zvuk i muzika na filmu (Sound and Music in Film, 2+1); Savremene tendencije u muzičkoj produkciji 1 and 2 (Contemporary Tendencies in Music Production); Muzika-događaj-publika (Music–Event–Audience); Master rad – istraživanje (research) and Master rad (thesis project). Electives, 12 ECTS to be chosen from: Istorija elektroakustičke muzike (History of Electroacoustic Music), Istorija popularne muzike (History of Popular Music), Produkcija muzike za nove medije (Music Production for New Media), Muzika u medijima (Music in Media), Dramaturgija savremenog filma, Metode u muzičkom obrazovanju u digitalnom okruženju.
programs.entryRequirements: THERE IS A DOCUMENTED CONTRADICTION BETWEEN TWO OFFICIAL DOCUMENTS — he must get this resolved in writing before doing anything else. (a) The 2026/27 konkurs text states: 'Студијски програм – Музичка продукција: завршене основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању из уметничке области Музичка продукција, или сродан студијски програм (240 ЕСПБ)' — i.e. a four-year BA IN THE ARTISTIC FIELD of music production or a RELATED programme. (b) The 2026/27 Informator for this exact programme states only: 'Пријемни испит могу полагати лица која су завршила основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању (240 ЕСПБ)' — any four-year 240-ECTS bachelor. Second, hard problem for HIM: 240 ECTS / four years is mandatory in both readings. A Tunisian three-year Licence in Software Engineering (180 ECTS) does NOT meet this. He must check what his SMU MedTech BSc is worth in ECTS and years, and whether a Serbian diploma-recognition decision (rešenje o priznavanju strane visokoškolske isprave) will grade it as a four-year/240-ECTS first degree. If it is 180 ECTS he is ineligible regardless of portfolio. Foreign nationals additionally submit: diploma-recognition decision, proof of health insurance, proof of Serbian language.
programs.portfolioSpec: With the application: (1) a PORTFOLIO of works created in the three years preceding the entrance exam; (2) motivation letter; (3) CV; (4) diploma/certificate of completed four-year BA (240 ECTS); (5) a MEDICAL CERTIFICATE INCLUDING AN AUDIOGRAM, signed by an ophthalmologist, an ENT specialist and a psychologist — an unusual and genuinely blocking requirement he must arrange in Tunisia in advance; (6) scanned ID; (7) photo min. 1200x800 px JPG under 1 MB; (8) proof of payment of the application fee. Submission is 100% electronic — one e-mail per candidate, all files under 12 MB total, each file named with the candidate's name. His one-year portfolio-building plan maps exactly onto the 'works from the previous 3 years' rule, so a portfolio built in 2026-27 is admissible for a 2027 application.
programs.auditionSpec: Two-stage entrance exam. PART ONE (pass/fail): a written test in the professional-artistic field of Music Production; a written analysis/evaluation of a piece of music against subjective and objective criteria set by the commission; an interview with the commission. Candidates who pass proceed to multi-day exercises and PART TWO: assessment of the submitted works — up to 30 points; practical work using the Academy's own equipment — up to 20 points; oral examination of knowledge in the professional-artistic field of audiovisual media (interview with the commission) — up to 30 points. Separately, BA grade average scores up to 20 points (10.00 = 20 pts, down to 6.00-6.49 = 4 pts). A candidate who does not exceed 50 total points fails and is not ranked. The exam is conducted in Serbian.
programs.equipmentRequired: Part two of the entrance exam is 'практичан рад на материјалу Академије' — practical work on the Academy's own material/equipment, so no personal studio rig is required for the exam. What he must bring is a portfolio of finished audio work. Studio equipment inventory not published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: The programme is delivered with practical studio work at the Academy (the entrance exam itself is run on Academy equipment). No published inventory of studios, control rooms, consoles or immersive/Atmos capability — UNVERIFIED. Ask the Drama Department / Katedra za audiovizuelne medije directly.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Ambiguous and decisive for him — see entryRequirements. The Informator wording admits any 240-ECTS four-year bachelor (which would let a software engineer in); the konkurs wording restricts to the artistic field of music production or a cognate programme. Even on the permissive reading, the entrance exam is a subject-matter exam in music production plus a portfolio, so it is not a soft entry. He has no music degree and no portfolio yet, which makes this a stretch but not an automatic exclusion — unlike a conservatory performance master, there is no instrumental audition.
programs.tuitionEU: Not applicable as a category in Serbia. Domestic self-financing students: 125,000 RSD per year (official 2026/27 konkurs quota table).
programs.tuitionNonEU: EUR 1,800 per year — THE RATE HE WOULD PAY. The official 2026/27 konkurs quota table has a dedicated column 'Школарина за странце (евра)' showing 1800 for every study programme at the Academy, including this one. Note the anomaly: at ~117 RSD/EUR, 125,000 RSD is roughly EUR 1,065, so the foreigner rate is about 70% higher than the domestic self-financing rate but still very low by European standards.
programs.otherFees: Application/entrance-exam fee: amount not stated in the extracted konkurs text — UNVERIFIED (paid to account 840-32790845-46; ask Služba za studije). Diploma and certificate issuing fees: 4,000 RSD to the University plus 4,000 RSD to the Academy (payment reference 300 for the Drama Department). Diploma recognition (nostrifikacija) fee at the University of Novi Sad — UNVERIFIED. Compulsory health insurance for foreign students — cost UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition EUR 1,800 for the whole degree (it is a one-year, 60-ECTS master). Living costs in Novi Sad are not published by the Academy — UNVERIFIED; do not use third-party estimates as fact. This is nonetheless among the cheapest genuinely accredited music-production masters found anywhere in the region.
programs.fundingLevel: Check. There are 2 state-budget (fee-free) places on this programme against 8 self-financing places. The konkurs says a foreign national may enrol 'под истим условима као и домаћи држављанин' (under the same conditions as a domestic citizen), yet it simultaneously publishes a separate foreigner tuition rate — so whether a Tunisian can actually take one of the 2 budget places is UNVERIFIED and must be asked in writing before applying. Realistically, plan for EUR 1,800.
programs.scholarships: No programme-level or Academy-level scholarship for non-EU applicants is published on any official page opened for this record — UNVERIFIED. Do not assume one exists. Where to ask: (1) the Serbian Ministry of Education's bilateral/developing-country scholarship offers, which are distributed to candidates through their home ministry — he should ask the Tunisian Ministère de l'Enseignement Supérieur whether Serbia offers Tunisia places in a given year; (2) the University of Novi Sad international office. Erasmus+ credit mobility is inbound-only for enrolled students and is not an admission route.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle — this is an accredited programme at a state university, which is the category that supports a Serbian temporary residence permit for the purpose of education (privremeni boravak radi školovanja). A Tunisian national requires a visa D (long-stay study visa) obtained before travel, then converts to temporary residence in Serbia. The konkurs itself confirms the institution enrols foreign nationals and lists the extra documents required (diploma recognition, health insurance, Serbian language proof). Exact visa D document list, fees and processing times are NOT published by the Academy — UNVERIFIED; the authoritative sources are the Serbian Ministry of Interior (MUP) and the Serbian embassy accredited to Tunisia. Serbia is not in the EU or Schengen, so this permit gives no EU mobility rights.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, October start (Serbian academic year).
programs.applicationOpens: For the 2026/27 cycle the konkurs text was published 29 May 2026 and the application portal/informator went live in July 2026. For his SEPTEMBER/OCTOBER 2027 target he should expect the 2027/28 konkurs to be published around May-June 2027 with the informator in July 2027 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.

For a 2027 entry he applies around early October 2027 — but he must start the diploma-recognition process and the audiogram/medical certificate many months earlier.
programs.recommendation: THE SINGLE BEST FIND IN THIS SLICE FOR HIS STATED CAREER GOAL, and cheap enough to be realistic (EUR 1,800 total tuition). But three hard gates, in order of severity: (1) the 240-ECTS / four-year first-degree rule — if his SMU MedTech BSc is a three-year 180-ECTS licence he is ineligible, full stop, so verify this FIRST via a Serbian diploma-recognition enquiry; (2) proof of Serbian language, level unspecified — with Arabic/French/English and no Slavic language, a year of Serbian study is a real commitment and he should ask now what certificate is accepted; (3) a subject-matter entrance exam in music production plus a three-year portfolio window plus an ENT audiogram. His IELTS/TOEFL gap is irrelevant here, which is a genuine advantage. Concrete next step: e-mail aofarts@uns.ac.rs and aunsprijemni.dramski@uns.ac.rs asking, in one message, (a) whether a 180-ECTS three-year foreign bachelor can ever be accepted, (b) which Serbian-language certificate and level satisfies the requirement, (c) whether foreign nationals may compete for the 2 budget places.

programs.program: Master akademske studije DIZAJN VIDEO IGARA (MAS Video Game Design) — Interdisciplinary Studies
programs.institution: Akademija umetnosti (Academy of Arts), Univerzitet u Novom Sadu
programs.institutionType: State art academy, constituent faculty of the public University of Novi Sad. The programme sits under 'Interdisciplinarne studije' and is run out of the Drama Department's Katedra za audiovizuelne medije (Chair of Audiovisual Media).
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC — same evidence as the Music Production entry: constituent of the state University of Novi Sad, enrolment numbers fixed by a Government of Serbia decision, 2 state-budget places published in the official quota table.
programs.language: Serbian only. The official programme page states the programme is taught in Serbian; the entrance exam, informator and curriculum are Serbian. No English track.
programs.languageRequirement: Foreign nationals must supply 'доказ о познавању српског језика' (proof of knowledge of Serbian) per the 2026/27 konkurs. Required level/certificate NOT published — UNVERIFIED; ask Služba za studije, +381 21 422-177.
programs.englishTest: None required.
programs.qualification: Master akademske studije (MAS), a genuine state-recognised second-cycle degree, 60 ECTS, 1 year. (The first-cycle sibling programme confers 'diplomirani umetnik digitalnih medija'; the exact master title was not machine-readable from the scanned accreditation certificate — UNVERIFIED, ask the Academy.)
programs.accreditationStatus: Accredited. Listed on the Academy's official accreditation page as 'Uverenje o akreditaciji studijskog programa Dizajn video igara' under 'Master akademske studije akreditovane 2024. godine' (https://akademija.uns.ac.rs/wp-content/uploads/2019/10/MAS-Dizajn-video-igara-1.pdf, scanned). The first-cycle programme was accredited in 2017 and the Academy describes it as the first accredited video-game programme in the Western Balkans.
programs.durationEcts: 1 year, 60 ECTS (official curriculum table 5.1b).
programs.focus: Video game design — included here ONLY because game audio sits inside it as an elective strand. This is not an audio degree.
programs.whatYouStudy: Compulsory (official curriculum table): MA701 Žanrovska analiza i sinteza video igara (12 ECTS); MA703 Studije video igara (4); MP2102 Grafičke komunikacije u interaktivnim medijima (6); MA7002 Imerzivne igre / Immersive Games (6); MAZRD Završni rad (12); MAZRI Završni rad – istraživanje (12). Electives, 12 ECTS chosen from a list that is where the audio content lives: MSMIM Muzika u medijima (Music in Media, 6); MA1003 Zvuk u filmskoj umetnosti (Sound in Film Art, 6); MA4003 Produkcija muzike za nove medije (Music Production for New Media, 6); MA1002 Audiovizuelna artikulacija (6); MA2002 Postprodukcija filmske slike (6); MLVIA Video art (6). At most 12 ECTS of the 60 can be audio.
programs.entryRequirements: Clean and permissive, and identical in BOTH official documents (no contradiction here, unlike the Music Production programme): 'Студијски програм – Дизајн видео игара: завршене основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању' / 'лица која су завршила основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању (240 ЕСПБ)' — ANY four-year, 240-ECTS bachelor in any field. No artistic-field restriction. The 240-ECTS / four-year rule is still the gate for a Tunisian three-year licence. Foreign nationals additionally file a diploma-recognition decision, health insurance proof and Serbian language proof.
programs.portfolioSpec: With the application: (1) an EXPLICATION of the artistic-research project the candidate intends to realise as the master's thesis; (2) a motivation letter; (3) a PORTFOLIO of the candidate's previous works in the field of video game design; (4) diploma/certificate of a four-year 240-ECTS bachelor; (5) CV; (6) scanned ID; (7) photo 1200x800 px; (8) proof of application-fee payment. NOTE: unlike Music Production, NO medical certificate or audiogram is demanded.
programs.auditionSpec: Two stages. PART ONE (pass/fail): test of knowledge of the history and aesthetics of video games; a combined test of creative solution of design tasks; analysis of the submitted entry work plus interview with the commission. PART TWO (after multi-day exercises): assessment of works submitted with the application — up to 25 points; practical work in video game design — up to 25 points; oral examination in the professional-artistic field of video game design — up to 30 points. BA grade average adds up to 20 points. Under 50 total points = fail, no ranking. Conducted in Serbian.
programs.equipmentRequired: Practical exam work is done at the Academy. No personal equipment requirement published. A demonstrable body of game-design work is the real requirement.
programs.facilities: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Ask Katedra za audiovizuelne medije. The presence of a compulsory 'Imerzivne igre' (Immersive Games) course implies some interactive/VR capability but nothing is documented.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly. Any four-year 240-ECTS bachelor qualifies, in both the konkurs and the informator. For a software engineer this is by far the most accessible second-cycle art-academy programme found anywhere in this eight-country slice, and his coding background is a direct asset rather than a handicap. The trade-off is that it is a game-design degree with only 12 ECTS of optional audio.
programs.tuitionEU: Not an applicable category in Serbia. Domestic self-financing rate: 125,000 RSD per year.
programs.tuitionNonEU: EUR 1,800 per year — THE RATE HE WOULD PAY, from the 'Школарина за странце (евра)' column of the official 2026/27 konkurs quota table, which shows 1800 for this programme. Total tuition for the degree is EUR 1,800 since it is one year.
programs.otherFees: Application/entrance-exam fee — amount UNVERIFIED (paid to Academy account 840-32790845-46). Diploma and certificate issuing: 4,000 RSD to the University + 4,000 RSD to the Academy. Diploma recognition fee and compulsory health insurance — UNVERIFIED.
programs.totalCostEstimate: EUR 1,800 tuition for the whole master. Living costs in Novi Sad not published by the institution — UNVERIFIED.
programs.fundingLevel: Check. 2 state-budget places and 8 self-financing places (2026/27). Whether a foreign national may compete for a budget place is UNVERIFIED — the konkurs says foreigners enrol under the same conditions as domestic citizens but publishes a separate foreigner tariff. Plan for EUR 1,800.
programs.scholarships: None published at programme or Academy level for non-EU applicants — UNVERIFIED. Route to ask: Tunisian Ministère de l'Enseignement Supérieur (bilateral Serbian government scholarship offers, if any in a given year) and the University of Novi Sad international office.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle — accredited programme at a state university, the category that supports a Serbian temporary residence permit for education. Tunisian nationals need a long-stay visa D first. Document lists, fees and timelines are not published by the Academy — UNVERIFIED; authoritative sources are the Serbian MUP and the Serbian embassy accredited to Tunisia. Serbia is outside the EU/Schengen.
programs.intakes: One intake per year, October start.
programs.applicationOpens: 2026/27 konkurs text published 29 May 2026, informator July 2026. Expect the 2027/28 equivalents around May-July 2027 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.deadline: 2026/27 cycle (PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for 2027/28): electronic application 05.10.2026; entrance exam 07-13.10.2026; preliminary list 15.10.2026; final list and enrolment 20.10.2026. Applications close in early October of the year of entry.
programs.recommendation: Report this as his BACKUP / realistic-entry option in Serbia, not his first choice. It is the only programme found in this whole eight-country academy sweep whose published entry rule admits any four-year bachelor without an artistic-field restriction, and his software-engineering background is directly relevant. But be honest with him: it is a game-design master, audio is capped at 12 of 60 ECTS (Music in Media, Sound in Film Art, Music Production for New Media), it will not make him a DJ or a record producer, and it still requires a video-game-design portfolio he does not have. The same 240-ECTS/four-year gate and the same Serbian-language gate apply. If he wants Novi Sad, the Music Production MAS is the right target and this is the fallback if the artistic-field restriction blocks him.

programs.program: Master akademske studije MUZIČKA PRODUKCIJA (MAS Music Production), Fakultet digitalnih umetnosti
programs.institution: Univerzitet Metropolitan
programs.city: Belgrade (programme delivered in person at the Belgrade campus, Tadeuša Košćuška 63; the university also has a Niš campus)
programs.institutionType: Private university with four faculties (Information Technologies, Management, Digital Arts, Foreign Languages). This programme is at the Faculty of Digital Arts (FDU Metropolitan — not to be confused with the state FDU Belgrade).
programs.publicPrivate: PRIVATE. Evidence from the university's own official accreditation page: it operates under a 'dozvola za rad' (work licence) issued by the Serbian authorities, first issued in 2010 and most recently amended in November 2025 — the licensing regime that applies to privately founded HEIs. There are no state-budget places; all study is fee-paying. It is nevertheless a licensed, accredited university, not a diploma mill.
programs.language: Serbian. The programme page, all course descriptions (AD511, AD560, AD570, AD512, MG525, AD591/592) and the fee table are published in Serbian only, and the delivery mode is stated as 'tradicionalni (u prostorijama univerziteta u Beogradu)' — classroom and music studio in Belgrade. Whether an English-medium delivery of THIS programme exists is NOT stated anywhere on the official page — UNVERIFIED (the university does run English-language and internet-study offerings elsewhere, so it is worth asking explicitly).
programs.languageRequirement: Not published for this programme — UNVERIFIED. The admissions page for master studies states only that enrolment is open year-round and gives no prior-degree, language, document or foreign-national requirements at all. Ask upis@metropolitan.ac.rs in writing.
programs.englishTest: Not published — UNVERIFIED. No IELTS/TOEFL band is stated for this programme.
programs.qualification: Master akademske studije (MAS), 60 ECTS, 1 year, 2 semesters. Professional title: 'Master muzički producent' (Master Music Producer). Field declared as IMT (interdisciplinary/multidisciplinary/dual-field), areas: Dramatic and Audiovisual Arts + Management and Business. This is a real second-cycle academic degree, not a private 'diploma' — it is an accredited MAS.
programs.accreditationStatus: Accredited. The university's official accreditation page lists 'Muzička produkcija' among the accredited master programmes of the Faculty of Digital Arts, and the programme page itself carries the 'AKREDITOVANO' mark. Accrediting bodies named on the official page: the Commission for Accreditation and Quality Assurance and the National Council for Higher Education; the general accreditation decision covering all 18 programmes is dated 2025. A specific accreditation decision number/date for this individual programme is NOT published — UNVERIFIED, request the uverenje.
programs.durationEcts: 1 year / 2 semesters, 60 ECTS.
programs.focus: Music production plus music-industry management and marketing. Explicitly aimed at people who want to build a career in the music industry, including content creation for film, TV, social platforms and streaming services — the closest programme found in this slice to his stated 'international DJ and producer' goal, in intent if not in prestige.
programs.whatYouStudy: Official course list from the programme page: AD511 Muzička produkcija 1 (audio technology, music software, arranging, microphone placement, instrument miking, basic mixing and mastering); AD512 Muzička produkcija 2 (theory of analogue and digital recording and sound processing, equipment and techniques, sound formats and carriers); AD560 Kreativna radionica zvuka (creative sound workshop — practical sound-design projects, experimentation with digital audio tools, sound installations, history of music-scenic performance); AD570 Novi mediji i tehnologija u performansu; MG525 Upravljanje inovacijama i tehnologijama; elective block 1 (MK520 Kreiranje digitalnog brenda / MK525 Digitalne marketinške kampanje); elective block 2 (AD535 Advertajzing / AD565 Digitalna kultura); elective 3 (MG535 Digitalno preduzetništvo / MG545 Strateški menadžment i liderstvo); AD591 Završni rad muzičke produkcije – SIR and AD592 Završni rad – izrada i odbrana.
programs.entryRequirements: NOT PUBLISHED. The official master admissions page states only that 'upis na master akademske studije može se izvršiti bez ograničenja tokom čitave godine' (master enrolment can be done without restriction throughout the whole year) and gives no prior-degree, ECTS, entrance-exam, portfolio, nostrification or foreign-national requirements — UNVERIFIED. The programme page says the studies are 'intended for musicians, music producers, performers, and any interested candidates who wish to create or advance a career in the music industry, in accordance with their interests and previously acquired experience', which reads permissively but is marketing copy, not a rule. He must obtain the written admission rules (pravilnik o upisu) and the required prior-degree ECTS from upis@metropolitan.ac.rs before treating this as an option.
programs.portfolioSpec: Not published — UNVERIFIED. No portfolio, audition or entrance-exam specification appears on any official page for this programme.
programs.auditionSpec: Not published — UNVERIFIED. No entrance exam is described for master entry.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Teaching is stated to take place in classrooms and a music studio ('predavanja i vežbe u učionici i muzičkom studiu').
programs.facilities: A music studio at the Belgrade campus is referenced in the programme description. No inventory, no studio specification, no immersive/Atmos claim — UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Probably yes on the marketing copy ('all interested candidates... in accordance with their previously acquired experience') and there is no published entrance exam or portfolio bar — but nothing in the official admission rules confirms it. Treat as UNVERIFIED until confirmed in writing. Note that a third of the curriculum is management/marketing, which a software-engineering graduate would handle comfortably.
programs.tuitionEU: Not an applicable category in Serbia. The published rate of EUR 4,500 per year is explicitly headed 'CENA ŠKOLARINA ZA DRŽAVLJANE R. SRBIJE I BIVŠIH SFRJ REPUBLIKA' — i.e. it applies to citizens of Serbia and of the former Yugoslav republics only. Payable in monthly instalments.
programs.tuitionNonEU: NOT PUBLISHED — UNVERIFIED, and this is a material finding. The only fee table on the official page is expressly restricted to Serbian and ex-Yugoslav nationals; a Tunisian national falls outside it and the rate he would actually pay is nowhere stated. Do not assume it is EUR 4,500 — private Serbian universities commonly charge non-regional students more. He must ask upis@metropolitan.ac.rs / +381 11 20 30 885 for the written foreign-national tariff for MAS Muzička produkcija before considering this.
programs.otherFees: Not published — UNVERIFIED. No application fee, enrolment fee, diploma fee or health-insurance cost is stated. The university advertises 'specijalni popusti i pogodnosti' (special discounts) — terms not published for foreign students.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Cannot be stated. Even the tuition input is unknown for a Tunisian national. As a floor, the ex-Yugoslav rate of EUR 4,500 for one year is 2.5x the Academy of Arts Novi Sad foreigner rate for a comparable one-year 60-ECTS master — so on published evidence this fails his 'only self-pay if genuinely cheap' test.
programs.fundingLevel: None visible. It is a private university with no state-budget places. The scholarships page is aimed at competitions for domestic entrants; nothing for non-EU master applicants is published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarships: Nothing a Tunisian applicant can realistically win is published on the official site — UNVERIFIED. The 'Stipendije i takmičenja' page exists but no non-EU master scholarship is documented. Ask admissions directly.
programs.visaEligible: Probably yes, but confirm. The university holds a Serbian work licence and its programmes are accredited, which is the class of institution whose enrolment supports a temporary residence permit for education in Serbia; a Tunisian would need a visa D first. However, the university publishes NOTHING about foreign-national enrolment, diploma recognition or visa support — UNVERIFIED. Before paying anything, confirm with the Serbian Ministry of Interior (MUP) and the Serbian embassy accredited to Tunisia that enrolment at this specific private university is accepted as the basis for a study residence permit, and ask the university for its international-student office. Serbia is outside the EU/Schengen.
programs.intakes: Enrolment is advertised as open throughout the year for master studies, which in practice means rolling admission rather than a single fixed intake. October start is the standard Serbian academic-year start.
programs.applicationOpens: Rolling — the official admissions page states master enrolment can be done without restriction all year. Online application via the university's admission portal.
programs.deadline: No published deadline (rolling admission). For a September/October 2027 start this is administratively the easiest calendar in the whole slice, but the visa timeline, not the university deadline, becomes the binding constraint.
programs.recommendation: A genuine gap-fill — an accredited Serbian master in music production that no earlier sweep caught — and the curriculum (two semesters of music production, a creative sound workshop, plus branding/marketing/entrepreneurship) is unusually well aligned with an aspiring producer-DJ who also wants to run himself as a business. But three warnings he must hear. First, the price he would pay is unknown: the only published figure, EUR 4,500/year, is expressly for Serbian and ex-Yugoslav nationals, so his rate is UNVERIFIED and likely higher. Second, at that price it is roughly 2.5x the public Academy of Arts Novi Sad, which teaches a deeper, more artistically serious music-production master for EUR 1,800 — so this only makes sense if Novi Sad's 240-ECTS or Serbian-language gates block him. Third, essentially nothing about admission requirements, portfolio, language or foreign-national procedure is published; a programme that will not tell you its entry rules before you enquire deserves caution even when accredited. Action: one e-mail to upis@metropolitan.ac.rs asking for (a) the foreign-national tuition for MAS Muzička produkcija, (b) the minimum prior degree in years and ECTS, (c) the language of instruction and any language certificate, (d) whether they support study-residence-permit applications.

programs.program: Звукорежисура и звуков дизайн за игри (Sound Engineering and Sound Design for Games)
programs.institution: Национална музикална академия „Проф. Панчо Владигеров" / National Academy of Music "Prof. Pancho Vladigerov", Sofia
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. State higher-education institution established by law, listed in the NEAA (National Evaluation and Accreditation Agency, government.bg) register of accredited institutions; it operates state-subsidised places ("държавна поръчка") allocated by the Council of Ministers, and its rector's orders are issued under the Higher Education Act (ЗВО). Ministry of Education and Science is the founding authority.
programs.institutionType: Music academy (specialist state conservatoire)
programs.qualification: ОКС „магистър" — a real, state-recognised second-cycle (Master's) degree under the Bulgarian Higher Education Act. Fully supports a type-D student visa and student residence permit for a third-country national (the academy runs a formal non-EU admission channel with MES Certificate of Acceptance).
programs.accreditationStatus: Institutionally accredited by NEAA (Bulgarian national accreditation agency). Programme sits in the Teoretiko-kompozitorski i dirigentski fakultet (Theory-Composition-Conducting Faculty) and appears in the officially approved 2025/2026 candidate-master handbook signed by the Rector.
programs.focus: Game audio / sound design
programs.whatYouStudy: Sound engineering and sound design specifically for video games. The entrance syllabus (and by implication the taught content) covers physical acoustics and behaviour of sound in space; sound-technical devices — electroacoustic transducers, mixing consoles, amplifiers, processors; spatial audio formats (characteristics, specifics, applications); and computer/electronic music technologies. Reading list is Ballou 'Handbook for Sound Engineers', Huber & Runstein 'Modern Recording Techniques', Huber 'The MIDI Manual', Eargle 'The Microphone Book' and 'Loudspeaker Handbook', Blackstock 'Fundamentals of Physical Acoustics', plus Bulgarian acoustics texts by Malyakov and Kusev.
programs.durationEcts: 2 academic years (двугодишна магистратура) for applicants whose bachelor's is in a DIFFERENT field. A 1-year version exists only for those who already hold a bachelor's in the same specialty. ECTS total: UNVERIFIED — the handbook states duration in years, not credits; ask the ТКДФ faculty office (Теоретико-композиторски и диригентски факултет, nma.bg).
programs.language: Bulgarian. No English-taught track exists for this specialty.
programs.languageRequirement: A Bulgarian-language proficiency certificate issued by a Bulgarian higher-education institution. Applicants without it must sit written AND oral Bulgarian-language examinations (minimum grade Мн. добър 4.50 each for state-funded places), or complete the academy's one-year Bulgarian preparatory course first. No IELTS/TOEFL is accepted or relevant.
programs.entryRequirements: A completed bachelor's or master's degree. CRITICAL AND FAVOURABLE POINT FOR THIS CANDIDATE: unlike Музикознание, Композиция and Дирижиране — where the 2025/26 handbook explicitly states "Необходимо е кандидатът да притежава музикална образователно-квалификационна степен „Бакалавър"" (a MUSIC bachelor's is required) — the two Звукорежисура specialties carry NO such clause. A non-music bachelor (e.g. BSc Software Engineering) enters the two-year track. Non-EU applicants additionally need: NACID recognition of the foreign diploma, legalised/translated documents, passport copy, two photos, GDPR declarations.
programs.auditionSpec: Single-stage oral interview (събеседване) on four set topics: (1) physical acoustics, behaviour of sound in space, sound phenomena; (2) sound-technical devices — electroacoustic transducers, mixing desks, amplifiers, processors; (3) spatial sound formats; (4) computer and electronic music technologies. No instrumental audition. No solfège test. This is a THEORY interview, not a performance audition — realistically preparable in a year by a technically-minded software engineer.
programs.portfolioSpec: No portfolio is required by the published exam programme — admission is by interview on the technical syllabus only. This is unusual and materially advantageous for a candidate with no portfolio. Confirm with the faculty office, as practice can differ from the printed handbook.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED. Not stated in the admission handbook. Ask the ТКДФ faculty office whether a personal laptop/DAW licence is expected.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED for this specialty specifically. NMA operates recording studios attached to the sound-engineering department; no published equipment inventory was found. Ask the department directly.
programs.tuitionEU: State-subsidised (държавна поръчка) places are free of tuition for Bulgarian and EU/EEA nationals who have not previously held a state-funded master's place; fee-paying Bulgarian/EU places exist at the academy's domestic rate (figure not published on the pages checked — UNVERIFIED).
programs.tuitionNonEU: €8,500 per academic year. This is the rate he would pay as a Tunisian national. Quoted verbatim from NMA's own non-EU admissions page: "ГОДИШНИ такси за обучение за новоприети: … За магистратура – 8500 евро". If he needs the Bulgarian preparatory language year first, that is a further €5,500 for that year. Non-EU applicants are NOT eligible for the state-subsidised places.
programs.otherFees: Application fee for domestic-channel candidates 100 leva; for non-EU candidates a candidate fee set by the number of entrance exams. Bulgarian-language exam fee €50. Expedited September application fee €230.08 (versus €153.39 for the June round). Living costs in Sofia are additional.
programs.scholarships: No NMA scholarship for self-funding non-EU nationals was found on the official site. Bulgaria has no broad national scholarship equivalent to Stipendium Hungaricum open to Tunisia on the evidence found; state-subsidised places are reserved for Bulgarian/EU nationals and for persons of Bulgarian origin under ПМС 103/1993 and ПМС 228/1997, neither of which a Tunisian national qualifies for. The only realistic routes are (a) a Tunisian government bilateral scholarship — ask the Bulgarian Embassy in Tunis and the Tunisian Ministère de l'Enseignement Supérieur about the Bulgaria–Tunisia educational cooperation programme, and (b) after enrolment, Erasmus+ mobility. Treat this programme as effectively self-funded at €8,500/yr.
programs.applicationOpens: Non-EU documents are received from roughly spring; the 2026/27 non-EU deadline was 12 June 2026. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Domestic-channel master's document window for 2025/26 was 27 May – 4 June 2025 (ТКДФ). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.deadline: For a September 2027 start expect a non-EU document deadline around 12 June 2027. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date — the exact 2027 date is published on nma.bg/priem each spring.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. NMA runs an explicit non-EU ("извън ЕС") admission route culminating in a Ministry of Education and Science Certificate of Acceptance, which is the document required to apply for a Bulgarian type-D long-stay visa and then a student residence permit.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — and this is the key finding. The 2025/26 official handbook imposes the "music bachelor's required" condition only on Musicology, Composition and Conducting; the two sound-engineering specialties are open to any prior higher education, taking the two-year route. A BSc Software Engineering is therefore an eligible entry qualification.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Approximately €17,000 in tuition for the two-year master's, plus roughly €5,500 if a Bulgarian preparatory language year is needed first (so up to ~€22,500 tuition over three years), plus Sofia living costs (UNVERIFIED — no official figure published; budget separately) and application/exam fees of a few hundred euro.
programs.recommendation: WORTH A SERIOUS LOOK ON ACADEMIC FIT, BUT PROBABLY UNAFFORDABLE. This is the single best academic match found anywhere in this three-country slice: game audio, spatial sound, electronic music technology, entry by a technical interview rather than a music audition, no portfolio demanded, and — uniquely — no music bachelor's required. For a software engineer it is the most winnable admission in Hungary/Romania/Bulgaria. The two killers are money and language: €8,500/year with no scholarship he can win, and instruction entirely in Bulgarian with a certified Bulgarian-language requirement he cannot meet by September 2027 without a paid preparatory year. Realistic plan if he wants it: decide by autumn 2026, start Bulgarian immediately, budget ~€22.5k, and email the ТКДФ faculty office now to ask (a) whether the interview can be sat in English or with an interpreter, (b) the ECTS total, (c) whether any tuition reduction exists for non-EU students. If the answer on language is no, drop it.

It teaches the business of music (labels, copyright, industry tech), not sound design or production craft, so it does not build the studio skills he says he wants. Its defects are identical to the game-audio programme: €8,500/year unfunded and taught entirely in Bulgarian, plus a September application window that is very tight against non-EU visa timelines. programs.institutionType: Music, dance and fine arts academy (state)

programs.focus: Sound engineering / studio production
programs.whatYouStudy: Sound recording and reproduction technology; sound-technical devices; MIDI technology; DAW work (curriculum names Cubase SX/Sonar with automation and key editing); studio acoustics and musical acoustics; psychoacoustics; sound synthesis; multimedia post-production; specialised computer training; radio and live-sound practice; plus a foreign language. programs.durationEcts: 1.5 years (три семестъра) full-time after a bachelor's degree. ECTS total: UNVERIFIED — the published учебен план gives duration, not a credit total. Ask the Учебен отдел.
programs.language: Bulgarian. No English track.
programs.languageRequirement: Not published on the admission-conditions page. Since teaching is in Bulgarian and foreign diplomas must go through the Bulgarian academic-recognition procedure before applying, assume a Bulgarian-language requirement and/or the academy's €4,600 language course (езиков курс) is needed. AMTII sells that language year as a priced product in the same Rector's order, which strongly implies non-Bulgarian speakers are routed through it. CONFIRM with uchebenotdel@artacademyplovdiv.com. programs.entryRequirements: Completed bachelor's degree (ОКС „бакалавър"). Foreign diploma holders MUST complete the Bulgarian academic-recognition procedure BEFORE submitting the application — this is a hard sequencing constraint that takes months and must be started early. Documents: application form on the academy template, two declarations, secondary-school diploma, bachelor's diploma, proof of fee payment; a CV is required for certain other specialties. Whether a MUSIC bachelor's is required for Тонрежисура specifically is UNVERIFIED — the published pages do not say. This is the single most important question to ask; email gergina.nedelcheva@artacademyplovdiv.com (Учебен отдел, master's admissions, 032 601 445 / 0885 218 736).
programs.auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED. The specialty page and the general master's admission-conditions page do not publish an entrance-exam specification for Тонрежисура. Candidate exam fees at AMTII run €24–€40 depending on specialty, which implies an exam of some kind exists. Ask the Учебен отдел for the конспект.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — not published. Ask the Учебен отдел.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — not published.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED — no published studio inventory. The curriculum references studio acoustics, radio and live-sound practice, implying studio and broadcast facilities. Ask for a studio tour or a facilities list.
programs.tuitionEU: Bulgarian/EU/EEA/Swiss rates are published in a separate order ("Такси BG студенти и докторанти") — figure not extracted; UNVERIFIED. State-subsidised places exist for Bulgarian/EU nationals.
programs.tuitionNonEU: €7,600 per academic year for full-time (редовно обучение) master's-after-bachelor's study. This is THE RATE HE WOULD PAY as a Tunisian national. Quoted from Rector's Order РД-16-366/05.06.2026: "Образователно-квалификационна степен „магистър" след придобита „бакалавър": 4.1. Редовно обучение - 7600 евро". Part-time (задочно) is €4,200/year, but a part-time enrolment will generally NOT support a student residence permit — do not assume the cheaper rate is available to him. A preparatory language course, if required, is €4,600.
programs.otherFees: Candidate/entrance-exam fee €24–€40 (46.94–78.23 BGN) depending on specialty. Bulgarian diploma-recognition procedure costs and translation/legalisation costs additional (UNVERIFIED). Plovdiv living costs additional — materially cheaper than Sofia, but no official figure published.
programs.scholarships: None found that a Tunisian national can win. The ПМС 103/1993 and ПМС 228/1997 channels AMTII operates are for persons of Bulgarian origin and for citizens of North Macedonia, plus persons granted temporary protection — a Tunisian national does not qualify. Ask the Bulgarian Embassy in Tunis whether a Bulgaria–Tunisia bilateral education agreement offers places.
programs.applicationOpens: Varies by specialty and is published annually. The ПМС/foreign-channel entrance exams for 2026/27 were set for 10 September 2026. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED for the master's foreign-student channel. Published deadlines vary by specialty and year. Ask uchebenotdel@artacademyplovdiv.com. Note the diploma-recognition step must complete BEFORE the deadline, so work back at least six months.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — AMTII admits foreign nationals under Art. 95(8) of the Higher Education Act with a published foreign-student fee schedule, which is the state channel that produces the MES Certificate of Acceptance needed for a type-D visa and student residence permit.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED and decisive. The academy does not publish whether a music bachelor's is required. Given it is a music academy and the curriculum assumes musical literacy (musical acoustics, arrangement-adjacent content), assume the answer may be no until confirmed in writing. Ask this first — everything else is moot if the answer is that a music degree is required.
programs.totalCostEstimate: ~€11,400 tuition for the 1.5-year full-time master's, plus ~€4,600 if the preparatory language course is required, plus Plovdiv living costs (UNVERIFIED) and a few hundred euro in exam/recognition/translation fees. So roughly €16,000 in fees before living costs.
programs.recommendation: CHEAPER THAN SOFIA BUT STILL SELF-PAY, AND TOO MANY UNKNOWNS TO RANK YET. Substantively this is a proper studio-craft sound-engineering master's — recording, acoustics, psychoacoustics, synthesis, multimedia post-production — and at 1.5 years it is shorter and €900/yr cheaper than the Sofia equivalent, in a much cheaper city. But four critical facts are simply not published: whether a music bachelor's is required, what the entrance exam is, whether a portfolio is demanded, and the Bulgarian-language requirement. He must email the Учебен отдел (gergina.nedelcheva@artacademyplovdiv.com) with exactly those four questions before spending any more time on it. Also note the Bulgarian diploma-recognition procedure is a prerequisite to applying, not a formality — start it a year ahead. Do not treat this as a funded option: there is no scholarship route open to a Tunisian national.

programs.qualification: ОКС „магистър" — genuine state-recognised second-cycle Master's degree; supports a student residence permit for a non-EU national.

programs.whatYouStudy: Music journalism; music arrangement; contemporary music culture; media methodology; radio and television practice; sound technology; audio editing; history of pop and jazz music; rhetoric and speech technique; music-and-media studies; advertising. Practical training covers reporter equipment and sound-engineering work in broadcast and recording studios, plus the music-editing software used in media, and preparing live music broadcasts. Career targets: music editor in media, music arranger for concerts and shows, music producer, music publisher.

programs.tuitionNonEU: €7,600 per academic year, full-time — the academy-wide non-EU master's-after-bachelor's rate that he would pay as a Tunisian national (Rector's Order РД-16-366/05.06.2026). Because the programme is one year, total tuition is €7,600. Part-time €4,200/yr exists but part-time study generally will not support a student residence permit.
programs.otherFees: Candidate exam fee €24–€40; diploma recognition, translation and legalisation costs (UNVERIFIED); Plovdiv living costs additional.
programs.scholarships: None available to a Tunisian national. ПМС 103/228 channels require Bulgarian origin or North Macedonian citizenship. Ask the Bulgarian Embassy in Tunis about any bilateral Tunisia–Bulgaria places.
programs.applicationOpens: Published annually, varies by specialty. Foreign-channel exams for 2026/27 were on 10 September 2026. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — ask uchebenotdel@artacademyplovdiv.com. Allow six months ahead for diploma recognition.
programs.visaEligible: Yes, via the Art. 95(8) foreign-student channel and MES Certificate of Acceptance.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED. Not published. Given the arranging and music-journalism content, musical literacy is likely assumed even if a music degree is not formally demanded.

The cheapest total-tuition figure of any real master's found in this slice — but only because it is one year, and only if he already speaks Bulgarian.
programs.recommendation: NOT RECOMMENDED FOR HIM, RECORDED FOR COMPLETENESS. On paper the €7,600 single-year cost is the lowest total in this sweep and the syllabus does touch studio sound engineering and music production. But the core of the degree is Bulgarian-language music journalism, radio presentation, rhetoric and speech technique — it trains a radio music editor, not a producer or sound designer, and it is the one programme here where the language barrier is not merely an obstacle but the actual subject matter. A Tunisian with working English and no Bulgarian cannot succeed in it. Include it only so he can see it and rule it out knowingly. If he ever wants a Plovdiv option, Тонрежисура at the same academy is the right one.

Which schedule governs a jointly-delivered programme is UNVERIFIED — ask NMA's ТКДФ office, since documents are submitted there. Moot in practice, as he is not eligible to apply.

A Tunisian software-engineering graduate cannot qualify, now or after a portfolio year. The only theoretical path in would be to first complete the AMTII Тонрежисура master's and then this one — a five-year, ~€25k sequence that makes no sense. programs.program: Arta sunetului de film (The Art of Film Sound), studii universitare de masterat
programs.institution: Universitatea Națională de Artă Teatrală și Cinematografică „I.L. Caragiale" București (UNATC), Facultatea de Film
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. State university under the Romanian Ministry of Education; it has state-budget-funded places ("locuri la buget") allocated by the Ministry, its fees are set by Senate decision published on the .ro institutional domain (Hotărârea Senatului nr. 290/2026), and it is ARACIS-accredited. Rector Prof.univ.dr. Liviu Lucaci.
programs.institutionType: Film and theatre university (state)
programs.qualification: Diplomă de master — a genuine, state-recognised second-cycle degree (ciclul II, studii universitare de masterat) under Romanian law. Supports a student residence permit for a non-EU national via the Ministry of Education Letter of Acceptance route.
programs.accreditationStatus: ARACIS-accredited state university; the programme is listed in the official 2026 admissions site and in the Senate fee schedule as a Faculty of Film master's programme.
programs.focus: Film sound design and post-production
programs.whatYouStudy: Film sound as an art form: sound design, recording, editing and post-production for cinema, worked through DAW projects. The admission exam itself tests "film culture and sound design technical knowledge", and candidates must present a DAW session from their own work in one of Avid Pro Tools, Steinberg Nuendo, Cockos Reaper, Adobe Audition, Adobe Premiere Pro or Fairlight/DaVinci Resolve — which indicates the professional toolchain taught.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 ECTS, full-time (cu frecvență).
programs.language: Romanian. This is not an English-taught programme. (UNATC's Faculty of Film does run separate English-taught masters — Design for New Media, Visual Effects, Audiovisual Preservation and Programming, Interactive Technologies for Performing and Media Arts, Art of Game Design — but Arta sunetului de film is not among them.)
programs.languageRequirement: For non-EU applicants: either completion of the Romanian-language preparatory year, or a certificate/attestation of Romanian linguistic competence of MINIMUM B1 level per the CEFR, issued by an accredited Romanian institution. Romanian national rules require at least 6 months of preparatory Romanian for master's-level entrants who cannot prove competence. No IELTS/TOEFL requirement — English tests are irrelevant here, which cuts both ways for him.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree (diplomă de licență) or equivalent, any field on the face of the published rules. Non-EU applicants apply through UNATC's dedicated "Admiterea cetățeni străini – Facultatea de Film – Masterat" route, uploading documents to the 2BitsEDU platform, and must obtain a Ministry of Education Letter of Acceptance. Minimum admission mark 6.00/10 for both budget and fee-paying places.
programs.auditionSpec: Single-stage evaluation in two parts: (1) a WRITTEN test on film culture and technical sound-design knowledge; (2) an ORAL exam built on a portfolio work of the candidate's choosing, at which he must present the actual DAW project file. Both in Romanian.
programs.portfolioSpec: MANDATORY AND SUBSTANTIAL — this is the binding constraint for him. Required: a Europass CV plus a portfolio of artistic works demonstrating sound-design work (digital copies of films or relevant sound-design projects), AND at the oral exam an openable DAW session file from one portfolio piece in Pro Tools, Nuendo, Reaper, Audition, Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve/Fairlight. He currently has none of this. Building it is a 12-month project in its own right and should start now — specifically, sound-designing short films rather than producing club tracks, because the portfolio must show film sound work.
programs.equipmentRequired: A working DAW project in one of the six named applications, which he must be able to open and discuss at the oral exam. Practically: a laptop and a licence for one of Pro Tools, Nuendo, Reaper (cheapest), Audition, Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve (free tier includes Fairlight).
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED — no published studio inventory found on the admissions site. UNATC is Romania's national film school with production facilities; ask the Faculty of Film secretariat for a facilities list and studio-access policy for master's students.
programs.tuitionEU: 13,750 lei per academic year for fee-paying places, per Hotărârea Senatului nr. 290/2026, Annex II.2 (Faculty of Film). Budget-funded (free) places exist but are contested and effectively reserved in practice for Romanian/EU candidates.
programs.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED — and this is a material gap. The Senate fee schedule (Hotărârea 290/2026) contains NO figure for non-EU students studying "pe cont propriu valutar"; the words valutar, euro and străin do not appear in it. Romanian non-EU tuition is set per institution above a Government-Ordinance 22/2009 minimum and is normally quoted in EUR per month. For calibration, comparable Romanian arts faculties charge in the €750–950/month range (e.g. UBB Cluj Faculty of Theatre and Film 2026-27: €750/month for theatre, €950/month for cinematography and media, payable 9 months a year). DO NOT assume the 13,750 lei figure applies to him — it almost certainly does not. Ask UNATC's international/admissions office in writing for the euro rate for a non-EU master's student in Arta sunetului de film.
programs.otherFees: Admission fee payable online at registration (amount in the separate "TAXE ADMITERE 2026-2027" annex — UNVERIFIED). Document legalisation/translation and Ministry Letter of Acceptance processing costs additional. Bucharest living costs additional (UNVERIFIED — no official figure).
programs.scholarships: Two real Romanian government routes exist for a Tunisian national, both programme-agnostic and both requiring Romanian-language study: (1) MFA/Romanian Government Scholarships via studyinromania.gov.ro — applications to about 31 March, results about 15 July, open to non-EU citizens, requires a study-years average of at least 7/10, excludes medicine/dentistry/pharmacy, and beneficiaries at bachelor's and master's level STUDY ONLY IN ROMANIAN with a preparatory Romanian year granted to non-speakers. (2) ARICE scholarships (Romanian Agency for Investments and Foreign Trade with the Ministry of Education) — for 2026-27 documents were emailed 11 May – 12 June to burse@arice.gov.ro, for accredited state institutions. Both are plausible for this programme precisely because it is Romanian-taught and at a state university. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates for the 2027 intake.
programs.applicationOpens: Online registration 4 August 2026 (2026-27 cycle). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Non-EU candidates must start much earlier because of the Ministry Letter of Acceptance.
programs.deadline: Registration closed 9 September 2026 with admission tests 15–20 September 2026 (2026-27 cycle). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For a September 2027 start, expect a similar August–September 2027 window, but the Romanian Government Scholarship deadline is far earlier — about 31 March 2027.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. UNATC operates a published non-EU admission route for Faculty of Film master's programmes; the Ministry of Education issues a Letter of Acceptance, which supports the Romanian long-stay study visa and student residence permit.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes in principle — the published requirement is a bachelor's degree or equivalent with no field restriction, and there is no music-degree clause. His BSc Software Engineering is acceptable as the academic qualification. The barrier is not his degree; it is the portfolio and the Romanian language.
programs.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED pending the non-EU euro rate. If UNATC charges in the €750–950/month band typical of Romanian arts faculties, budget roughly €6,750–8,550 per year × 2 years, plus a Romanian preparatory year if he cannot certify B1, plus Bucharest living costs. If he wins a Romanian Government or ARICE scholarship, tuition and the preparatory year are covered and the figure collapses to near zero.
programs.recommendation: THE STRONGEST FUNDED PROSPECT IN THIS SLICE — BUT ONLY IF HE COMMITS TO ROMANIAN AND BUILDS A FILM-SOUND PORTFOLIO. Unlike Bulgaria, Romania actually has a government scholarship a Tunisian national can win (MFA/studyinromania and ARICE), it is open to master's level, it covers a Romanian preparatory year, and it is not restricted to particular fields beyond excluding medicine. That converts an otherwise unaffordable degree into a potentially fully-funded one. The programme itself is the real thing: 2 years, 120 ECTS, at Romania's national film school, taught on a professional DAW toolchain. Two hard conditions. First, the scholarship demands a study-years average of at least 7/10 — he must check his SMU MedTech transcript converts above that. Second, the entrance exam requires a portfolio of FILM SOUND work plus a live DAW session walkthrough, in Romanian. That means his portfolio year should be spent sound-designing short films, not only making DJ tracks — a genuine redirection of effort from what he currently plans. Action now: (a) verify his GPA converts to ≥7/10; (b) start Romanian; (c) email UNATC for the non-EU euro tuition rate; (d) begin collaborating with student filmmakers to accumulate film-sound credits. Deadline discipline matters — the scholarship closes around 31 March 2027, five months before the university's own admission window.

programs.program: Design, lumină și sunet în artele spectacolului (Design, Light and Sound in the Performing Arts), studii universitare de masterat
programs.institution: Universitatea Națională de Artă Teatrală și Cinematografică „I.L. Caragiale" București (UNATC), Facultatea de Teatru
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. State university under the Romanian Ministry of Education, ARACIS-accredited, with Ministry-allocated budget places and fees set by published Senate decision (Hotărârea Senatului nr. 290/2026).
programs.institutionType: Film and theatre university (state) — this programme sits in the Theatre Faculty, not the Film Faculty
programs.qualification: Diplomă de master — genuine state-recognised second-cycle degree (ciclul II). Supports a non-EU student residence permit via the Ministry Letter of Acceptance route.
programs.accreditationStatus: ARACIS-accredited state university; programme published on the official 2026 admissions site and in the Senate fee schedule (Annex II.1, Faculty of Theatre). UNATC describes it as "unicul program de studii din România" — the only programme of its kind in Romania.
programs.focus: Live sound design and lighting design for performing arts
programs.whatYouStudy: Training of light designers and sound designers for the performing arts. Covers lighting and sound design concepts for stage — the written entrance exam is explicitly on lighting and sound design concepts, and the portfolio must be a personal artistic project in performing arts sound and/or lighting.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 ECTS, full-time (cu frecvență).
programs.language: Romanian.
programs.languageRequirement: For non-EU applicants: Romanian-language preparatory year, or a certificate of Romanian linguistic competence of at least B1 (CEFR) from an accredited Romanian institution. Romanian national rules require at least 6 months preparatory Romanian at master's level absent proof of competence. No IELTS/TOEFL relevance.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree (licență) or equivalent — no field restriction published, so a BSc Software Engineering is acceptable as the academic qualification. Non-EU applicants go through UNATC's foreign-citizen route with a Ministry of Education Letter of Acceptance. Minimum admission mark 6.00/10.
programs.auditionSpec: Two components: (1) a 15-minute portfolio interview, graded 1–10; (2) a 3-hour WRITTEN examination on lighting and sound design concepts, graded 1–10. Minimum pass 6.00. Conducted in Romanian.
programs.portfolioSpec: MANDATORY. A personal artistic project in the performing arts (sound and/or lighting), accompanied by a written theoretical argument of 3–5 typed pages, plus supporting materials demonstrating artistic relevance. Note the required work is THEATRE/PERFORMANCE sound or light — not club music, not film. He has none of this and would need to build it by working on student theatre productions.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — not published. The written exam is theoretical; the portfolio is documentation-based.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED — no published inventory. UNATC has theatre venues and technical stages; ask the Faculty of Theatre secretariat.
programs.tuitionEU: 8,000 lei per academic year for fee-paying places, per Hotărârea Senatului nr. 290/2026, Annex II.1 (Faculty of Theatre). Notably cheaper than the Film Faculty's 13,750 lei.
programs.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED. The Senate fee decision contains no non-EU/valutar rate — the words valutar, euro and străin do not appear in it. For calibration, UBB Cluj's Faculty of Theatre and Film charges non-EU students €750/month (theatre domain) for 2026-27, payable 9 months a year. Do NOT assume 8,000 lei applies to him. Ask UNATC's international office in writing for the euro rate.
programs.otherFees: Admission fee payable at online registration (amount in the separate TAXE ADMITERE annex — UNVERIFIED). Legalisation, translation and Letter of Acceptance costs additional. Bucharest living costs additional (UNVERIFIED).
programs.scholarships: Same two Romanian government routes as above and both apply here: (1) Romanian Government/MFA scholarships via scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro — deadline about 31 March, results about 15 July, non-EU citizens, minimum study-years average 7/10, bachelor's and master's beneficiaries study ONLY in Romanian with a preparatory Romanian year granted; (2) ARICE scholarships with the Ministry of Education, documents by email in the May–June window. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates. Also note only 3 budget-funded and 3 fee-paying places exist in total, which makes any route into this programme highly competitive.
programs.applicationOpens: 4 August 2026 (2026-27 cycle). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.deadline: 9 September 2026 (2026-27 cycle). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Scholarship deadlines are much earlier — about 31 March.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — via UNATC's foreign-citizen admission route and the Ministry of Education Letter of Acceptance, which supports the Romanian long-stay study visa and student residence permit.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — a licență in any field is accepted, with no music-degree clause. The obstacle is the performing-arts portfolio and the Romanian-language written exam, not his degree.
programs.totalCostEstimate: UNVERIFIED pending the non-EU euro rate; if it tracks the Romanian arts norm of roughly €750/month over 9 months, budget around €6,750/year × 2 years, plus a preparatory Romanian year if needed, plus Bucharest living costs. Fully covered if he wins a Romanian Government or ARICE scholarship.
programs.recommendation: A REAL BUT NARROW OPTION — WORSE FIT THAN THE FILM SOUND MA AT THE SAME UNIVERSITY. It is a genuine, accredited, 120-ECTS master's in sound design, the only one of its kind in Romania, at half the Film Faculty's domestic tuition, and it is eligible for the same Romanian government scholarships. But three things count against it for him. First, it is half lighting design — a field he has expressed no interest in and will be examined on in a 3-hour written paper. Second, the portfolio must be a live performing-arts project with a 3–5 page theoretical argument, which is further from club music and electronic production than film sound is. Third, and most seriously, there are only 6 places in total (3 budget, 3 fee), making it a lottery. Treat it as a second UNATC application submitted alongside Arta sunetului de film rather than as a primary target — the same Romanian-language investment and the same scholarship application serve both, so listing it costs him little. If he applies, he must build stage-sound credits with a student theatre company, not only studio work.

programs.program: Digital Interactive Arts (Arte digitale interactive), MA
programs.institution: Universitatea Babeș-Bolyai din Cluj-Napoca (UBB), Facultatea de Teatru și Film — Departamentul de Cinematografie și Media
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Romania's largest state university, ARACIS-accredited, Ministry-funded with state budget places; its fee schedules are adopted by Senate decision and published on ubbcluj.ro (Regulament privind taxele 2026-2027, Annex 4).
programs.institutionType: Comprehensive state university (Faculty of Theatre and Film)
programs.qualification: Diplomă de master — genuine state-recognised second-cycle degree (ciclul II). Supports a non-EU student residence permit via the Ministry of Education Letter of Acceptance.
programs.accreditationStatus: ARACIS-accredited state university; programme published on the official faculty site as one of three English-taught master's programmes in the Cinematography and Media department.
programs.focus: Digital interactive arts / new media, with a sound design elective
programs.whatYouStudy: Interactive technologies and digital art practice. Relevant to him: the curriculum includes an elective "Sound Design for Digital Media (opt.4)" covering sound design for the media field and multi-channel digital sound projects with multimedia applications. Be clear-eyed: sound is ONE ELECTIVE, not the spine of the degree. The programme's centre of gravity is interactive digital art, not audio.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters (2 years), full-time. Total ECTS not stated on the programme page — UNVERIFIED; a Romanian 2-year master's is normally 120 ECTS. Confirm with the faculty.
programs.language: ENGLISH. Stated on the official programme page: "Teaching language: English". This is the ONLY English-taught programme with meaningful sound content found anywhere in Hungary, Romania or Bulgaria in this sweep.
programs.languageRequirement: English. The specific certificate and band demanded are UNVERIFIED — not published on the programme page. He has not yet taken IELTS or TOEFL, so this must be established early: email constantin.parvulescu@ubbcluj.ro or the faculty secretariat (+40 264 590 066 / +40 264 405 357) and ask what English evidence is required for a non-EU applicant and whether the university accepts alternatives. No Romanian-language requirement applies to an English-taught programme — Romanian national rules exempt students on foreign-language programmes from the preparatory year, which removes a full year and a major barrier.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree; no field restriction published, and the selection is built on the artistic project and portfolio rather than on a prior arts degree. Non-EU applicants apply through UBB's Centrul de Cooperări Internaționale with a Ministry of Education Letter of Acceptance.
programs.auditionSpec: Oral examination assessing (a) ability to articulate the relevance and significance of the proposed digital art project and (b) demonstrated knowledge of the specific characteristics of artistic production. Conducted in English.
programs.portfolioSpec: MANDATORY, TWO PARTS: (1) an individual artistic project demonstrating interest in interactive technologies, and (2) a portfolio of artistic works. The application is only considered complete on confirmed receipt of BOTH. Critically, the project can be proposed rather than completed — the oral exam tests whether he can argue its relevance. For a software engineer this is the most reachable portfolio requirement in the whole sweep: an interactive audio-visual project (a generative music system, a reactive installation, an audio plugin, a game-audio prototype) plays directly to his existing coding skills rather than requiring conservatoire craft he does not have.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — not published. Assume a personal laptop.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED — no published inventory. Ask Prof. dr. Rodica Mocan (programme contact for Digital Interactive Arts) what studio, lab and multi-channel audio facilities master's students can access.
programs.tuitionEU: Romanian/EU fee-paying and budget places per UBB's domestic schedule — figure UNVERIFIED for this programme; see ubbcluj.ro/ro/taxe.
programs.tuitionNonEU: €950 per MONTH — the rate for the Faculty of Theatre and Film, domain "cinematografie și media", for citizens of non-EU/non-EEA/non-Swiss states studying "pe cont propriu valutar" in 2026-2027, per UBB Senate Regulation Annex 4. Fees are payable for 9 months of the academic year (10 months where the curriculum has a distinct practice period), so approximately €8,550 per year, or about €17,100 over two years. THIS IS THE RATE HE WOULD PAY as a Tunisian national. Note the neighbouring "teatru și artele spectacolului" domain is cheaper at €750/month — confirm in writing which domain Digital Interactive Arts is charged under, as the difference is €1,800/year.
programs.otherFees: €50 non-refundable admission dossier processing fee for non-EU applicants, regardless of study level (UBB Senate Regulation art. 15.1). Tuition excludes accommodation and meals. Document legalisation, translation and Letter of Acceptance costs additional. Cluj-Napoca living costs additional (UNVERIFIED).
programs.scholarships: The Romanian Government/MFA scholarship route (scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro, deadline about 31 March, minimum 7/10 study average) is open to non-EU nationals at master's level — BUT with a critical catch for this programme: MFA scholarship beneficiaries at bachelor's and master's level "study only in Romanian", with only doctoral holders permitted a foreign language. That rule appears to exclude an English-taught master's from MFA funding. ARICE scholarships may operate differently — verify. So the very feature that makes this programme accessible (English) may disqualify it from the main Romanian scholarship. CONFIRM directly with studyinromania.gov.ro before assuming either way; this single question determines whether the programme is a €17,100 self-pay or a funded option.
programs.applicationOpens: Application 13–17 July 2026; exam 24 July 2026; final results 30 July 2026 (2026-27 cycle). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Non-EU applicants must start far earlier for the Letter of Acceptance.
programs.deadline: 17 July 2026 for the 2026-27 cycle. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For a September 2027 start expect a July 2027 window, with the Ministry Letter of Acceptance process beginning several months earlier.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — UBB admits non-EU students on the "cont propriu valutar" basis through its Centrul de Cooperări Internaționale, with a Ministry of Education Letter of Acceptance supporting the Romanian long-stay study visa and student residence permit.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, and it is the best structural fit for his actual background. No music degree, no conservatoire training and no instrumental audition are required. Selection turns on an interactive-technology artistic project — which a software engineering graduate is unusually well placed to produce. This is the one programme in the sweep where his BSc is an asset rather than an anomaly.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Roughly €17,100 in tuition over two years (€950/month × 9 months × 2), plus the €50 application fee, plus Cluj-Napoca living costs (UNVERIFIED — no official figure), plus IELTS/TOEFL costs. No preparatory language year needed, which saves a year of both time and money relative to every Romanian-taught option.
programs.recommendation: THE BEST OVERALL FIT IN THIS THREE-COUNTRY SLICE, WITH ONE UNRESOLVED FUNDING QUESTION. It is the only English-taught programme found in Hungary, Romania or Bulgaria with real sound content; it needs no preparatory language year; its selection criteria reward exactly what he has (coding, interactive systems) rather than what he lacks (conservatoire training, instrumental skill); and the artistic project can be proposed rather than already built, which suits someone starting a portfolio from zero. Be honest about the trade-off: sound design is one elective, not the degree. If his goal is to become a working sound designer this is thinner than UNATC's film-sound MA; if his goal is to become a producer/DJ with a technical creative practice and an EU degree that gets him residence, this is the most winnable route. Three actions in order of priority: (1) ask studyinromania.gov.ro whether an English-taught master's can be MFA-funded — if yes, this becomes a funded first choice, if no, it is a €17,100 self-pay decision; (2) ask the faculty which fee domain applies (€950 vs €750/month) and what English certificate is required; (3) spend the portfolio year building ONE strong interactive audio project with documentation, not a scattering of tracks.
