programs.program: Sound Design — szakirányú továbbképzés (postgraduate specialist training). WARNING: THIS IS NOT A MASTER'S DEGREE.
programs.institution: Moholy-Nagy Művészeti Egyetem (MOME) / Moholy-Nagy University of Art and Design
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC-FOUNDATION ("közfeladatot ellátó közérdekű vagyonkezelő alapítvány" model). MOME is a state-recognised Hungarian university of art and design, formerly directly state-run, now maintained by a public-interest asset management foundation under the 2021 Hungarian model — this is the ambiguity flagged in the brief. It is NOT a private company or church institution, it is state-recognised and appears in the Hungarian higher-education register, and it hosts Stipendium Hungaricum places on its degree programmes. But it is no longer a directly state-maintained institution either, and its fees are set commercially.
programs.institutionType: University of art and design
programs.qualification: NOT A MASTER'S DEGREE. The award is explicitly "Specialist training" (szakirányú továbbképzés) — a Hungarian post-bachelor specialist qualification that requires a prior degree to enter but does NOT confer a mesterfokozat (second-cycle master's degree) and does not carry 120 ECTS. It is a legitimate, accredited Hungarian qualification, not a fake, but it is NOT a second-cycle degree and will not be treated as a master's for further study or for most immigration purposes.
programs.accreditationStatus: A genuine accredited Hungarian szakirányú továbbképzés at a state-recognised university — so not a diploma mill. But it sits outside the Bologna second cycle. Anyone reading the English page, which markets it under "Programmes" alongside MA courses, could easily mistake it for a master's. It is not one.
programs.focus: Sound design for film, games and spatial audio
programs.whatYouStudy: Sound design and sound art with a complex, cross-disciplinary view; collaboration with film and video game work. Students must complete three practical projects — a film sound project, a game sound project, and a spatial sound composition project — which together form a sound-design portfolio. Broad grounding in sound-design theory and technology and creative handling of the relevant software. Led by sound artist Ádám Krasz (director of MOME TechPark) and Csaba Hajnóczy DLA.
programs.durationEcts: 1 year / 2 semesters. Delivered as a NIGHT COURSE ("Night course" on MOME's own English page; designed to be completed alongside employment). ECTS not published — UNVERIFIED. Being part-time evening study is itself disqualifying for a study residence permit in most cases.
programs.language: HUNGARIAN. MOME's own English-language programme page states "Language: Hungarian". There is no English track. All teaching, the application documents and the interview are in Hungarian.
programs.languageRequirement: Hungarian. No formal certificate level is published — UNVERIFIED — but the motivation letter, CV and interview are conducted in Hungarian, so functional Hungarian is required in practice. IELTS/TOEFL are irrelevant and will not help him.
programs.entryRequirements: A completed bachelor's, master's, or university/college-level degree ("Alap- vagy mesterfokozat, illetve egyetemi vagy főiskolai szintű végzettség") — so his BSc would satisfy the degree condition. BUT he must also already have: knowledge of sound design and music-theory fundamentals, and working knowledge of Pro Tools and Ableton at basic level. Plus a professional portfolio.
programs.auditionSpec: Three stages: (1) online application form; (2) upload of documents; (3) admission interview. For the 2026 intake the interviews were held 3–4 September 2026, and only the strongest applicants on the strength of motivation letters and portfolios were invited. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates.
programs.portfolioSpec: MANDATORY. Required uploads: a motivation letter (max 1 A4 page), a CV, a PROFESSIONAL PORTFOLIO of existing work — explicitly a showreel or previous musical works, maximum 100 MB — and a scanned copy of the degree certificate. He currently has no portfolio, so he could not apply today.
programs.equipmentRequired: Basic working knowledge of Pro Tools and Ableton Live is an explicit entry requirement, so access to and competence in both is assumed on day one.
programs.facilities: MOME operates the MOME Sonic Studio and a Spatial Experimentation Studio, and the programme is run out of MOME TechPark — genuinely strong spatial-audio facilities by regional standards. No published equipment inventory. Partly UNVERIFIED.
programs.tuitionEU: 790,000 HUF per semester, self-funded (önköltséges) — so 1,580,000 HUF for the full 2-semester course. Roughly €4,000 at prevailing rates, but do not rely on that conversion; the published figure is in forint.
programs.tuitionNonEU: The SAME 790,000 HUF/semester — MOME publishes a single self-funded rate with no separate international tier for this course. So the rate he would pay as a Tunisian national is 790,000 HUF × 2 semesters = 1,580,000 HUF. Note this does not make it accessible: the barrier is language and immigration status, not price tiering.
programs.otherFees: A non-refundable special procedure fee of 5,000 HUF per application; failure to pay excludes the applicant from the admission procedure entirely.
programs.scholarships: NONE. Critically, Stipendium Hungaricum does NOT fund this. Tunisia IS an eligible Stipendium Hungaricum sending partner (the Tunisian Republic is named in the official 2026/27 Call for Applications, with the Ministère de l'Enseignement Supérieur as sending partner, deadline 15 January, stipend HUF 43,700/month plus HUF 40,000/month accommodation contribution plus tuition waiver and medical insurance) — but the Call restricts postgraduate specialist training courses and partial study to particular frameworks, and applicants may only apply for the study fields fixed in the bilateral educational cooperation programme between Hungary and Tunisia. A Hungarian-taught, part-time, non-degree evening course is not a realistic Stipendium Hungaricum target. Check the Tunisia entry at stipendiumhungaricum.hu/partners/ for the exact fields agreed with Tunisia.
programs.intakes: September (course started 14 September 2026 for the 2026 cohort). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.applicationOpens: Application form deadline 24 August 2026; document upload deadline 27 August 2026; interviews 3–4 September 2026. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates.
programs.deadline: 24 August 2026 for the 2026 intake. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.visaEligible: ALMOST CERTAINLY NOT. Two independent problems: (1) it is a szakirányú továbbképzés, not a degree programme; (2) it is delivered as a part-time night course, and Hungarian study residence permits generally require full-time enrolment in a degree programme. Do not apply for this expecting it to produce a student residence permit. If he wants certainty, ask MOME's international office in writing whether the course issues the enrolment certificate accepted by the National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing — but expect the answer to be no.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Degree-wise yes — any bachelor's satisfies the formal entry condition, and no music degree is named. But the SUBSTANTIVE prerequisites exclude him today: he must already know sound design and music-theory fundamentals, already work in Pro Tools and Ableton, and already have a professional showreel or body of musical work. This is a course for people who are already practising, designed to specialise them further.
programs.totalCostEstimate: 1,580,000 HUF tuition plus 5,000 HUF application fee, plus Budapest living costs, plus whatever it costs to reach functional Hungarian. In practice not a viable expenditure for him.
programs.recommendation: DO NOT PURSUE — INCLUDED SPECIFICALLY AS A TRAP TO RULE OUT. This will surface prominently in any search he runs: it is marketed in English, on a well-known university's site, under a menu called "Programmes", was launched with press coverage as "Hungary's first accredited degree-granting sound design programme", and covers exactly his interests (film sound, game audio, spatial composition) with genuinely good facilities. It is nonetheless wrong for him on four independent grounds, any one of which is fatal: (1) it is NOT a master's degree — the award is 'Specialist training', outside the Bologna second cycle; (2) it is taught entirely in HUNGARIAN, with a Hungarian-language interview; (3) it is a part-time NIGHT COURSE and so will almost certainly not support a student residence permit for a Tunisian national; (4) it requires an existing professional showreel plus working Pro Tools and Ableton skills he does not yet have. There is also no funding: Stipendium Hungaricum, for which Tunisia IS eligible, will not cover a Hungarian-taught non-degree evening course. He should look at MOME only for its full MA programmes, and note that MOME's Média design MA is likewise not offered in English, and that Budapest Metropolitan University's Media Design MA states plainly "We do not offer this course in English".

programs.program: Regie muzicală (Music Directing / Sound Direction) — studii postuniversitare. WARNING: THIS IS NOT A MASTER'S DEGREE.
programs.institution: Universitatea Națională de Muzică din București (UNMB) / National University of Music Bucharest
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. State university of music, functioning as a public university since 2001, under the Romanian Ministry of Education; the certificate it issues is co-issued by the Ministry of Education and UNMB, which itself confirms state status.
programs.institutionType: Music university (state conservatoire)
programs.qualification: NOT A MASTER'S DEGREE. The award is a "certificat de competență profesională" (professional competency certificate) for the occupation of music director, C.O.R. code 265228, issued by the Ministry of Education and UNMB. It is officially inscribed in the National Registry of Postgraduate Programmes — so it is a real, state-registered qualification and NOT a scam — but it is a postgraduate professional certificate, not a second-cycle (ciclul II) degree, and confers no master's.
programs.accreditationStatus: Genuine and state-registered (National Registry of Postgraduate Programmes; Ministry-issued certificate). But categorically outside the Bologna second cycle. This is exactly the category the brief warns about: a real institution selling a real but non-degree postgraduate award that reads like a master's in the field he is searching.
programs.focus: Music directing / sound direction (tonmeister-style)
programs.whatYouStudy: Music direction (regie muzicală) — the classical Romanian tonmeister discipline. Detailed syllabus not published on the page checked — UNVERIFIED. The entrance exam content (melodic dictation, transposing-instrument notation, timbral hearing, instrument recognition) shows the discipline is built on classical-music aural skill, not electronic production.
programs.durationEcts: 146 contact hours, 15 ECTS. For scale: a genuine Romanian master's is 120 ECTS over two years. At 15 ECTS this is one-eighth of a master's — it is a short professional course.
programs.language: Romanian. Explicitly stated: instruction is delivered in Romanian.
programs.languageRequirement: Not separately published — UNVERIFIED — but as teaching is in Romanian, Romanian competence is required in practice. Ask UNMB. No IELTS/TOEFL relevance.
programs.entryRequirements: A bachelor's degree or equivalent. No music degree is formally named, but see the entrance exam — it assumes conservatoire-level aural training.
programs.auditionSpec: DISQUALIFYING FOR THIS CANDIDATE. Two parts: (1) a WRITTEN test covering melodic dictation and notation of transposing instruments; (2) an ORAL examination assessing timbral hearing and instrument recognition. Melodic dictation and transposing-instrument notation are skills acquired over years of formal solfège training. Someone with no conservatoire background and no music degree cannot pass this within a year of self-study.
programs.portfolioSpec: None specified — the gate is the aural-skills examination, not a portfolio.
programs.equipmentRequired: UNVERIFIED — not published.
programs.facilities: UNMB operates a Centre for Electronic Music and studio facilities, and runs a separate optional module "Producție Muzicală în Studioul de Muzică Electronică" (Music Production in the Electronic Music Studio) for its own students. Facilities inventory UNVERIFIED.
programs.tuitionEU: 8,000 lei for Romanian participants, payable in three instalments.
programs.tuitionNonEU: €1,600 for international participants, payable in three instalments. This IS the rate he would pay as a Tunisian national, and it is explicitly published as the international rate — one of the few places in this sweep where a distinct non-EU figure is actually stated. It is cheap because the course is short and non-degree, not because it is good value for him.
programs.otherFees: 100 RON registration fee plus 150 RON enrolment fee.
programs.scholarships: None. Romanian Government/MFA and ARICE scholarships fund bachelor's, master's and doctoral study at accredited institutions — a 15-ECTS postgraduate certificate is not a study cycle and would not be covered. Do not expect funding.
programs.intakes: UNVERIFIED — not published on the page checked. Ask UNMB's postgraduate studies office.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — not published. Ask UNMB.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — not published. Ask UNMB's Studii Postuniversitare office.
programs.visaEligible: ALMOST CERTAINLY NOT. A 146-hour, 15-ECTS postgraduate certificate is not a degree programme and will not support a Romanian long-stay study visa or student residence permit for a third-country national. Romania's Letter of Acceptance machinery is built around bachelor's, master's and doctoral study cycles. Do not plan a move to Romania around this.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO in practice. Although the formal condition is only a bachelor's degree, the entrance examination requires melodic dictation, notation of transposing instruments, and aural instrument/timbre recognition — conservatoire skills. Without a music background he would fail the exam.
programs.totalCostEstimate: €1,600 tuition plus 250 RON in fees, plus Bucharest living costs for the duration. Irrelevant in practice, because it neither confers a degree nor supports a residence permit.
programs.recommendation: DO NOT PURSUE — RECORDED AS A TRAP. Searching 'music direction Romania master' or 'regie muzicală' will lead him straight here, at Romania's national music university, at an apparently affordable €1,600 for international students. It is not a master's degree. It is a 146-hour, 15-ECTS professional certificate — one-eighth the volume of a real second-cycle degree — it will not support a student residence permit, it is taught in Romanian, and its entrance exam (melodic dictation, transposing-instrument notation, timbral hearing) is a conservatoire aural test he cannot pass without years of solfège training. The low price is a signal of what it is, not a bargain. Note also that UNMB's actual master's portfolio contains NO sound-technology programme at all: the Faculty of Composition, Musicology and Music Pedagogy offers only Stil și limbaj compozițional, Sinteză muzicologică, Stilistică dirijorală, Jazz și culturi muzicale pop, Educație muzicală contemporană and Culturi muzicale religioase, and the Faculty of Musical Interpretation offers only performance-stylistics masters. UNMB is therefore a dead end for him and should be closed off entirely.
programs.sourceUrl: https://www.unmb.ro/oferta-educationala/studii-postuniversitare/regie-muzicala/ (official UNMB postgraduate programme page: postgraduate status, 146 hours, 15 ECTS, exam content, 8,000 lei / €1,600 fees, Romanian instruction, C.O.R. 265228 certificate) and https://www.unmb.ro/admitere/ (official UNMB admissions page listing the actual master's programmes, none sound-related)

programs.program: Master of Music – main subject Electronic Music Performance (EMP), Jazz department
programs.institution: Conservatorium Maastricht, Zuyd University of Applied Sciences (Zuyd Hogeschool)
programs.institutionType: Publicly funded university of applied sciences (hbo / hogeschool); Conservatorium Maastricht is the music faculty of Zuyd
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Known because Zuyd is a government-funded (bekostigd) hbo institution: only bekostigde instellingen may charge the wettelijk collegegeld (statutory fee) set by the Ministry of OCW, and Zuyd's own fee tool publishes both a statutory rate (EU/EEA) and an instellingscollegegeld (non-EEA) for the master Muziek. Zuyd also acts as an IND-recognised sponsor - its own admission page states non-European applicants receive a questionnaire around May for the residence-permit application.
programs.qualification: Master of Music (MMus), 120 EC. A real, state-recognised Dutch second-cycle hbo-master, NVAO-accredited, registered in CROHO as 'Muziek' (hbo-master). Supports a Dutch student residence permit for a non-EU national.
programs.accreditationStatus: NVAO-accredited hbo-master 'Muziek' at Zuyd; degree title Master of Music confirmed on the institution's own Fast Facts panel. Full NVAO decision number UNVERIFIED - check the NVAO register (nvao.net) or ask bo.conservatoriummaastricht@zuyd.nl.
programs.language: English. The institution states plainly: 'The programmes of Master of Music are taught in English.'
programs.languageRequirement: English at B2, proven by certificate uploaded by 1 July: IELTS Academic 6.0, or TOEFL iBT 80 (paper 550), or PTE Academic 61, or LanguageCert Academic 65, or TOEIC 865 L&R / 335 S&W, or Cambridge CAE/FCE 169. Exemption if the previous bachelor was fully taught in English. No Dutch required.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years full-time, 120 EC (60 EC per year). Curriculum published per year: Main Subject 29+24 EC, Band & Performing 6+6, Introduction to Studio Recording & Music Production 2+2, Composing & Arranging 2+2, Find Your Own Music 2+2, Tools in Creation 4+4, Current Jazz 2+2, Impro Lab 2+2, Master Research 5+10, Health & Well-being 1+1, Your Art as a Business 3+3, Outreach 2+2, Elective Modules 6+6.
programs.focus: Electronic music production and live performance of it. The programme sits deliberately at the junction of electronic music and jazz: 'Produce music at a professional level and then perform it, in new creative ways, with talented musicians. Making the most of all the possibilities music technology has to offer.'
programs.whatYouStudy: Main subject EMP lessons (production + live performance), band and performing, studio recording and music production, composing and arranging, 'Tools in Creation', improvisation lab, current jazz, plus a two-year artistic Master Research project and 'Your Art as a Business' entrepreneurship. Electives include 'Producing your own music', mixing & mastering, composing & arranging for film/big band/world, conducting & ensemble leading. Teaching staff for EMP include Frederik Tings (music production / live sound & effects), and guest teachers Paul Frick (Brandt Brauer Frick) and Frank Wienk (Binkbeats / Noisia circle).
programs.entryRequirements: A Bachelor's degree in Music, OR 'proof of an equivalent level of knowledge and skills tailored to the programme'. This second clause is the door for a non-music graduate - it is explicit on the official How-to-apply page, and the department also operates a Preparatory Course Master (a bridging year) for applicants who audition below master level. Registration is via Studielink under Zuyd University of Applied Sciences, programme 'Master of Music'. Diploma check via the Zuyd Enrolment Office (enrolmentoffice@zuyd.nl). No audition fee.
programs.auditionSpec: Three stages. (1) Portfolio of unlisted YouTube video links: candidate introduces him/herself in English (max 10 min); THREE own productions in a DAW (originals) - show the entire production and then talk through the tools and techniques used; plus a video of the candidate playing an instrument (jazz skills valued; piano and/or guitar 'a plus'); optionally live-performance footage and notated/arranged scores via a cloud folder. (2) 'Live' audition, may be held online, 20-45 minutes: discussion of the portfolio, presentation of the candidate's vision, demonstration of playing skills on the preferred instrument and on piano, and an ear test. Stated main focus: 'the quality of your writing and your vision'. (3) Master interview (~20 min) with the jazz master coordinator on the Master Research Project - investigative attitude and critical thinking.
programs.portfolioSpec: See auditionSpec: three complete original DAW productions with a spoken walkthrough of technique, plus instrumental playing evidence. This is a portfolio a self-taught producer can genuinely build in a year - but the instrumental/ear-training component is a real barrier for a pure DJ with no keyboard skills.
programs.equipmentRequired: Own DAW and production setup implied for the portfolio (three finished originals). Institutional list of required student equipment UNVERIFIED - ask bo.conservatoriummaastricht@zuyd.nl.
programs.facilities: Studio recording and music production teaching is embedded in the curriculum (Introduction to Studio Recording & Music Production; electives in mixing & mastering and band recording), so studio access exists. Specific studio/control-room specification, immersive-audio rigs and DAW licences UNVERIFIED - ask the Educational Affairs Office, bo.conservatoriummaastricht@zuyd.nl.
programs.intakes: One intake, start of academic year 1 September each year. Introduction days in the last week of August.
programs.applicationOpens: Studielink for the following academic year normally opens in the preceding October. Exact opening date for the Sept-2027 intake UNVERIFIED - PRIOR CYCLE pattern; confirm with enrolmentoffice@zuyd.nl.
programs.deadline: Non-EU candidates: apply before 1 MARCH. (EU candidates before 1 March, with 1 March - 1 May still possible but no guaranteed place.) First-round auditions 15 March - 15 April; second-round auditions 15 May - 15 June. English certificate must be uploaded by 1 July. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: these dates are published without a year on the official How-to-apply page and reflect the current cycle; the September-2027 cycle dates must be re-confirmed with irja.zeper@zuyd.nl (head of programme) from autumn 2026.
programs.tuitionEU: €2,694 per year (wettelijk collegegeld, 2026-2027, full-time master, first Dutch master) per Zuyd's official fee application.
programs.tuitionNonEU: €12,280 PER YEAR - this is the rate a Tunisian national pays. Zuyd's official 2026-2027 tuition application publishes, for the master 'Muziek' / 'Music': wettelijk €2,694 (voltijd) and instelling €12,280 (voltijd). Non-EU/EEA nationals pay the instellingscollegegeld.
programs.otherFees: Studielink registration is free and there is NO audition fee ('you only pay tuition once admitted'). IND residence-permit and MVV charges, health insurance and instrument/equipment costs are additional and UNVERIFIED here - ask enrolmentoffice@zuyd.nl.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition alone: €12,280 x 2 years = €24,560 for the full 120 EC master. Living costs in Maastricht and the IND proof-of-means figure are NOT published on these pages - UNVERIFIED; get the current proof-of-sufficient-means amount from the IND and from Zuyd International.
programs.scholarships: Two that a Tunisian national can realistically win, both named on the official Conservatorium Maastricht funding page: (1) Zuyd Excellence Scholarship - explicitly aimed at students who must pay the institutional tuition fee, i.e. non-EU/EEA students; conditions are that the holder obtains at least 45 of 60 EC each year and works five hours a month as an ambassador for Conservatorium Maastricht. Award amount UNVERIFIED - ask Zuyd International. (2) NL Scholarship (Holland Scholarship), the OCW-funded scheme for non-EEA bachelor/master students, routed through Zuyd International. Also listed: Cultuurfonds grants (€1,000-€20,000, but aimed at study/research abroad) and the Conservatorium Maastricht Foundation for enrolled students. NOTE: nothing here is a full ride - realistic outcome is a partial offset against a €12,280/yr bill.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. Zuyd's own admission page states that non-European applicants receive a questionnaire around May for the application of the residence visa/residence permit, i.e. Zuyd handles the IND sponsorship procedure for the MVV + VVR student residence permit.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, conditionally - and this is the single most important finding for this candidate. The official prior-education requirement is 'A Bachelor's degree in Music, OR proof of an equivalent level of knowledge and skills tailored to the programme.' A BSc in Software Engineering plus a strong producer portfolio can satisfy the second clause, and the department runs a Preparatory Course Master as a formal fallback for applicants who audition below master level. The catch is the audition: he must play an instrument, sit an ear test, and demonstrate jazz-related musicianship (piano/guitar a plus). Pure DJ skills will not carry the audition.
programs.recommendation: HIGHEST-PRIORITY TARGET OF THIS WHOLE SWEEP for him. It is the only public, English-taught, electronic-music-production master found in Belgium or the Netherlands whose written entry rule explicitly admits equivalent knowledge instead of a music bachelor, and whose portfolio brief is exactly 'three of your own DAW productions'. Action plan for a September-2027 start: (a) take IELTS Academic by spring 2027 targeting 6.0+ (he needs only B2 - his working English should reach this with modest prep); (b) spend 2026-27 producing at least three finished, fully mixed original tracks and be able to narrate the production chain in English on camera; (c) start piano/keyboard and ear training NOW - this is his weakest point and the audition tests it; (d) contact head of programme Irja Zeper (irja.zeper@zuyd.nl) in autumn 2026, state the software-engineering background plainly, and ask directly whether his profile is assessed as 'equivalent level' or whether he should apply for the Preparatory Course Master; (e) apply before 1 March 2027 and simultaneously apply for the Zuyd Excellence Scholarship and NL Scholarship. Budget realistically for €12,280/yr minus a partial scholarship - this is NOT cheap self-pay.

programs.program: Master of Music – Composition for Media, Video and Games (Master in de muziek – compositie voor media, video en games)
programs.institution: KASK & Conservatorium, School of Arts of HOGENT and Howest (Hogeschool Gent)
programs.institutionType: Publicly funded Flemish hogeschool (university college); KASK & Conservatorium is the joint School of Arts of HOGENT and Howest
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Known because HOGENT and Howest are Flemish Community-funded hogescholen: their tuition is set by the Flemish decree formula (a fixed 'vast bedrag' plus a per-credit 'variabel bedrag'), which only recognised, publicly funded Flemish institutions charge, and the school publishes the officially decreed non-EEA 'verhoogd studiegeld' alongside it.
programs.qualification: Master of Music / Master in de muziek, 120 ECTS. A real, state-recognised Flemish second-cycle degree registered in the Higher Education Register of the Flemish Community; supports a Belgian type-D student visa and student residence permit for a non-EU national.
programs.accreditationStatus: Accredited Flemish master (NVAO/Flemish Higher Education Register). Programme is described by the institution as 'the first in Flanders to focus on composing music for various audiovisual productions'. Specific NVAO decision reference UNVERIFIED - check the Flemish Hogeronderwijsregister (hogeronderwijsregister.be) or ask toelatingsproeven@hogent.be.
programs.language: DUTCH. The official enrolment page states explicitly: 'This is a Dutch spoken programme.' Campus Grote Sikkel, Biezekapelstraat 9, Ghent.
programs.languageRequirement: For this Dutch-taught master a Dutch-language proof is required. KASK's general admission page says master's programmes 'can be studied in Dutch or English' and that for English 'Vantage B2 level is strongly recommended', but it gives no formal test list; HOGENT's international pages require Dutch for Dutch-taught programmes and note that non-EEA applicants who need a preparatory language year can only get a visa for it once enrolled in a full course at a university language centre. The exact Dutch certificate accepted (ITNA / CNaVT / B2) for THIS master is UNVERIFIED - ask toelatingsproeven@hogent.be.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, 120 ECTS (60 + 60). Year 1: composition for media/video/games, electroacoustic composition, virtual orchestration, film history, seminars. Year 2: master thesis (30 ECTS), audiovisual composition, film analysis, professional practice in the arts field.
programs.focus: Composing music for audiovisual production - film, documentary, animation, games, theatre - plus the electroacoustic and technical craft behind it.
programs.whatYouStudy: Composition for documentary, animation, games and theatre contexts; electroacoustic composition; virtual orchestration; film history and film analysis; 'the technical knowledge needed to thrive in a constantly and rapidly evolving practice'; a 30-ECTS master project. Collaboration with HOWEST (game development) and with Film Fest Gent for masterclasses and networking. Staff contacts named: Ruben De Gheselle and Dominique Pauwels.
programs.entryRequirements: Route depends on prior degree, per the official admission-requirements page: holders of an academic bachelor in the same discipline are admitted directly after passing the orientation interview/audition; holders of a professional bachelor must first complete a transition programme (schakelprogramma); holders of an academic bachelor in a DIFFERENT artistic discipline may be required to take a preparatory programme (voorbereidingsprogramma). The admissions officer and track counsellors evaluate the degree. Registration via webreg.hogent.be, then documents (with apostille/legalisation depending on country of issue - a physical original-stamped copy is required before formal enrolment), then the orientation test.
programs.auditionSpec: Orientation test in two parts. ASSIGNMENT: the candidate provides soundtracks for TWO video clips of 2-3 minutes; the music is the candidate's own choice, of several possible kinds and genres; the clips are emailed three weeks before the deadline. INTERVIEW: an intake with the orientation committee (several teachers and field experts) covering motivation, artistic discipline, communication skills and knowledge of the specific domain. Interviews normally in person on a Ghent campus, but 'if you have to travel far, you can also participate in the interview or audition online' - important for a Tunisian applicant. Result by email within two working weeks.
programs.portfolioSpec: A dossier is assessed alongside the assignment ('Based on your dossier and the assignment, you will be invited for an interview'). Detailed dossier contents are not published - UNVERIFIED; ask toelatingsproeven@hogent.be.
programs.equipmentRequired: Not published; a personal DAW/scoring setup is implied by the assignment. UNVERIFIED - ask the programme via toelatingsproeven@hogent.be.
programs.facilities: Electroacoustic composition and virtual orchestration are taught subjects, and the school runs its music campus at Grote Sikkel in central Ghent, with links to HOWEST game development and Film Fest Gent. Specific studio/immersive-audio specification UNVERIFIED.
programs.intakes: September (single annual intake, Flemish academic year).
programs.applicationOpens: Registration via webreg.hogent.be, with orientation-test sessions announced per season. For the 2026-27 cycle registration for the April session closed 27.03.2026. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for the Sept-2027 intake.
programs.deadline: Published cycle (2026 entry): registration deadline for the April session 27.03.2026, interview 27.04.2026; assignment deadline for the August session 25.06.2026, interviews 24-26.08.2026. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For a September-2027 start expect an equivalent March/April 2027 session and a late-June/August 2027 session; a non-EEA applicant should aim at the SPRING session because of visa lead time. Confirm from autumn 2026 at toelatingsproeven@hogent.be.
programs.tuitionEU: €1,181.40 for a full-time 60-credit year in 2026-2027 (fixed €305.40 + €14.60 per credit).
programs.tuitionNonEU: €8,800.20 PER YEAR - the rate he would pay. HOGENT/KASK publishes for 2026-2027 an increased non-EEA tuition of a fixed €916.20 plus €131.40 per credit, i.e. €8,800.20 for a full 60-credit year. The school notes that 'some non-EEA students belong to a category exempted from paying the increased tuition fee' - the exemption list is a linked document; whether a Tunisian national qualifies is UNVERIFIED, ask the KASK admissions officer / HOGENT student administration.
programs.otherFees: A separate 'contribution towards study costs' (studio/atelier fee) is charged on top, varying by programme and credit load. Amount for this master UNVERIFIED - ask the KASK study administration. Belgian visa, residence-permit and health-insurance costs additional.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition alone: €8,800.20 x 2 = €17,600.40 for 120 ECTS, plus an unpublished studio-cost contribution. Living costs in Ghent and the Belgian proof-of-means figure for a student visa are not published on these pages - UNVERIFIED; get the current annual sufficient-means amount from the Belgian Immigration Office (Dienst Vreemdelingenzaken).
programs.scholarships: The realistic route for a Tunisian national is the Flemish Government Master Mind Scholarship (already in the database as a cross-cutting scheme) - it funds non-EEA students on eligible masters at Flemish institutions and is nominated through the institution, so HOGENT must put the programme and the candidate forward. Whether THIS master is on HOGENT's Master Mind list for the 2027-28 call is UNVERIFIED - ask HOGENT International Office. No programme-specific scholarship is published on the course page.
programs.visaEligible: Yes - a recognised Flemish second-cycle degree at a publicly funded hogeschool supports a Belgian type-D student visa and student residence permit. HOGENT's international pages describe the student-visa application through the Belgian Embassy/Consulate with the acceptance letter as a required document, and set out the diploma legalisation/apostille chain.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO, not realistically for a September-2027 start. A BSc in Software Engineering is neither an academic bachelor in music nor in another artistic discipline, so at best the admissions officer would route him into a preparatory or transition programme first - and the whole master is taught in Dutch, which he does not speak. The orientation-test assignment (scoring two video clips) is something he could plausibly do; the language and prior-degree gates are what stop him.
programs.recommendation: Genuinely new find for the database and a strong programme in its field, but a poor fit for THIS candidate: Dutch-taught, aimed at composers, and requiring a bridging route for a non-artistic bachelor. Worth keeping on file only if he is willing to spend a preparatory year on Dutch (note HOGENT's warning that a visa for a language-preparation year requires enrolment in a full course at a university language centre). If he wants Ghent, the English-language route at the same school is the InMICS master - see the separate record - though that one demands a music undergraduate degree.

programs.program: Composition for Screen – InMICS (International Master in Composition for Screen)
programs.institution: KASK & Conservatorium, School of Arts of HOGENT and Howest (Hogeschool Gent) - with CNSMD de Lyon, Conservatorio di Musica G.B. Martini Bologna and Université de Montréal

Martini Bologna (Italian AFAM state conservatoire) and Université de Montréal (Quebec public university). programs.qualification: International master, 2 years, 120 ECTS. On the Belgian side it sits inside HOGENT's accredited Flemish master in music. programs.accreditationStatus: The Belgian component is delivered within HOGENT's accredited master in music (Flemish Higher Education Register). The consortium-level accreditation status and the exact awarding institution(s) are UNVERIFIED - confirm with info@inmics.org and with HOGENT.

programs.whatYouStudy: Composition for audiovisual media across four partner conservatoires/universities, with placements and exposure through the four professional partners: Festival International du Film d'Aubagne, Fondazione Cineteca di Bologna, Film Fest Gent and Permission Inc. programs.facilities: Access to four public conservatoire/university facilities (Ghent, Lyon, Bologna, Montréal) plus festival and cinémathèque partners. Specific studio specification UNVERIFIED.

programs.tuitionNonEU: UNVERIFIED for this specific master, and this matters. If he is enrolled at HOGENT he would fall under the published Flemish non-EEA rate of €916.20 fixed + €131.40 per credit = €8,800.20 for a 60-credit year; but a consortium programme administered through CNSMD de Lyon may charge a different, consortium-wide fee, and Lyon/Bologna/Montréal each have their own non-EU rates. programs.visaEligible: For the Belgian portion, yes - a recognised Flemish master supports a type-D student visa. UNVERIFIED how the consortium handles this - ask info@inmics.org directly and in writing.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO. The stated requirement is an undergraduate degree in music (or equivalent) PLUS active composition experience for screen media. If he does contact them, the three questions worth asking are: what degree is actually awarded and by whom; what the non-EU fee is across all four mobility periods; and how the consortium handles visas for a Tunisian national travelling to Canada mid-programme.

programs.program: Interface Cultures — Master Programme (MA)
programs.institution: Universität für künstlerische und industrielle Gestaltung Linz (Kunstuniversität Linz / University of Arts Linz)
programs.institutionType: Public federal art university (Kunstuniversität) under the Austrian Universitätsgesetz 2002
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. How I know: the university's own tuition-fee page states the fee amount is set by 'the 2002 Universities Act' (Universitätsgesetz 2002), the federal statute that governs Austria's 22 state universities, and it levies the statutory federal rates (EUR 363.36 / 726.72) rather than a market price. It is federally funded via the BMBWF. Not a Privatuniversität.
programs.accreditationStatus: Real, state-recognised second-cycle degree. Kunstuniversität Linz is a federal public university established by law; its Masterstudien are ordentliche Studien under UG 2002 and award a Master of Arts. Admission as an ordentliche/r Studierende/r in a degree programme is the basis for an Aufenthaltsbewilligung – Studierende under §64 NAG, so it supports a student residence permit for a Tunisian national.
programs.qualification: Master of Arts (MA) — a genuine second-cycle degree, not a certificate or 'Lehrgang'. Kunstuni Linz's own Study & Admission page confirms 'Master's Programme — Duration: 4 semesters'.
programs.focus: Media art / digital art, interactive art, interface design, participatory practice at the art–technology–research intersection. Sound is present as a medium inside interactive/installation work, but this is NOT a music-production or audio-engineering degree.
programs.whatYouStudy: Artistic and scientific development of interactive media; human–machine, human–human and machine–machine interaction; critical data, sustainable IT and the environmental politics of digitalisation; conceptual and practical prototype development. Strong link to Ars Electronica (Linz), which is the single biggest reason this department matters for a portfolio-builder.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters. Kunstuni Linz's Study & Admission page states master's duration = 4 semesters; the standard Austrian equivalent is 120 ECTS, but the exact ECTS figure is not published on the Interface Cultures pages — UNVERIFIED, ask interfacecultures@kunstuni-linz.at.
programs.language: ENGLISH. The official programme text states: 'The master program is fully held in English language.' This is one of the few fully English-taught art-university masters in Austria.
programs.languageRequirement: No specific IELTS/TOEFL band is published on the Interface Cultures pages — UNVERIFIED. The comparable Kunstuni Linz master (Timebased Media) publishes 'English: Level B2 proficiency required before program start if completing coursework in English' and 'German: Level B1 by third-semester enrolment'. Ask the Student Service Center (international.office@kunstuni-linz.at) whether an IELTS/TOEFL certificate is demanded for Interface Cultures or whether a self-declared B2 / interview in English suffices. This matters for him because he has not sat IELTS.
programs.entryRequirements: 'To study at Interface Cultures you need a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree to qualify for admission.' Application materials: copy of degree, motivation letter, CV, and a portfolio of works. Plus the departmental entrance exam — Kunstuni Linz's Study & Admission page: 'To be admitted to a Master's programme, applicants need a compatible Bachelor's certificate and have to pass the entrance exam of the department.' Note: no music degree is required and no conservatory training is required. A BSc in Software Engineering is a plausible, even attractive, base here — the department explicitly wants people who can build things.
programs.portfolioSpec: Portfolio of own works + letter of motivation + CV, submitted online. The sister programme's procedure (same admissions machinery) is: online registration → portfolio + motivation letter upload → ~30-minute admission interview including 'a ten-minute presentation of selected work samples' → result by email/PIN. Exact Interface Cultures portfolio format/file limits are not published — UNVERIFIED, ask interfacecultures@kunstuni-linz.at.
programs.auditionSpec: No musical audition. An admission interview with work presentation, not a performance audition. This is a significant advantage for a candidate with no conservatory background.
programs.equipmentRequired: None stated. Department provides shared kit.
programs.facilities: Two dedicated computer rooms, a production workshop, a rapid-prototyping lab (3D printers, soldering stations, laser cutters), and shared equipment including MIDI controllers, cameras, speakers, projectors and VR headsets. Note the MIDI controllers and speakers — usable for sound work, but there is no published professional studio/control-room or spatial-audio rig here.
programs.intakes: Winter semester (September/October) start only, as far as published.
programs.applicationOpens: Around mid-March. For the 2026/27 cycle the parallel Kunstuni Linz master opened online registration on 18 March 2026. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Interface-Cultures-specific opening date UNVERIFIED — ask interfacecultures@kunstuni-linz.at.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED for Interface Cultures specifically. The comparable Kunstuni Linz master (Timebased Media) ran: online registration 18 March – 7 June 2026, portfolio due 7 June 2026, interviews 30 June – 1 July 2026 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. CRITICAL PLANNING POINT: this is a SPRING deadline (March–June), not the October–February window he is planning around. For a September 2027 start he must be ready to submit a portfolio by roughly June 2027, and register from about March 2027.
programs.tuitionEU: EUR 363.36 per semester (EU/EEA nationals are exempt during the standard duration plus a two-semester grace period; Austrians exempt).
programs.tuitionNonEU: EUR 726.72 PER SEMESTER — this is the rate he would pay as a Tunisian national. Quoted directly on the Interface Cultures page ('non-EU-citizens currently have to pay a fee of 726,72 € per semester') and on the university's tuition-fee page. That is EUR 1,453.44 per academic year, EUR 2,906.88 for the whole 4-semester degree. By European standards this is very cheap. Note: Kunstuni Linz states a reduction to the EU rate can be requested in some 'close relationship to Austria' cases — not applicable to a first-time arrival.
programs.otherFees: Austrian National Union of Students (ÖH) fee including insurance: EUR 24.70 per semester as quoted on the Kunstuni Linz page. The ÖH fee is indexed and rises most years (other Austrian institutions already quote EUR 25.20 / 26.20) — treat 24.70 as a floor and confirm at enrolment. Payment must be made in full within the admission period or admission is refused; partial payment is not accepted.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Tuition + ÖH over 2 years: approx. EUR 2,996. Living costs in Linz are the real expense and are NOT published by the university — budget separately. For the Austrian student visa he must additionally prove sufficient means to the immigration authority (a fixed monthly figure set annually by the ASVG — UNVERIFIED here, confirm with the Austrian embassy/OeAD).
programs.scholarships: None attached to this programme. Kunstuni Linz publishes no programme scholarship for non-EU master applicants. Realistic external routes for a Tunisian: OeAD-administered Austrian government scholarships (Ernst Mach Grant is aimed mainly at short research stays, not full masters) and the Ernst Mach Grant – worldwide. Nothing verified as covering a full Kunstuni Linz master — treat as UNVERIFIED and ask OeAD (grants.at) directly.
programs.visaEligible: Yes. Admission to an ordentliches Masterstudium at an Austrian public university is the standard basis for the Aufenthaltsbewilligung – Studierende (§64 NAG). He must apply at the Austrian representation in Tunis before travelling.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly. Requirement is 'a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree', not a music or art degree. A Software Engineering BSc plus a strong interactive/sound portfolio is a coherent application here.
programs.recommendation: ONE OF THE TWO BEST FITS FOUND IN THIS ENTIRE SLICE, but with an honest caveat. In its favour: fully English-taught (removes the German wall that kills almost every other Austrian and Swiss option for him); EUR 726.72/semester is among the cheapest real master's degrees in Western Europe; no music degree, no conservatory training and no audition required; the entry gate is a portfolio he can genuinely build in a year as a software engineer (interactive sound objects, generative audio, installations, Max/MSP or SuperCollider work, web-audio pieces); the Ars Electronica connection is a real career asset. Against it: this is media art, not music production — it will not train him as a DJ or a record producer, and there is no published pro studio. He should treat it as a route into sound art and creative technology, not into the club/label industry. ACTION: (1) email interfacecultures@kunstuni-linz.at NOW to get the 2027 registration window, the exact portfolio spec and whether an English certificate is required, because the deadline is in SPRING, several months earlier than the Oct–Feb window he has assumed; (2) build 4–6 interactive sound works over the coming year, documented on video.

programs.program: Zeitbasierte Medien / Timebased Media — Master Programme (MA)
programs.institution: Universität für künstlerische und industrielle Gestaltung Linz (Kunstuniversität Linz / University of Arts Linz)
programs.institutionType: Public federal art university (Kunstuniversität) under the Austrian Universitätsgesetz 2002
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Same evidence as above: federal university governed by the Universitätsgesetz 2002, levying the statutory federal tuition rates set by that Act, funded by the BMBWF. Not a private provider.
programs.accreditationStatus: Real, state-recognised second-cycle degree (ordentliches Masterstudium under UG 2002), awarding a Master of Arts. Supports the §64 NAG student residence permit for a non-EU national.
programs.qualification: Master of Arts (MA), 4 semesters. A genuine second-cycle degree.
programs.focus: Time-based media: video (practice and theory), film theory, SOUND, media installation and staging, interactive systems, design with digital media, innovative programming. Sound is named as an explicit component of the programme — this is why it belongs on the list and why it was worth digging past the famous names.

programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters. ECTS not stated on the programme pages — the Austrian standard for a 4-semester master is 120 ECTS but the exact figure is UNVERIFIED here; ask gerlinde.schmierer@kunstuni-linz.at or the Student Service Center.
programs.language: GERMAN AND ENGLISH. The official registration/admission page states the degree programme accommodates both German and English, with admission interviews available in English for international applicants. So teaching is bilingual in practice, not English-only.
programs.languageRequirement: Two separate, both published officially: German level B1 required by enrolment in the THIRD semester (i.e. not needed at entry, but needed a year in); English level B2 required BEFORE programme start if he will complete coursework in English. programs.auditionSpec: No musical audition. A 30-minute selection interview with a 10-minute presentation of work samples.
programs.equipmentRequired: None stated.
programs.facilities: Not published on the programme pages — UNVERIFIED. Ask gerlinde.schmierer@kunstuni-linz.at for a facilities list before applying — this is exactly the sort of thing an audio-focused applicant must check.
programs.applicationOpens: 18 March 2026 for the 2026/27 cycle. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Expect roughly mid-March 2027 for a September 2027 start.
programs.deadline: Online registration 18 March – 7 June 2026; portfolio submission deadline 7 June 2026; admission interviews 30 June – 1 July 2026. ALL PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates. programs.tuitionEU: EUR 363.36 per semester; EU/EEA nationals exempt for the standard duration plus two semesters.
programs.tuitionNonEU: EUR 726.72 PER SEMESTER — the rate he would pay as a Tunisian national, set by the Universitätsgesetz 2002 and quoted on the university's own tuition-fee page. EUR 1,453.44/year; EUR 2,906.88 for the full degree.
programs.otherFees: ÖH student union fee incl. insurance EUR 24.70 per semester (university's own figure). Indexed annually — confirm. Non-payment in full within the admission period means no admission or de-matriculation.

programs.visaEligible: Yes — ordentliches Masterstudium at an Austrian public university, the standard §64 NAG basis.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: PARTIALLY. No music degree is needed, but the stated prior fields are media/film/video/sound rather than 'any bachelor'. A CS/software background must be argued through the portfolio and the 'comparable degree' clause. Get this confirmed in writing before applying.
programs.recommendation: WORTH APPLYING TO ALONGSIDE INTERFACE CULTURES, as the second shot at the same institution in the same cycle. Advantages: sound is an explicitly named subject; German is NOT required at entry (only B1 by semester three), which is unusually forgiving; the fee is the same EUR 726.72/semester; no audition. ACTION: write to the department now with his CV and ask two blunt questions — (a) does a BSc Software Engineering count as 'comparable' for admission, and (b) what audio facilities does the department actually have. programs.program: Digital Arts (Master) — Master of Arts in Arts and Design, programme code 0628
programs.institution: FH Oberösterreich / University of Applied Sciences Upper Austria, Campus Hagenberg (FH OÖ Studienbetriebs GmbH)
programs.institutionType: Fachhochschule (university of applied sciences), Austrian FH sector
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC-SECTOR, with a caveat worth stating precisely. Austria's FH system is genuinely ambiguous by design: FH programmes are run by a legally separate provider company (here FH OÖ Studienbetriebs GmbH) but are publicly co-financed by the federal government per study place and are state-accredited under the Fachhochschulgesetz by AQ Austria. How I know it is on the public side: it charges exactly the statutory federal tuition rates (EUR 363.36 / 726.72) and collects the ÖH fee — a purely private provider sets its own price. The company's shareholding (the Province of Upper Austria) is not stated on the pages I opened — that ownership detail is UNVERIFIED; confirm at studienbeitrag@fh-ooe.at or in the company register if it matters to him.
programs.accreditationStatus: Real, state-recognised second-cycle degree. Austrian FH master's degrees are accredited under the Fachhochschulgesetz and quality-assured by AQ Austria; the award here is 'Master of Arts in Arts and Design', a standard Austrian FH master title. Admission supports the §64 NAG student residence permit for a non-EU national.
programs.qualification: Master of Arts in Arts and Design (MA). 4 semesters, full time. A genuine second-cycle degree — not a 'Lehrgang' or a certificate.
programs.focus: Digital arts: 2D/3D animation, motion design, visualisation, games and mixed reality. Official strapline: 'Design-Oriented Know-How and Practical Skills in Computer Animation, Audio/Video & Games'. Audio appears as part of the Audio/Video & Games strand, but the master's own emphasis list is animation/motion/games — audio is a supporting discipline here, not the core.
programs.whatYouStudy: Deepening and specialisation in 2D/3D animation, motion design, visualisation, games and mixed reality, with an Audio/Video & Games strand. Semester abroad possible in semesters 3 and 4.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters, full time. Total ECTS for the master is not stated on the programme page — UNVERIFIED (the Austrian norm is 120); ask da@fh-hagenberg.at.
programs.language: GERMAN. Stated flatly in the official fact box: 'Language: German'. This is decisive for him — he has no German at all.
programs.languageRequirement: 'Good proficiency in German' is written into the access requirements. No CEFR level or named certificate is published — UNVERIFIED; ask da@fh-hagenberg.at what level and what certificate they accept. In practice German FH programmes expect B2. He would need roughly two years of German study to reach that, which does not fit a September 2027 start.
programs.entryRequirements: THE HARD GATE: 'Completion of at least a 6 semester specialised relevant Bachelor's degree (e.g. in the field of media technology, media design, video/film and timebased & interactive media) with audio/video, multimedia and computer animation strand worth a minimum of 60 ECTS towards accreditation, or comparable higher education at university level. Good proficiency in German.' A BSc in Software Engineering will not normally contain 60 ECTS of audio/video/multimedia/animation coursework. Unless his transcript genuinely shows that, he is not eligible — this is not a portfolio-fixable gap, it is a credit-count gap.
programs.portfolioSpec: Selection process is 'Interview, Portfolio (could include graphic design, drawings, short-films, animations, games, etc.)'. Note that audio work is not listed among the example portfolio items.
programs.auditionSpec: None — no musical audition. Interview plus portfolio review.
programs.equipmentRequired: None stated.
programs.facilities: Not published on the programme page — UNVERIFIED. Hagenberg is a media-technology campus with animation and games labs; no audio studio inventory is published. Ask da@fh-hagenberg.at.
programs.intakes: Annual intake of 20 places, winter-semester (autumn) start.
programs.applicationOpens: Not published as a fixed opening date — UNVERIFIED; ask da@fh-hagenberg.at.
programs.deadline: For the 2026/27 cycle: 31 May 2026 for applicants who require a visa; 30 June 2026 general deadline for EU/EEA citizens and visa-free entrants; 31 August 2026 extended deadline if places remain. ALL PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates. IMPORTANT FOR HIM: as a Tunisian national he falls under the EARLIER 31 May visa-required deadline, a month before everyone else. Expect roughly 31 May 2027 for a September 2027 start — again a spring, not an autumn/winter, deadline.
programs.tuitionEU: EUR 363.36 per semester for EU/EEA students (Austrian statutory FH rate).
programs.tuitionNonEU: EUR 726.72 PER SEMESTER — the rate he would pay as a Tunisian national holding a §64 NAG student residence permit. FH OÖ additionally publishes that the fee can be reduced from EUR 726.72 to EUR 363.36 on written request to studienbeitrag@fh-ooe.at where a 'close relationship to Austria' is proven — that will not apply to a first-time arrival from Tunis, but it is worth knowing the reduction mechanism exists.
programs.otherFees: ÖH student union contribution per semester. FH OÖ's own material quotes EUR 24.70 in one place and the ÖH's own published rate is EUR 26.20 — the figure is indexed annually and the two sources disagree, so treat the exact number as UNVERIFIED and confirm at studienbeitrag@fh-ooe.at. Either way it is a rounding error against living costs.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Approx. EUR 2,907 tuition + roughly EUR 100–105 ÖH over 2 years. Living costs in Upper Austria not published — budget separately, plus the means-of-subsistence proof for the Austrian student visa.
programs.scholarships: None published for this programme. Note the database already contains a generic Austrian FH funding scheme attachable to FH studies — check whether that instrument covers non-EU students, because most Austrian study-grant instruments are restricted to Austrians and equated persons. UNVERIFIED for a Tunisian national; ask the FH OÖ international office.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — an Austrian FH master's degree programme supports the §64 NAG student residence permit. FH OÖ's earlier 31 May deadline for visa-required applicants exists precisely to allow visa processing time.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO music degree is required — but a media/audio-video bachelor with 60 ECTS in the relevant strands effectively IS required. That is the binding constraint, not music.
programs.recommendation: REPORT AS A NEAR-MISS, NOT A TARGET. It fills a real gap in the database (FH OÖ Hagenberg was not covered) and it is genuinely cheap and genuinely accredited, but for this candidate two independent things block it: teaching is entirely in German with 'good proficiency in German' written into the admission rule, and admission demands 60 ECTS of audio/video/multimedia/animation credit in the bachelor, which a Software Engineering BSc will not have. Audio is also a minor strand here rather than the subject. He should not spend time on it unless (a) his transcript unexpectedly shows 60 ECTS of media coursework AND (b) he commits to German to B2, in which case the 2028 intake, not 2027, is the realistic target. If he does pursue it, the one date to remember is the 31 May visa-applicant deadline.

programs.program: Master of Arts in Music, Major Komposition — combined with Minor Electronic Music Composition, Minor Media Composer or Minor Groove und Electronics
programs.institution: Hochschule Luzern – Musik (Lucerne School of Music, Lucerne University of Applied Sciences and Arts)
programs.institutionType: University of applied sciences and arts (Fachhochschule), music department
programs.publicPrivate: PUBLIC. Hochschule Luzern is the university of applied sciences and arts of central Switzerland, carried by the six central Swiss cantons under the inter-cantonal FH Zentralschweiz concordat — its own site footers as 'FH Zentralschweiz'. It is institutionally accredited under the Swiss federal HFKG (the site states 'Institutionell akkreditiert nach HFKG 2019–2026'). It is not a private conservatory or a foundation school.
programs.accreditationStatus: Real, state-recognised second-cycle degree. Institutionally accredited under the Swiss Hochschulförderungs- und -koordinationsgesetz (HFKG) 2019–2026, as published on its own pages. A Swiss MA from an accredited hochschule supports a Swiss student residence permit (B permit for studies) for a non-EU national, subject to cantonal quota and proof of funds.
programs.qualification: Master of Arts in Music (MA), with a declared Major and optional Minors. A genuine second-cycle Swiss degree. HSLU – Musik offers exactly two masters: MA in Music and MA in Musikpädagogik.
programs.focus: THIS IS THE FIND: the MA in Music carries an official Minor Electronic Music Composition, a Minor Groove und Electronics, and a Minor Media Composer, alongside Minor Komposition, Minor Jazz, Minor Improvisation, Minor Digitale Kompetenzen für Musik, Bildung und Kultur and others. Central Switzerland's electronic-music teaching sits inside this minor structure and is easy to miss because the minors are not marketed as standalone programmes.
programs.whatYouStudy: Major Komposition is deliberately open: the curriculum is explicitly 'not profile-specific' and is set by individual target agreements, with Classical and Jazz orientations that 'can be individually modified and mixed'. On top of the major, the student stacks minors — Electronic Music Composition, Groove und Electronics, and Media Composer being the three that map onto electronic music production and scoring.
programs.durationEcts: Master's programmes build on the bachelor; the standard Swiss MA in Music is 4 semesters / 120 ECTS but the exact ECTS is not stated on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED, ask musik@hslu.ch. IMPORTANT ADDITIONAL RULE, published officially: applicants WITHOUT a bachelor's degree from a Swiss music university may be required to sit a 'Standortbestimmung Theorie' (theory placement assessment), and depending on the outcome must pass an Auflagenmodul (bridging module) in the first master semester covering the target competences of the HSLU bachelor. Continuation beyond the first semester depends on passing it. For a candidate with no music degree at all, this bridging module is not a formality — it is a second exam.
programs.language: GERMAN. Teaching is in German; the studienführer, curricula and fee regulations are published in German only, and the language rule below confirms German is the working language.
programs.languageRequirement: Published officially and specific: B1 German for most master's programmes (including MA Music); B2 for Major Instrumental/Vocal Pedagogy and Church Music; C1 for Major Musiktheorie and School Music II. Crucially, HSLU states 'Knowledge of German is not required for the entrance examination, but knowledge of the German language must be proven in a language test' before studies begin. So he could sit the audition without German, but must certify B1 German before starting. No English certificate is required for the MA (C1 English is required only for the doctorate).
programs.entryRequirements: A bachelor's degree plus a successful entrance examination ('Access to the Master of Arts in Music with majors including Composition is possible with an entrance examination'). Plus, for non-Swiss-music-bachelor holders, the theory placement assessment and possible bridging module described above. There is no published route that waives the entrance examination.
programs.portfolioSpec: For a composition major, a portfolio of scores/works is the normal basis of the entrance examination. HSLU does not publish the composition portfolio specification on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED; request the Aufnahmeprüfung requirements for Major Komposition from musik@hslu.ch.
programs.auditionSpec: Entrance examination required — this is a music-university audition/assessment, not an interview. HSLU charges 'CHF 200 per entrance examination (will be credited upon enrolment)', and the admission fee schedule refers to CHF 390 for two practical examinations, which implies the practical exam is a real, separately-priced component.
programs.equipmentRequired: None published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Not published on the pages I opened — UNVERIFIED. Given the Minor Electronic Music Composition and Minor Groove und Electronics exist, electronic-music studios must exist; ask musik@hslu.ch for a studio and equipment list before applying.
programs.intakes: Autumn (September) start, one intake per year — consistent with a single 28 February application deadline.
programs.applicationOpens: Not published as a fixed opening date — UNVERIFIED; online registration runs up to the 28 February deadline. Ask musik@hslu.ch.
programs.deadline: 28 FEBRUARY ANNUALLY (29 February in leap years) for all degree programmes — stated as a standing annual rule, not a one-off cycle date, so this one does not need the prior-cycle caveat. Entrance examination fees are due at online registration. THIS IS THE ONE PROGRAMME IN THIS SWEEP WHOSE DEADLINE ACTUALLY FALLS INSIDE HIS OCTOBER 2026 – FEBRUARY 2027 WINDOW: for a September 2027 start he applies by 28 February 2027.
programs.tuitionEU: CHF 800 per semester for domestic students. Note that Switzerland's split is Swiss/resident versus foreign-domiciled, NOT EU versus non-EU — an EU national who moves to Switzerland to study pays the same surcharge he would.
programs.tuitionNonEU: CHF 1,300 PER SEMESTER — the rate he would pay. HSLU's exact official wording: 'CHF 1'300.– for international students (for students with foreign citizenship who enter or have entered Switzerland for the purpose of studying.)' That is CHF 2,600 per year, CHF 5,200 tuition over a 4-semester master. The surcharge exists because students entering Switzerland to study do not attract cantonal FHV subsidies.
programs.otherFees: All published officially and all mandatory, and they add up: per semester — module examination CHF 150, photocopying CHF 45, service fee CHF 45, university sport CHF 25 (= CHF 265 per semester on top of tuition). One-off — enrolment fee CHF 390, HSLU card CHF 50, admission fee CHF 200 plus CHF 390 for two practical examinations, degree and certification CHF 220. Other — break from studies CHF 200 per semester, student exchange application CHF 200.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Fees only, over 4 semesters: tuition 4 × CHF 1,300 = CHF 5,200; compulsory per-semester extras 4 × CHF 265 = CHF 1,060; one-off admission/enrolment/card/diploma ≈ CHF 1,250 (200 + 390 + 390 + 50 + 220). Total institutional cost roughly CHF 7,500. Living costs in Lucerne are the dominant expense and are NOT published — Switzerland is the most expensive country in this slice, and the Swiss student permit requires proof of sufficient means (figure set cantonally — UNVERIFIED, confirm with the Swiss representation in Tunis and Kanton Luzern migration office).
programs.scholarships: Nothing published at programme level. The database already holds the Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships – Art Scholarships stream, which is the one instrument that genuinely funds a first master's at a Swiss conservatory for a foreign national; Tunisia's eligibility and the art-stream country list change yearly, so confirm on the SERI/FCS official list for the 2027 call. UNVERIFIED for this programme specifically.
programs.visaEligible: Yes in principle — an accredited Swiss hochschule degree programme supports a student residence permit, but Swiss student permits for non-EU nationals are discretionary, require proof of funds and of intent to leave, and are handled cantonally. Budget time for this.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO, not realistically. There is no music-degree requirement written as such, but the entrance examination for a composition major, plus the explicit theory placement assessment and bridging module for anyone without a Swiss music bachelor, together amount to a conservatory-level gate. A candidate with no music degree, no conservatory training and no portfolio cannot clear it in one year.
programs.recommendation: IMPORTANT AS A DATABASE GAP, NOT AS A 2027 APPLICATION. Hochschule Luzern – Musik was absent from the database entirely, and its Minor Electronic Music Composition / Minor Groove und Electronics / Minor Media Composer are the closest thing to electronic-music-production training in central Switzerland — that is worth recording. But for THIS candidate the verdict is negative and should be stated plainly: a composition entrance examination, a theory placement test with a first-semester bridging module he must pass to continue, B1 German certified before he starts, roughly CHF 7,500 in institutional fees plus Swiss living costs, and no funding he is known to be eligible for. The single thing worth doing now, cheaply: the deadline is a standing 28 February, which does fit his planning window, so if in eighteen months his portfolio and German have both moved further than expected, this becomes reachable for a 2028 or 2029 start. File it, do not chase it.

programs.program: Master of Arts in Music Composition & Theory — Major in Composition
programs.institution: Scuola universitaria di Musica, Conservatorio della Svizzera italiana (affiliated to SUPSI — University of Applied Sciences and Arts of Southern Switzerland)
programs.institutionType: University-level music school (scuola universitaria di musica) operated by a foundation and affiliated to a public university of applied sciences
programs.publicPrivate: AMBIGUOUS BY DESIGN — and this is exactly the case where the country's system makes the label unsafe, so here is the structure rather than a guess. The Conservatorio della Svizzera italiana is run by a private-law foundation, NOT by the canton directly. However, since 2006 its University School of Music has been affiliated to SUPSI, the public university of applied sciences of Italian-speaking Switzerland, and its degrees are issued in the Swiss public UAS system. Two pieces of hard evidence that it operates on the public side despite the private carrier: it charges the regulated Swiss two-tier fee (CHF 750 for Swiss nationals and residents versus CHF 1,500 for everyone else) and it explicitly grants the lower rate 'under the Intercantonal Agreement on Universities' — a private school has no access to intercantonal subsidy mechanisms. Practical answer: treat it as a state-recognised public-system music university with a private-foundation carrier. If the distinction matters for a scholarship application, get it in writing from the Conservatorio.
programs.accreditationStatus: Real, state-recognised second-cycle Swiss degree. It is a Swiss KMHS (Konferenz Musikhochschulen Schweiz) member programme delivered in the SUPSI/UAS system, awarding a Master of Arts. It supports a Swiss student residence permit for a non-EU national — the institution runs its own 'Visas and permits' guidance for exactly this.
programs.qualification: Master of Arts in Music Composition & Theory — Major in Composition. 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, full time. A genuine second-cycle degree, not a MAS/CAS. NOTE THE TRAP: the same institution separately offers a 'MAS in Music Composition' under continuing education — a MAS is a post-master continuing-education certificate, NOT a second-cycle degree, and it will not do the same job for a visa or for further study. He must apply for the MA, not the MAS.
programs.focus: Composition and music theory, emphasising 'the creative dimension of composition, integrating reflection and craftsmanship'. Electronic music IS present but through an external arrangement: 'The electronic music section is arranged in partnership with the IRMus of the Accademia Internazionale della Musica in Milan.' That is a meaningful qualification — the electronic strand is delivered via a Milan partner institute rather than in-house, so ask what that means in practice for contact hours, travel and studio access.
programs.whatYouStudy: Composition, with an electronic music section run in partnership with IRMus (Accademia Internazionale della Musica, Milan). Only one major is offered — composition; there are no alternative majors within this MA.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters, 120 ECTS, full time. Officially described as requiring 'total dedication in terms of time and emotional involvement'.
programs.language: ITALIAN. The course descriptor is published in Italian and the institution's language rule targets Italian, not English or German. Web pages are available in English, which is misleading — the teaching language is Italian.
programs.languageRequirement: Published officially and unusually generous in timing: 'A sufficient level of Italian is equivalent to level B2 according to the CEFR, or CELI 3. Those who do not have this language level at the start of their studies must nevertheless demonstrate a sufficient level of Italian and reach level B2 or CELI 3 by the end of their first year of study.' So B2 Italian is not required at entry — it must be reached within the first year. No English certificate is mentioned. For a French-fluent Arabic native, Italian to B2 in a year is more achievable than German to B2, which is worth noting even though the rest of this record is negative.
programs.entryRequirements: Application review followed by entrance examinations by invitation: 'Candidates will receive timely invitations by email to the various examinations, which will take place in April.' A bachelor-level qualification plus the composition entrance examination. Specific academic prerequisites are not itemised on the programme page — UNVERIFIED; request the admission dossier for the MA Composition from the Conservatorio.
programs.portfolioSpec: Not published on the programme page — UNVERIFIED. For a composition major a portfolio of scores and/or recordings will be required; the institution publishes per-programme admission pages (e.g. 'Admission BAM Composition') so ask for the master-level equivalent directly.
programs.auditionSpec: Entrance examinations held in APRIL, by invitation only after application review. This is a music-university admission examination, not an interview.
programs.equipmentRequired: None published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Not published — UNVERIFIED, and materially important here because the electronic music section is run through a Milan partner (IRMus) rather than in-house. Ask specifically: what electronic-music studio facilities exist in Lugano, and how much of the electronic strand is taught in Milan.
programs.intakes: Autumn start, single annual intake (consistent with a 20 February deadline and April examinations).
programs.applicationOpens: Not published — UNVERIFIED. Applications close 20 February, so the window opens some months earlier; ask the Conservatorio.
programs.deadline: 20 FEBRUARY, with entrance examinations in April (2026 cycle: application deadline 20 February 2026). PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date, though the 20 February date is presented as the standing master's deadline. For a September 2027 start, expect 20 February 2027 — INSIDE his October 2026 – February 2027 planning window.
programs.tuitionEU: CHF 750 tuition + CHF 250 administrative fee = CHF 1,000 per semester — but ONLY for Swiss nationals and residents qualifying under the Intercantonal Agreement on Universities. There is no EU rate as such; EU nationals arriving from abroad pay the higher rate below.
programs.tuitionNonEU: CHF 1,500 tuition + CHF 250 administrative fee = CHF 1,750 PER SEMESTER — this is the rate he would pay as a Tunisian national ('all other students'). CHF 3,500 per year; CHF 7,000 over the 4-semester master.
programs.otherFees: Matriculation CHF 250 one-time; student union CHF 5 per semester; final exam CHF 250; reassessment of main subject CHF 200; reassessment of a non-main subject CHF 100; deferred exam CHF 500. The CHF 500 deferred-exam fee is worth noting — Swiss music schools price re-sits aggressively.
programs.totalCostEstimate: Institutional fees over 4 semesters: 4 × CHF 1,750 = CHF 7,000, plus matriculation CHF 250, student union CHF 20, final exam CHF 250 — roughly CHF 7,520 before any re-sits. Living costs in Lugano are not published and are high by any non-Swiss standard. Swiss student permit requires proof of means — figure UNVERIFIED, confirm with the Swiss representation in Tunis and the Ticino migration authority.
programs.scholarships: Nothing published at programme level. The relevant instrument is the Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships Art Scholarships stream (already in the database) — confirm Tunisia's inclusion in the art-stream country list for the 2027 call, because that list is narrower than the research-scholarship list and changes yearly. UNVERIFIED for this institution.
programs.visaEligible: Yes — and the Conservatorio publishes its own 'Visas and permits' guidance with a critical operational warning for him: 'EU/EFTA citizens do not need to get a visa for sitting admission examinations; citizens from all other countries must check the updated list of requisites on the portal of the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM). In many cases, candidates must request a visa to be able to come to Lugano for the admission exam.' A Tunisian applicant may therefore need a visa merely to ATTEND the April entrance examination, months before any study permit. That is a real cost and a real timeline risk that almost no directory site mentions.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO. A composition entrance examination by invitation, at a KMHS music university, is not passable by a candidate with no music degree, no conservatory training and no existing portfolio.
programs.recommendation: RECORD IT, DO NOT APPLY. This closes a genuine hole — the Conservatorio della Svizzera italiana was absent from the database, and it is the only Italian-language music university in this slice with an electronic-music strand. Three findings from it are useful to him even though the programme is not: (1) the visa-to-attend-the-audition problem, which applies to every Swiss music-school audition he might ever consider and must be planned around months in advance; (2) the MA-versus-MAS trap at this institution — the 'MAS in Music Composition' is continuing education, not a degree, and would be the wrong thing to apply for; (3) the Italian B2-by-end-of-first-year rule, which is the most forgiving language regime found anywhere in this sweep and worth remembering if he ever looks at Italian-language options. As an application target for September 2027 it fails on the audition, on the CHF 7,500+ fees with no funding he is known to qualify for, and on the fact that composition is not music production.
